Large, rustic chunks of braised chicken are nestled among tender, irregular potato chunks, thick carrot rounds, and translucent onion wedges. A few dark green pieces of rehydrated wakame seaweed are visible, adding depth. The sauce is a rich, glossy brown, coating the ingredients. The dish is placed on a well-used, light wooden dining table. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests casually on the table beside the bowl, with a small, unadorned white rice bowl nearby, partially filled with steamed white rice. The setting is a cozy, lived-in family kitchen, illuminated by warm, natural overhead lighting, creating a comforting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice.
Eat using chopsticks.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into large, rustic 4cm chunks. Pat dry.
Peel potatoes and cut into irregular 3cm chunks. Soak in cold water for 10 minutes. Drain well.
Peel carrots and cut into thick 2cm rounds or half-moons.
Peel onion and cut into large 8-part wedges.
Rehydrate dried wakame seaweed in cold water for 5 minutes. Squeeze out excess water. Roughly chop if pieces are too large.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until lightly browned on all sides, about 5 minutes. Do not cook through. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add potatoes, carrots, and onion to the same pot. Sauté for 5 minutes until lightly softened.
Return chicken to the pot. Add soy sauce, mirin, sugar, and water or dashi stock.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Skim any foam from the surface.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C/167°F) and vegetables are tender. Stir occasionally.
Add rehydrated wakame seaweed to the pot during the last 5 minutes of simmering.
Stir in toasted sesame oil just before serving.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped scallions.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust sweetness and saltiness to taste by adding more sugar or soy sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Sourdough Crostini with Fermented Chicken & Pickled Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A clean, minimalist presentation on a light-colored, handcrafted ceramic platter or a light reclaimed wood board. Each sourdough crostini, a rustic golden-brown base, is topped with a generous, organic mound of creamy, off-white shredded chicken. The chicken is mixed with a tangy fermented brine. Artfully crowned upon the chicken is a vibrant, glistening tangle of slender, translucent pickled pasta, punctuated by bright orange julienned carrots and thin pink radish slices. Negative space is abundant, allowing each component to stand out. A few scattered, finely chopped green radish greens or delicate edible flowers add a subtle, natural color accent without overcrowding. The texture contrast is key: crisp bread, tender chicken, and slightly firm, tangy pasta. Lighting is soft, natural, enhancing the natural colors of the ingredients. The overall composition is simple, elegant, and ingredient-focused, reflecting sustainable, eco-conscious dining.

ingredients.name: small pasta shapes (e.g., ditalini, or broken spaghetti pieces)

instructions: Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain and rinse with cold water. Set aside.
In a small saucepan, combine 150ml water, white wine vinegar, 15g sugar, and 5g salt. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from heat.
Add julienned carrot and sliced radish to the warm brine. Add cooked pasta to the brine. Let cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 5ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side, until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from pan and let rest for 5 minutes. Shred chicken finely using two forks.
In a bowl, combine shredded chicken, yogurt or crème fraîche, lacto-fermented vegetable brine, and chopped chives. Mix well. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Brush both sides of sourdough slices lightly with 15ml olive oil.
Bake for 8-10 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Let cool slightly.
Arrange crostini on a serving platter. Spoon a generous amount of fermented chicken mixture onto each crostini.
Top with a small portion of pickled pasta, allowing some brine to add moisture.
Garnish with finely chopped radish greens or edible flowers, if using. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Soy-Braised Chicken with Seaweed
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of soy-braised chicken and vegetables is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. Tender, dark brown chicken chunks, approximately 4-5 cm, are nestled among golden-brown potato chunks (3-4 cm) and bright orange carrot chunks (2 cm). Onion wedges are also visible, softened and translucent. The components are coated in a glossy, rich dark brown soy-based sauce, creating an appetizing sheen. The dish is generously garnished with vibrant green chopped spring onions and scattered pieces of crumbled dark green nori. The bowl rests on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table, suggesting a homely kitchen setting. A simple metal spoon and chopsticks are placed beside the bowl. A small, white side dish containing bright red kimchi is visible in the background, along with a casually placed cloth napkin. Natural, soft light illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting textures and warm colors of the meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice.
Serve with various Korean banchan (side dishes), such as kimchi or pickled radishes.
Enjoy family-style, with individual portions served from a central pot or platter.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 4-5 cm chunks. Set aside.
Peel and chop onion into large wedges. Peel and chop potatoes into 3-4 cm chunks. Peel and chop carrots into 2 cm chunks. Mince garlic. Grate ginger.
Heat neutral cooking oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks to the pot. Sear until lightly browned on all sides. Remove chicken from the pot and set aside.
Add onion, minced garlic, and grated ginger to the pot. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
Return chicken to the pot. Add potatoes, carrots, dried kelp, soy sauce, mirin, sugar, and water or chicken stock.
Bring the mixture to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot and simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C) and vegetables are tender.
Remove dried kelp from the pot and discard.
Stir in toasted sesame oil.
Chop green onions. Crumble dried nori into small pieces.
Serve hot. Garnish individual portions with chopped green onions and crumbled nori.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust the amount of sugar and soy sauce to suit your taste preference.
Other vegetables like mushrooms or bell peppers can be added during simmering for more variety.

recipes.recipe_name: Carrot & Spinach Popcorn Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Carrot & Spinach Popcorn Salad is presented in a simple, deep ceramic bowl, reflecting a home kitchen setting. Vibrant shredded orange carrots form the base, mixed with roughly chopped dark green spinach and thinly sliced red onion. A creamy mayonnaise-based dressing coats all ingredients, creating a cohesive, comforting appearance. Small, tender pieces of shredded chicken are sparsely distributed, adding subtle texture without dominating the vegetables. The salad is generously topped with fluffy white popcorn, providing a playful, crunchy contrast. The arrangement is natural and unpretentious, ingredients casually mixed. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table. Warm kitchen light illuminates the dish. A simple cloth napkin and basic fork complete the homely scene.

ingredients.name: Red onion
ingredients.quantity: 1 small, very thinly sliced or finely diced

instructions: Prepare the vegetables: Shred the carrots. Roughly chop the spinach. Thinly slice or finely dice the red onion.
Prepare the chicken: Ensure chicken breast is cooked through and cooled. Shred it into small pieces.
Make the dressing: In a medium bowl, whisk together the mayonnaise, apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper until smooth.
Combine ingredients: In a large mixing bowl, gently combine the shredded carrots, chopped spinach, thinly sliced red onion, and shredded chicken.
Dress the salad: Pour the prepared dressing over the vegetable and chicken mixture. Toss gently until all ingredients are evenly coated.
Add popcorn: Just before serving, fold in the plain popped popcorn. Serve immediately to maintain popcorn crispness.
notes: For best texture, add popcorn just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spinach and Carrot Popcorn Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, homely individual portion of Spinach and Carrot Popcorn Salad is presented on a simple, round off-white ceramic plate. The fresh, dark green spinach leaves form the base, interspersed with bright orange shredded carrots and small, translucent pieces of finely diced yellow onion. A creamy, pale yellow mayonnaise-based dressing lightly coats all ingredients, integrating them naturally. Plain white popped popcorn is casually sprinkled over the top, adding a visible textural contrast. The salad components are arranged organically, allowing for natural overlapping and showcasing the diverse colors and textures. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen lighting. A simple silver fork rests beside the plate. A casually folded beige cloth napkin completes the unpretentious, lived-in family kitchen setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a side dish with roasted chicken or grilled burgers.
Pairs well with classic American BBQ dishes.
instructions: Wash spinach thoroughly. Dry well. Set aside.
Shred carrots. Finely dice onion.
In a large bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, salt, black pepper, and sugar until smooth.
Add spinach, shredded carrots, and diced onion to the dressing. Toss gently to coat all vegetables evenly.
Just before serving, gently fold in the plain popped popcorn.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Bell Pepper and Popcorn Salad
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of Bell Pepper and Popcorn Salad rests on an everyday, slightly imperfect ceramic plate, positioned on a well-used wooden dining table. The salad is a vibrant mix of textures and colors: fluffy white popcorn pieces are interspersed with glossy black beans, bright yellow and red diced bell peppers, golden corn kernels, and finely diced red onion. Fresh green chopped cilantro is visible throughout, adding specks of verdant color. The simple lime-chili dressing lightly coats the ingredients, giving them a subtle sheen. The arrangement is casual and natural, with components touching and overlapping, appearing as if just served from a family meal. A simple, folded cloth napkin and basic flatware are casually placed beside the plate. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, enhancing the homely, comforting atmosphere. The entire plate is visible, with adequate negative space.

ingredients.name: Black beans, canned, rinsed and drained
Corn kernels, canned or frozen, thawed

instructions: Pop the popcorn. Set aside to cool.
In a large bowl, combine rinsed black beans, corn kernels, diced red bell pepper, diced yellow bell pepper, and finely diced red onion.
Add chopped fresh cilantro to the bowl.
In a small bowl, whisk together lime juice, olive oil, ground cumin, chili powder, salt, and black pepper.
Pour the dressing over the vegetable mixture. Toss gently to combine all ingredients thoroughly.
Just before serving, add the cooled popcorn to the salad. Toss lightly to mix.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Apple and Black Currant Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single, comforting portion of Apple and Black Currant Crumble rests in a rustic, off-white ceramic bowl on a well-worn wooden kitchen table. The crumble topping is a rich, golden brown, unevenly spread, with some areas slightly darker and crispier, showcasing its homemade nature. Gaps in the crumble reveal glimpses of the dark, bubbling black currants and soft, pale apple pieces underneath, their juices visibly thick and glossy. A generous dollop of fresh, white heavy cream is poured over one side of the warm crumble, starting to melt slightly into the hot fruit and topping. The bowl itself has natural imperfections and a slightly irregular shape, reflecting an everyday, cherished kitchen item. A simple, silver spoon is casually placed beside the bowl. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy kitchen, casting soft shadows that enhance the texture of the crumble. The background is minimal, hinting at a lived-in family dining area, allowing the focus to remain entirely on the comforting dessert.

ingredients.name: Apples
ingredients.quantity: 4 medium (approx. 600g), peeled, cored, diced into 1.5 cm cubes

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Prepare fruit filling. Combine diced apples, black currants, granulated sugar, and 15g flour in a large bowl. Stir well. Add lemon juice if using.
Transfer fruit mixture to a 20cm x 20cm baking dish.
Prepare crumble topping. In a separate bowl, combine 150g flour, cold butter cubes, brown sugar, and rolled oats (if using).
Rub butter into dry ingredients using fingertips. Mix until mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs. Do not overmix.
Evenly sprinkle crumble topping over fruit mixture in baking dish.
Bake for 35-45 minutes. Crumble topping should be golden brown. Fruit filling should be bubbling.
Let crumble cool slightly before serving.
Serve warm with a generous pour of heavy cream.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Apple and Fermented Black Currant Galette
recipes.visual_description: A single slice of Rustic Apple and Fermented Black Currant Galette rests on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate. The galette features a golden-brown, free-form pastry crust, imperfectly folded around a generous fruit filling. Thinly sliced apples, their edges slightly caramelized, are layered with whole, dark fermented black currants, some bursting to release deep purple juices. The fruit filling is visibly tender and glistening. A natural, unpiped dollop of thick, white cultured cream sits elegantly beside the galette slice, its soft texture contrasting the crisp crust. The plate offers ample negative space, highlighting the dessert. The setting is a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. A natural beige linen napkin is subtly placed. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, creating gentle shadows and emphasizing the organic textures.
instructions: To ferment black currants: Wash black currants. Combine currants, 50g sugar, 100ml water, and starter culture in a clean jar. Stir gently. Cover loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days, until slightly bubbly and tangy. Refrigerate once desired tanginess is reached.
To make cultured cream: Combine heavy cream and yogurt or buttermilk in a clean jar. Stir well. Cover loosely. Let sit at room temperature for 12-24 hours, until thickened and tangy. Refrigerate.

To prepare galette dough: Combine flour and salt in a bowl. Cut in cold butter until pea-sized crumbs form. Add cold water, 1 tablespoon at a time, mixing until dough just comes together. Form dough into a disc. Wrap in plastic. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

To assemble and bake galette: Preheat oven to 190°C. On a floured surface, roll out dough into a 30cm circle. Transfer dough to a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Peel, core, and thinly slice apples. In a bowl, combine sliced apples, 20g sugar, cornstarch, and lemon juice. Toss to coat. Spread apple mixture evenly over dough, leaving a 5cm border. Spoon fermented black currants over apples. Fold dough border over filling, pleating as needed. Bake for 35-45 minutes, until crust is golden brown and filling is bubbly. Cool on a wire rack.
To serve: Slice galette into 4 portions. Serve warm or at room temperature. Top each slice with a dollop of cultured cream.
notes: Adjust fermentation time for black currants based on desired tanginess.
The cultured cream provides a tangy counterpoint to the sweet fruit.
For a zero-waste approach, apple peels and cores can be used to make a fruit scrap vinegar or infused water.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Loin Medallions with Apple-Black Currant Cream Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of pan-seared pork loin medallions is centrally placed on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. Two thick, golden-brown seared pork medallions are nestled together, not fanned. A generous ladle of rich, creamy, light purple-red sauce, infused with the vibrant hues of black currants, cascades over and around the pork. Visible within the sauce are tender, pale apple chunks and plump, dark black currants, providing textural contrast. The pork's exterior is crisp, while the interior appears juicy. The plate is positioned on a well-used wooden dining table, with a casually draped off-white cloth napkin to one side. The scene is lit with warm, inviting kitchen light, creating a cozy and comforting atmosphere, typical of a homely family meal. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space around the food.
instructions: Cut pork loin into 2 cm thick medallions. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear pork medallions for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove pork from skillet and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced shallot to the skillet. Cook for 2 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Core and cut apples into 2 cm chunks. Add apple chunks to the skillet. Cook for 3-4 minutes until slightly softened.
Stir in black currants. Cook for 2 minutes.
Sprinkle flour over the apple and currant mixture. Stir for 1 minute to cook the flour.
Gradually pour in chicken stock, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in heavy cream. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer. Cook for 3-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens slightly.
Return pork medallions to the skillet, nestling them into the sauce. Simmer for 1-2 minutes to heat through.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken Supreme, Artichoke Barigoule, Truffle Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly roasted chicken supreme rests elegantly on a pristine, matte white bone china plate. Its golden-crisp skin, deeply caramelized, contrasts with the succulent white meat visible at the edges. Adjacent to the chicken, a small, artfully composed cluster of tender artichoke barigoule quarters, some retaining a slight char, presents a subtle green-beige hue. A rich, dark black truffle jus forms an organic, flowing pool around the elements, its glossy surface catching the light. A few vibrant green micro-herbs are meticulously placed atop the artichoke, adding a delicate touch of color and height. Abundant white space surrounds the components, emphasizing the dish's minimalist elegance. The plate sits on a polished white Carrara marble surface, illuminated by dramatic, soft overhead lighting that creates subtle, refined shadows. A folded white linen napkin completes the luxurious, uncluttered setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Traditionally served as a refined main course in a multi-course French meal.

ingredients.name: chicken supremes (breast with skin and wing bone attached)
large globe artichokes (or high-quality frozen artichoke hearts)
fresh black truffle, thinly sliced or finely minced (or high-quality truffle oil/paste)

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).

**Prepare Artichoke Barigoule**: Trim fresh artichokes. Remove outer leaves, cut off top third, trim stem. Scoop out fuzzy choke. Immediately rub cut surfaces with lemon. Quarter hearts. If using frozen, thaw and quarter.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add shallot and garlic. Sauté until translucent, about 3 minutes.
Add artichoke hearts, white wine, 200 ml chicken stock, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook until tender, 15-20 minutes for fresh, less for frozen.
Remove artichokes. Reduce liquid by half. Return artichokes to liquid. Keep warm. Season with salt.
**Prepare Black Truffle Jus**: Pour 500 ml chicken stock into a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce stock by two-thirds, until thick and syrupy. This takes 15-20 minutes.
Add Madeira wine. Simmer 2 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in fresh truffle. Season with salt. (If using truffle oil/paste, add just before serving.)
Optional: Whisk in 5g butter for gloss. Keep warm.
**Cook Chicken Supreme**: Pat chicken supremes dry thoroughly. Season skin generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in an oven-safe, heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken supremes skin-side down in hot pan. Sear undisturbed for 6-8 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crisp.
Flip chicken. Add 30g butter to pan. Baste chicken with melted butter.
Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) at thickest part.
Remove chicken from oven. Rest on a wire rack for 5 minutes before plating.
**Plate the Dish**: Place a small, neat portion of artichoke barigoule (2-3 quarters or a small mound) slightly off-center on each plate.
Carefully place one rested chicken supreme next to the artichoke, skin-side up.
Spoon a generous drizzle of the black truffle jus around the chicken and artichoke.
Garnish with a few micro-herbs. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Apples with Black Currant Walnut Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly baked apple stands upright on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The apple's skin is a warm golden-brown, transitioning to a light tan where peeled. Its core cavity is filled with a rich, textured walnut crumble, dotted with dark, glossy black currants. The walnuts in the crumble are visibly chopped, offering textural contrast. Beside the apple, a neat, elegant dollop of smooth, off-white cinnamon cream reflects the natural light. A delicate, even dusting of dark cocoa powder lightly covers parts of the apple and the plate, adding visual depth and a subtle color contrast. The composition is balanced with appropriate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a neatly folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, blurred modern bistro background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Core each apple, leaving the bottom intact. Peel the top third of each apple's skin. Brush cut surfaces with lemon juice to prevent browning.
For the crumble: In a bowl, combine flour, brown sugar, 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon, and salt. Add cold butter cubes. Rub with fingertips until mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Stir in chopped walnuts.
In a small bowl, combine black currants with 20g granulated sugar and remaining 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon.
Stuff each apple cavity with the black currant mixture.
Place stuffed apples in a small baking dish. Top each apple generously with the walnut crumble mixture.
Add 50ml water to the bottom of the baking dish. This creates steam.
Bake for 30-40 minutes, or until apples are tender and crumble is golden brown. Baking time varies by apple size and type.
While apples bake, prepare the cinnamon cream. In a cold bowl, whip heavy cream, 2 tablespoons granulated sugar, and vanilla extract until soft peaks form.
Serve each baked apple warm. Place on a plate. Spoon a dollop of cinnamon cream beside it. Lightly dust the plate and apple with cocoa powder.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Pork Goulash
recipes.special_requests: Slavic cuisine, pork fillet, don't have fermented whole peeled tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A generous, homely single portion of Creamy Pork Goulash is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl, showcasing its rich, comforting essence. Tender pork chunks, about 3-4 cm, are nestled amongst soft, diced carrots and onions, all coated in a velvety, reddish-brown sauce. The sauce, thickened naturally, has a creamy sheen from the added dairy. A sprinkle of fresh, thinly sliced green onions provides a vibrant green contrast on top. The dish is casually arranged, allowing the hearty ingredients to naturally overlap. It sits on a well-worn wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen light. Beside the bowl, a simple, sturdy metal spoon rests on a casually folded linen napkin. The setting evokes a cozy, lived-in family kitchen, prioritizing warmth and authentic comfort over formality.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with mashed potatoes
Serve with egg noodles
Serve with crusty bread for dipping
Serve with pickled vegetables like dill pickles
instructions: Cut pork fillet into 3-4 cm chunks. Season pork generously with salt and black pepper.
Dice onions and carrots into 1 cm pieces. Mince garlic.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add pork chunks to the pot in a single layer. Brown pork on all sides. Do not overcrowd; work in batches if necessary. Remove browned pork and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onions to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add diced carrots and minced garlic. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in ground cumin and sweet paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and beef broth. Scrape the bottom of the pot to loosen any browned bits.
Return browned pork chunks to the pot. Bring the mixture to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low, cover the pot, and simmer for 60-90 minutes, or until the pork is very tender.
Stir in the heavy cream. Simmer for another 5 minutes, uncovered, allowing the sauce to thicken slightly.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and black pepper as needed.
Thinly slice green onions for garnish.
Serve hot, garnished with sliced green onions.
notes: Ensure the pork is braised until fork-tender for the best texture and flavor.
Adjust the amount of paprika to your preference; sweet paprika adds color and mild flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Pork Shoulder with Fermented Tomato Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of sustainable pork shoulder is presented on a handcrafted, matte off-white ceramic plate. Two generous, irregularly shaped chunks of golden-brown braised pork, deeply caramelized from searing, are nestled in a rich, glossy, deep red-orange fermented tomato sauce. The sauce coats the pork beautifully, with visible bits of tender onion and carrot. A vibrant green carrot top gremolata, finely chopped, is lightly sprinkled over the pork and sauce, adding a fresh contrast. A few delicate, thin slices of fresh green onion tops are scattered for garnish. The plate features ample negative space, highlighting the natural textures and colors of the ingredients. The setting is minimalistic: a light, reclaimed wood table surface, with an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone beside the plate. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from the side, emphasizing its pure beauty. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a subtle hint of green from a nearby plant, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.

ingredients.name: Green onions
ingredients.quantity: 1 bunch (white and green parts separated, root ends reserved)

instructions: Prepare zero-waste stock: Combine reserved onion peels, garlic skins, carrot peels, and green onion root ends in a saucepan. Add 1 liter of water. Simmer for 30 minutes. Strain and reserve stock.
Season pork chunks generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear pork chunks on all sides until deeply golden brown. Remove pork and set aside.
Add diced yellow onion and diced carrots to the Dutch oven. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add smashed garlic and ground cumin. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze the pot with 200ml of the reserved zero-waste stock, scraping up any browned bits. Add crushed fermented tomatoes and return pork to the pot.
Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low. Cover and braise for 2-2.5 hours, or until pork is fork-tender. Check liquid level periodically and add more stock if needed.
While pork braises, prepare carrot top gremolata: Finely chop reserved carrot green tops and fresh parsley. Combine in a small bowl with a drizzle of olive oil.
Remove pork from the pot. Increase heat to medium-high. Reduce the sauce until slightly thickened, about 10-15 minutes. Stir in heavy cream. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Return pork to the sauce. Serve individual portions of braised pork with ample sauce. Garnish with carrot top gremolata. Serve with finely sliced green onion greens.
notes: This recipe utilizes vegetable scraps to create a flavorful zero-waste stock, enhancing sustainability.
Fermented tomatoes provide a deep umami flavor and natural acidity.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Mushroom-Parmesan Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table. A rich, pale cream-colored mushroom-Parmesan sauce forms a base, slightly pooled in the center. Two to three thick medallions of pan-seared chicken, with a golden-brown crust, are arranged neatly on top of the sauce, showcasing their tender interior. Beside the chicken, vibrant green broccoli florets, tender-crisp with subtle charred edges, are artfully placed. Bright red halved cherry tomatoes, softened and slightly burst from roasting, add pops of color and a hint of sweetness. The composition is balanced and professional, with moderate negative space. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green parsley garnishes the dish, adding a touch of freshness. Standard silver flatware rests beside the plate, and a crisp white cotton napkin is folded nearby, completing the modern bistro setting under natural, even lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Toss broccoli florets and halved cherry tomatoes with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes, until tender-crisp and slightly charred.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Bake chicken for 8-12 minutes, until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Rest on a cutting board.
Return skillet to medium heat. Add butter. Sauté minced shallot for 2 minutes until softened.
Add sliced mushrooms to skillet. Cook for 5-7 minutes, until browned and tender.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from bottom of skillet. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer gently for 3-5 minutes, until sauce thickens slightly.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese until melted and smooth. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Slice rested chicken breasts into thick medallions.
Ladle creamy mushroom-Parmesan sauce onto individual plates. Arrange chicken medallions on top of sauce. Place roasted broccoli florets and cherry tomatoes alongside.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Always check chicken internal temperature with a meat thermometer to ensure food safety.
Adjust sauce consistency by simmering longer for thicker sauce, or adding a splash more broth for thinner.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Chicken and Beef Medallions with Parmesan Crust
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, on a simple wooden table. A seared chicken medallion and a seared beef medallion, both with a golden-brown parmesan-herb crust, are positioned slightly offset. The chicken is thick and juicy; the beef medallion shows a rich red medium-rare interior. Beside the meats, a vibrant cluster of roasted broccoli florets, tender-crisp with slight charring, is arranged with bright red halved cherry tomatoes. A small pool of rich, glossy mushroom jus, deep brown, is spooned artfully beside the proteins. The presentation is clean and organized, with moderate negative space. A folded cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors against a soft, blurred restaurant-style background.

ingredients.name: Chicken breasts
ingredients.quantity: 2 large (approx. 200-250g each), cut horizontally into 2 medallions each

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Combine grated parmesan, panko, chopped parsley, and thyme in a shallow dish. Season with salt and pepper.
Pat chicken and beef medallions dry. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken medallions for 3 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer to a plate. Cook to 75°C internal temperature.
Sear beef medallions for 2-3 minutes per side for medium-rare. Transfer to a plate.
Press one side of each seared chicken and beef medallion into the parmesan-herb mixture to form a crust.
Place crusted chicken and beef back into the pan (or on a baking sheet). Bake for 8-12 minutes, or until chicken reaches 75°C and beef is desired doneness. Rest meats for 5 minutes after baking.
Toss broccoli florets and halved cherry tomatoes with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes until tender-crisp.
In the same pan used for searing (or a clean pan), melt butter with remaining 15ml olive oil over medium heat. Add sliced mushrooms and cook until golden, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced shallots and garlic to mushrooms. Cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Deglaze pan with red wine (if using), scraping up browned bits. Reduce by half.
Pour in chicken stock. Simmer for 5-7 minutes until sauce slightly thickens. Season mushroom jus with salt and pepper.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Pork and Lentil Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spiced Pork and Lentil Stew is presented in a clean, white porcelain dinner bowl, placed on a simple wooden table. The stew forms a rich, inviting mound in the center, showcasing tender, irregular chunks of dark brown seared pork, nestled amongst plump, earthy brown lentils and soft, organic pieces of oyster mushrooms. The stew’s sauce is a deep reddish-brown, thick and glossy, clinging to the ingredients. A generous scattering of vibrant green, freshly chopped coriander leaves provides a striking color contrast and freshness atop the stew. To the side, a small white bowl of fluffy white basmati rice sits, ready to accompany the stew. A piece of warm naan bread, lightly charred, is folded neatly beside the rice. A simple cotton napkin rests nearby. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere typical of a casual bistro, with a subtly blurred background.
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Season pork chunks with salt and pepper. Sear pork in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove pork and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced ginger and garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in garam masala, ground cumin, and red chili powder. Toast spices for 30 seconds until aromatic.
Return seared pork to the pot. Add rinsed brown lentils, crushed tomatoes, vegetable broth, and oyster sauce. Stir well to combine.
Bring the mixture to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 60-75 minutes, or until pork is very tender and lentils are cooked through. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Stir in the torn oyster mushrooms during the last 15 minutes of cooking. Cook until mushrooms are tender.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped coriander.

recipes.recipe_name: Currant and Orange Drizzle Cake
recipes.visual_description: A comforting slice of Currant and Orange Drizzle Cake sits on a plain, cream-colored ceramic plate. The cake slice is golden-brown on the outside with a moist, light crumb visible inside, dotted generously with dark, plump currants. The top of the cake glistens from the absorbed orange drizzle, creating a slightly sticky, inviting texture. In the soft-focused background, the remaining whole cake rests on a simple, white cake stand, hinting at generous portions. The setting is a well-used wooden dining table under warm, ambient kitchen lighting. A casually placed, folded cloth napkin in a neutral tone lies nearby. The scene is unpretentious, emphasizing homemade comfort and warmth, as if prepared for a family gathering.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (160°C fan/Gas Mark 4).
Grease and line a 20cm round cake tin.
Cream softened butter and 175g caster sugar in a large bowl until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time, adding a spoonful of flour with each egg to prevent curdling.
Sift remaining self-raising flour and baking powder into the mixture.
Add milk and orange zest. Fold gently until just combined.
Stir in currants.
Spoon batter into the prepared cake tin. Level the top.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
While cake bakes, prepare the drizzle. Heat orange juice and 50g caster sugar in a small saucepan over low heat.
Stir until sugar dissolves. Bring to a gentle simmer for 2 minutes. Remove from heat.
Once cake is out of the oven, immediately pierce the top all over with a skewer.
Pour the hot orange drizzle evenly over the hot cake.
Let cake cool completely in the tin before turning out and serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Currant Sponge Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single generous slice of Classic Currant Sponge Cake sits on a simple, slightly off-white ceramic plate. The cake slice reveals a light, golden-yellow crumb, speckled generously with dark, plump currants. The top crust of the cake is a delicate golden-brown, with a fine dusting of white icing sugar. The texture appears soft and moist, with a tender crumb. In the background, on a well-worn wooden kitchen table, the remaining whole 18 cm round cake sits on a plain cake stand, mirroring the inviting warmth of the slice. A crumpled, light-colored linen napkin rests casually beside the plate. The scene is bathed in warm, natural light, evoking a comforting, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. No elaborate garnishes, just the cake's natural beauty.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour an 18 cm round cake tin. Line base with baking paper.
Cream butter and caster sugar in a bowl until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time. Mix well after each addition.
Sift flour, baking powder, and salt into the butter mixture. Fold gently until just combined.
Stir in dried currants. If batter is very thick, add milk.
Pour batter into prepared tin. Smooth top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes. Cake is done when golden and a skewer inserted into center comes out clean.
Cool in tin for 10 minutes. Transfer to wire rack to cool completely.
Dust with icing sugar before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Currant Tea Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single slice of Spiced Currant Tea Cake sits on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. The cake slice is golden-brown, revealing a tender crumb studded generously with dark, plump currants. A thin, delicate drizzle of white glaze cascades down its sides. In the background, slightly out of focus, the full Bundt cake rests on a plain wooden cake stand, showcasing its intricate, fluted shape and inviting golden hue. The setting is a homely family kitchen table made of well-used wood. A casually placed, light-colored cloth napkin and a standard metal fork complete the relaxed, comforting scene. Warm, cozy lighting illuminates the cake, emphasizing its inviting texture and classic appeal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour a 23 cm Bundt pan.
In a large bowl, cream softened butter and granulated sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time. Mix well after each addition.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
Add dry ingredients to wet ingredients in three additions, alternating with milk. Begin and end with dry. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Stir in vanilla extract.
Gently fold in dried currants.
Pour batter into prepared Bundt pan. Smooth the top.
Bake for 45-55 minutes. Or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Let cake cool in pan for 10 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
Prepare Glaze: Whisk powdered sugar and milk in a small bowl until smooth. Adjust consistency with more sugar or milk if needed.
Drizzle glaze over cooled cake. Let glaze set before serving.
notes: This cake serves 8 people generously. It is perfect for tea time or a simple dessert. It stays moist for several days when stored in an airtight container.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Currant Tea Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single generous slice of Classic Currant Tea Cake is presented on a simple, well-used white ceramic plate. The cake slice is golden-brown on top and around the edges, with a tender, moist crumb visible, speckled generously with dark, plump dried currants. The top of the cake has a light, delicate dusting of white icing sugar, creating a subtle contrast. The slice sits naturally on the plate, not perfectly centered, conveying a homemade feel. In the background, the remaining whole, round cake sits on a rustic wooden board or simple cake stand on a well-used wooden dining table. A casually placed, light-colored cloth napkin is nearby. The scene is bathed in warm, cozy lighting, evoking a relaxed family kitchen atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour a 15 cm round cake pan or small loaf pan.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Set aside.
In a large bowl, cream softened butter and granulated sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time. Mix in vanilla extract.
Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients, alternating with milk. Begin and end with dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Gently fold in dried currants.
Pour batter into prepared pan. Smooth top.
Bake for 35-45 minutes. Or until a skewer inserted into center comes out clean.
Cool cake in pan for 10 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
Dust cooled cake with icing sugar before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Currant Loaf Cake
recipes.visual_description: A thick, comforting slice of golden-brown Spiced Currant Loaf Cake stands upright on a simple, round ceramic plate. The cake's interior is moist and speckled with dark, plump currants, showcasing a tender crumb. The top of the slice is lightly dusted with white icing sugar. The plate, an off-white ceramic with a subtly imperfect rim, rests on a warm, well-worn wooden dining table. A plain silver fork lies casually beside the plate. In the softly blurred background, the remaining loaf cake sits on a rustic wooden cutting board, suggesting a recent slice. Natural, warm light from a nearby window illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere. A casually folded linen napkin is visible nearby. The overall impression is one of homemade comfort and simplicity.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a 900g loaf tin with baking paper.
Sift flour, baking powder, mixed spice, and salt into a bowl.
In a separate bowl, cream softened butter and caster sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition.
Fold half of the dry ingredients into the wet mixture. Stir in half of the milk.
Repeat with remaining dry ingredients and milk until just combined. Do not overmix.
Gently fold in the currants.
Spoon batter into the prepared loaf tin. Smooth the top.
Bake for 45-55 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Let cake cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
For the glaze: Mix icing sugar with a small amount of water or lemon juice until a thick, pourable consistency is reached. Drizzle over the cooled cake.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Currant Crumble Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous wedge of golden-brown Homestyle Currant Crumble Cake rests on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The cake slice is cut cleanly, revealing a tender, light-colored crumb studded with plump, dark currants. The top of the slice features a rustic, golden-brown crumble topping with visible coarse crumbs. The entire cake, a round 20 cm shape with its full crumble topping, sits on a wooden cake stand or cooling rack in the blurred background, hinting at more to come. The setting is a well-used wooden dining table, with a plain metal fork resting casually beside the plate and a crumpled cloth napkin nearby. Warm, cozy lighting illuminates the scene, creating a comforting, lived-in kitchen atmosphere. The focus is entirely on the inviting, homemade appearance of the cake.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a 20 cm round cake tin.
For the crumble: Combine 50g flour, 50g brown sugar, 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon, and 50g cold cubed butter in a bowl. Rub with fingertips until coarse crumbs form. Set aside.
In a large bowl, cream 120g softened butter and 150g granulated sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition.
Stir in vanilla extract.
In a separate bowl, whisk together 200g flour, baking powder, and salt.
Add dry ingredients to wet ingredients in three additions, alternating with milk. Mix until just combined.
Gently fold in 150g currants.
Pour batter into prepared cake tin. Sprinkle crumble topping evenly over the batter.
Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool cake in tin for 10 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

recipes.recipe_name: Kale and Brown Rice Fiesta Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented in a wide, shallow white ceramic bowl. Finely chopped dark green kale forms the base. Cooked brown rice kernels are scattered throughout. Black beans and golden corn kernels provide pops of color. Finely diced red onion and minced fresh green chili are evenly distributed. Cubes of creamy green avocado are gently folded in. Fresh, bright green cilantro leaves are sprinkled generously over the top. The chipotle-lime vinaigrette lightly coats all ingredients. A rich palette of greens, dark black beans, golden corn, and reddish-purple onion creates visual appeal. Textures include crisp kale, tender rice, firm beans, sweet corn, creamy avocado, and a slight crunch. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table surface with a natural cotton napkin. Lighting is natural and even. A simple, modern fork rests beside the bowl. A small ceramic dish with a lime wedge and cilantro sprigs sits nearby.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas on the side.
Offer a bowl of salsa roja or salsa verde for extra heat.
Pair with a glass of horchata or agua fresca.
instructions: Prepare brown rice. Cook according to package directions. Let cool.
Prepare kale. Wash kale leaves. Remove tough stems. Finely chop kale. Place in large bowl.
Prepare red onion. Finely dice red onion. Add to kale.
Prepare chili. Deseed and finely mince fresh chili. Add to bowl.
Prepare avocado. Dice avocado just before serving.
Combine salad ingredients. Add cooked brown rice, black beans, corn, and chopped cilantro to the bowl with kale and onion.
Make dressing. In a small bowl, whisk olive oil, lime juice, chipotle powder, cumin powder, minced garlic, maple syrup (if using), salt, and pepper.
Dress salad. Pour dressing over salad ingredients. Toss gently to combine.
Add avocado. Fold in diced avocado. Serve immediately.
notes: For best texture, add avocado just before serving to prevent browning.
Adjust chili quantity to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Raspberry Lemon Tartlets
recipes.visual_description: Four individual Raspberry Lemon Tartlets are elegantly presented on clean white porcelain dessert plates. Each tartlet, approximately 10 cm in diameter, features a perfectly golden, crisp shortcrust pastry shell with fluted edges. The shells are filled precisely with a smooth, pale yellow lemon curd, its surface gleaming softly. Vibrant red, plump fresh raspberries are meticulously arranged on top of the curd, forming a domed cluster. A delicate dusting of white powdered sugar lightly covers the raspberries and the pastry edge. The composition is clean and balanced, with ample negative space on the plate. A silver dessert fork is placed beside each plate. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface and natural, even lighting that highlights the tartlets' fresh colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served individually as a dessert.
Often accompanied by black coffee or tea.
instructions: Sift flour, icing sugar, and salt into a large bowl.
Add cold diced butter. Rub into flour mixture until it resembles coarse breadcrumbs.
Add egg yolk. Mix until dough just comes together. Do not overmix.
Form dough into a disc. Wrap in cling film. Chill for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Roll dough on a lightly floured surface to 3 mm thickness.
Cut out circles to fit 4 x 10 cm tartlet tins. Press dough into tins. Trim edges.
Prick bases with a fork. Line with parchment paper. Fill with baking beans.
Bake for 15 minutes. Remove beans and paper. Bake for another 5-7 minutes, until light golden.
Cool completely on a wire rack.
Combine lemon juice, zest, sugar, and eggs in a heatproof bowl.
Place bowl over a saucepan of simmering water (bain-marie). Do not let bowl touch water.
Whisk continuously until mixture thickens and coats the back of a spoon, approximately 8-10 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in cold butter until melted and smooth.
Strain curd through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl. This ensures smoothness.
Cover surface with cling film to prevent a skin forming. Chill until firm, at least 2 hours.
Spoon or pipe chilled lemon curd into each cooled tartlet shell. Fill almost to the brim.
Arrange fresh raspberries on top of the lemon curd. Place them neatly in a pleasing pattern.
Lightly dust with powdered sugar before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Currant Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A comforting, golden-brown currant crumble fills a rustic, deep ceramic bowl. The top crust is unevenly textured, with golden baked oats and flour crumbs. Deep purple-red currants bubble around the edges, their juices glistening from under the crisp topping. The dish is served warm, with a simple dollop of thick cream or a small jug of custard placed alongside the bowl. The bowl sits on a well-used, light wooden dining table. A plain white ceramic spoon rests next to the bowl. Natural, warm light illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, homely atmosphere. The plating is casual, showcasing a generous individual portion ready for consumption.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Wash currants. Place in a medium ovenproof dish.
Add 100g sugar and lemon zest to currants. Mix gently.
For the crumble topping: Combine flour, 75g sugar, salt, and oats in a large bowl.
Cut cold butter into small cubes. Add to flour mixture.
Rub butter into flour with fingertips until mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs.
Sprinkle crumble topping evenly over the currant mixture in the dish.
Bake for 30-35 minutes. Crumble should be golden brown. Fruit should be bubbling.
Serve warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Red Lentil Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of vibrant, reddish-orange hearty red lentil soup fills a rustic, deep ceramic bowl. The soup has a thick, comforting consistency, showcasing softened red lentils and small, tender diced carrots, celery, and onions. A swirl of its natural creaminess is visible. The surface is simply garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley, offering a fresh contrast. The bowl sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table, reflecting a homely family kitchen setting. A simple, silver spoon rests beside the bowl on a casually draped light-colored cloth napkin. The scene is bathed in warm, inviting light, creating a cozy and comforting atmosphere, emphasizing the soup's rustic appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
Offer lemon wedges on the side for a bright finish.
instructions: Rinse red lentils under cold water until water runs clear. Drain well.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Dice onion, carrot, and celery into small cubes. Add to pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Mince garlic. Add to pot with cumin and paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add rinsed lentils and vegetable broth to the pot.
Bring soup to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Simmer, uncovered, for 20-25 minutes, or until lentils are very tender and soup has thickened. Stir occasionally.
Season generously with salt and black pepper. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
For a smoother soup, use an immersion blender to partially blend the soup directly in the pot, leaving some texture. Or blend fully for a creamy consistency.
Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Chop fresh parsley. Garnish each serving with parsley. Serve immediately with lemon wedges on the side, if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Lavender Panna Cotta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lavender Panna Cotta rests on a plain, light-colored ceramic dessert plate. The panna cotta is a pale, creamy off-white with a smooth, slightly wobbly texture. It holds its shape perfectly, showcasing its delicate set. A small sprig of fresh lavender or a few vibrant raspberries are placed casually beside it for a pop of color and natural freshness. The plate is set on a well-used wooden dining table, reflecting a homely family kitchen environment. A casually placed cloth napkin and warm, soft lighting from kitchen fixtures enhance the inviting, lived-in atmosphere. The background is minimal, keeping focus on the comforting dessert.
instructions: Place gelatine leaves in a bowl of cold water. Let them soften for 5-10 minutes.
Combine double cream, whole milk, granulated sugar, and dried culinary lavender in a saucepan.
Heat mixture over medium heat. Stir until sugar dissolves. Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Cover saucepan. Let lavender steep for 15-20 minutes.
Strain mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl. Discard lavender.
Squeeze excess water from bloomed gelatine leaves. Add gelatine to warm strained mixture. Stir until fully dissolved.
Stir in vanilla extract.
Divide mixture evenly among four 150 ml ramekins or serving glasses.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or until fully set.
To serve, dip bottom of ramekins briefly in hot water. Invert onto dessert plates.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Glazed Mini Cakes
recipes.visual_description: Nine perfectly uniform, small square lemon glazed mini cakes are neatly arranged on a simple white ceramic serving platter. Each cake features a smooth, opaque, pale yellow lemon glaze, with a slight sheen, covering its top and sides. The texture of the cake beneath the glaze is subtly visible at the edges, suggesting a soft, tender crumb. The pieces are evenly spaced, creating a balanced and inviting display. The platter rests on a well-used light wooden dining table, suggesting a comfortable, lived-in kitchen atmosphere. Warm, cozy lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the cakes' vibrant color. A casually placed white linen napkin adds a touch of simple elegance. The overall presentation is clean and uncluttered, emphasizing the delicate, homemade quality of the petit fours.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with coffee or tea.
Present as part of an afternoon tea spread.
Offer as a light dessert after a meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a 20x20 cm square baking tin.
Cream softened butter and granulated sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time. Mix well after each addition.
Sift plain flour and baking powder together. Gradually fold into the wet mixture.
Stir in milk and lemon zest. Mix until just combined.
Pour batter into the prepared tin. Smooth the top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool cake in the tin for 10 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
Prepare glaze: Whisk powdered sugar and fresh lemon juice until smooth. Adjust consistency with more sugar or juice if needed.
Once cake is cool, trim edges. Cut cake into 9 uniform small square pieces.
Place wire rack over a baking sheet. Pour glaze evenly over each cake piece.
Let glaze set. Serve when glaze is firm.
notes: This recipe yields simple, classic petit fours perfect for home bakers.

recipes.recipe_name: Rigatoni with Spicy Italian Sausage and Sautéed Kale
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Rigatoni with Spicy Italian Sausage and Sautéed Kale is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The rigatoni pasta is perfectly al dente, coated in a light, savory sauce. Irregular chunks of browned Italian sausage are interspersed throughout the pasta. Dark green, tender sautéed kale leaves provide a vibrant color contrast. Finely diced yellow onion and minced garlic bits are visible within the sauce. A generous sprinkle of freshly grated Pecorino Romano cheese rests on top, along with a few vibrant red pepper flakes. The dish has a balanced composition, with moderate negative space around the edges. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple light wooden table surface, a white cotton napkin folded neatly beside the plate, and a silver fork resting next to the napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the textures. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with extra grated Pecorino Romano cheese.
Offer with crusty Italian bread for dipping.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120 ml pasta water. Drain pasta.

While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add sausage meat. Break it apart with a spoon. Cook until browned and cooked through. Remove sausage from skillet, leaving rendered fat.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Reduce wine by half.
Add chicken broth and chopped kale. Bring to a simmer. Cook until kale is tender, about 5-7 minutes.
Return cooked sausage to the skillet. Add cooked rigatoni. Toss to combine.
Add grated Pecorino Romano and half of the reserved pasta water. Toss well. Add more pasta water if needed to create a light sauce.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
notes: Ensure pasta is cooked al dente for best texture.
Adjust red pepper flakes to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Lavender Shortbread Cookies
recipes.visual_description: Lavender Shortbread Cookies are arranged casually on a rustic ceramic plate. The cookies are round, about 6 cm, with lightly pricked surfaces. Their color is a pale, creamy yellow from butter. Small, dark purple flecks of dried lavender are visible throughout the dough. Edges are lightly golden, centers remain soft and crumbly. The texture appears delicate and sandy, characteristic of classic shortbread. A few cookies are stacked loosely, others spread out, suggesting a homemade, approachable feel. The plate sits on a well-used wooden kitchen table, with a simple, folded linen napkin nearby. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen window illuminates the scene. A plain, ceramic teacup filled with steaming tea is placed beside the plate, completing the comforting, homely setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a cup of hot tea or coffee.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Cream softened butter and caster sugar in a large bowl until light and fluffy.
In a separate bowl, whisk together plain flour, dried culinary lavender, and a pinch of salt.
Gradually add dry ingredients to butter mixture. Mix until a soft dough forms. Do not overmix.
Gather dough into a ball. Flatten slightly into a disc. Wrap in cling film. Chill for 30 minutes.
On a lightly floured surface, roll out dough to 1 cm thickness.
Cut dough into rounds or squares. Alternatively, form a log and slice into 1 cm thick fingers.
Place cookies on the prepared baking tray. Prick each cookie with a fork a few times.
Bake for 20-25 minutes. Cookies should be pale golden at the edges.
Remove from oven. Let cool on the tray for 5 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
notes: Do not overwork the dough to ensure tender, crumbly shortbread.
Ensure lavender is culinary grade for consumption.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Hearty Lentil Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Rustic Hearty Lentil Soup is presented in a deep, simple, and slightly imperfect ceramic bowl. The soup is thick and substantial, showcasing whole, tender green lentils and clearly visible diced vegetables including carrots, celery, and onion, all retaining their natural shapes and earthy colors of brown, orange, and light green. A sprinkle of vibrant green, freshly chopped parsley garnishes the surface, contrasting with the soup's warm tones. The bowl sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table, suggesting a comfortable family kitchen setting. A simple metal spoon rests beside the bowl, and a casually folded cloth napkin is nearby. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of kitchen fixtures, creating a cozy and lived-in atmosphere with a soft, blurred background that might hint at everyday kitchen elements like a spice rack or worn cutting board, without distracting from the dish.
instructions: Rinse lentils thoroughly under cold water. Drain.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced bacon. Cook until crisp. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon; set aside. Leave rendered fat in the pot.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until vegetables soften.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rinsed lentils, broth, bay leaf, and dried thyme to the pot. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until lentils are tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove bay leaf. Season soup with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish with reserved crisp bacon and fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Green Lentil and Vegetable Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of hearty green lentil and vegetable soup fills a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. The soup is thick, showcasing tender green lentils and soft, small-diced carrots, celery, and onion. Its earthy brown and green tones are brightened by the orange of the vegetables and the red flecks from the tomatoes. A vibrant sprinkle of roughly chopped fresh parsley garnishes the surface, adding color and freshness. The bowl rests on a well-used, textured wooden dining table, with a simple metal spoon beside it. A casually folded, plain linen napkin completes the homely setting. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, emphasizing the comforting and nourishing qualities of this rustic, simple dish, evoking a cozy family kitchen.
instructions: Rinse green lentils under cold water. Drain well.
Small-dice carrots, celery, and onion.
Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced carrots, celery, and onion. Sauté 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, dried thyme, and bay leaf. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rinsed lentils, vegetable broth, and diced tomatoes.
Bring soup to a boil. Reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer 30-40 minutes, or until lentils are tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove bay leaf. Season soup with salt and black pepper to taste.
Roughly chop fresh parsley for garnish.
Serve hot in bowls, garnished with fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Indian Red Lentil Dal
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of vibrant, creamy Indian Red Lentil Dal is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with slightly chipped edges. The dal is a comforting yellow-orange, showcasing its smooth, slightly thick texture. A swirl of dark, glossy tempering oil (tadka) with visible crackled mustard seeds, cumin seeds, crisp curry leaves, and whole dried red chilies rests on the surface, creating a dynamic contrast. Scattered fresh, bright green chopped coriander leaves provide a final pop of color. The bowl is set on a warm, well-worn wooden dining table. To the side, a modest stack of soft, slightly charred naan bread is casually placed, ready for dipping. A simple, folded off-white cloth napkin lies nearby. The scene is bathed in warm, soft kitchen lighting, evoking a cozy, lived-in family dining atmosphere. The background is minimal, focusing entirely on the homely dish and its accompaniments, reflecting a traditional Indian meal setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with steamed basmati rice or warm naan bread.
Offer a side of plain yogurt or raita.
Include a small bowl of Indian pickles (achar) or a fresh kachumber salad (diced cucumber, tomato, onion).
instructions: Rinse red lentils thoroughly under cold water until water runs clear.
Combine rinsed lentils, 1 litre water, turmeric powder, and salt in a large pot.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer, uncovered, for 15-20 minutes. Lentils should be very soft and mushy. Stir occasionally.
While lentils cook, prepare the tempering (tadka). Heat ghee or oil in a small pan over medium heat.
Add mustard seeds. Let them splutter.
Add cumin seeds, asafoetida, curry leaves, and dried red chilies. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened and translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chili. Sauté for 1 minute until raw smell disappears.
Add diced tomato, cumin powder, and coriander powder. Cook for 5-7 minutes. Tomatoes should soften and mixture should thicken.
Pour the cooked lentil mixture into the pan with the tempering. Stir well to combine.
Simmer for another 5 minutes to allow flavors to meld. Add a splash of hot water if dal is too thick.
Garnish with fresh chopped coriander leaves before serving.
notes: Adjust green chili quantity to desired spice level.
For a smoother dal, mash lentils slightly with the back of a spoon before adding tempering.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Lentil Shepherd's Pie
recipes.visual_description: A generous, rustic portion of Hearty Lentil Shepherd's Pie is served on a simple, round white ceramic plate. The golden-brown mashed potato topping, slightly mounded, shows peaks and valleys from a fork, with a light crispness on its surface and scattered melted Parmesan. Below, the rich, savory lentil and vegetable filling, visible where the mash is slightly uneven, reveals diced carrots, onions, and mushrooms in a thick, herb-flecked gravy. The colors are warm and earthy: deep brown for the filling, golden-cream for the potato, and flecks of green from fresh herbs. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table. In the background, the full ceramic baking dish of the pie is visible, suggesting a family meal. A plain cloth napkin is casually placed nearby. Warm, natural light from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere typical of a family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served directly from the baking dish at the family table.
Often accompanied by a simple side of steamed green vegetables like peas or green beans.
instructions: Prepare lentils: Rinse lentils. Boil lentils in 1 litre water for 20 minutes. Drain.
Prepare vegetables: Dice carrots, onions, celery. Mince garlic. Slice mushrooms.
Sauté aromatics: Heat oil in a large pot or Dutch oven. Add diced onions, carrots, and celery. Cook 8-10 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook 5 more minutes.
Build base: Stir in tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes. Stir in flour. Cook 1 minute.
Add liquids and lentils: Gradually whisk in vegetable stock. Add cooked lentils, chopped thyme, and rosemary. Bring to a simmer.
Cook filling: Reduce heat. Simmer gently for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens and flavors meld. Season with salt and pepper.
Prepare mash: Peel and cut potatoes into large chunks. Boil potatoes in salted water until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well.
Mash potatoes: Return hot potatoes to the pot. Add butter and milk. Mash until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Assemble pie: Preheat oven to 190°C. Pour lentil filling into a large oven-safe baking dish (approx. 30x20 cm). Spread mashed potato evenly over the filling.
Bake: Sprinkle grated Parmesan cheese over the potato. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until topping is golden brown and filling is bubbling.
Rest and serve: Let pie rest 10 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Vietnamese Shaking Beef with Mint Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant single portion of Vietnamese Shaking Beef is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Seared beef tenderloin cubes, deeply caramelized with a glossy sheen, are neatly arranged on one side of the plate. Their rich brown exterior contrasts with a tender, pinkish interior. Adjacent to the beef is a generous, artfully mounded fresh salad composed of crisp romaine lettuce, delicate watercress, vibrant green mint leaves, and halved bright red cherry tomatoes. Thinly sliced red onion adds a subtle purple accent. The elements are balanced with moderate negative space. A small, elegant white bowl of light amber nuoc cham dipping sauce sits on the wooden table beside the plate, accompanied by a pair of polished chopsticks and a neatly folded cotton napkin. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and fresh colors against a subtle, blurred restaurant-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice.
Provide nuoc cham dipping sauce on the side.
Offer additional fresh herbs like cilantro or perilla for diners to add.
instructions: Cook jasmine rice according to package directions. Keep warm.
Cut beef tenderloin into 2.5 cm cubes. Pat dry with paper towels.
In a bowl, combine 15 ml soy sauce, 15 ml oyster sauce, 5 g sugar, 2.5 g black pepper, and 2 minced garlic cloves. Add beef cubes. Toss to coat. Marinate for at least 15 minutes.
Prepare the mint salad: Wash and dry romaine lettuce, watercress, and mint leaves. Tear larger lettuce leaves into bite-sized pieces. Halve cherry tomatoes. Thinly slice red onion.

For the dipping sauce (nuoc cham): In a small bowl, combine remaining fish sauce, lime juice, remaining sugar, 60 ml warm water, 2 minced garlic cloves, and thinly sliced red chili (if using). Stir until sugar dissolves.
Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a large wok or heavy skillet over high heat until smoking.
Add half of the marinated beef in a single layer. Sear quickly for 1-2 minutes per side until browned. Do not overcrowd the pan. Remove beef to a plate.
Add remaining 15 ml vegetable oil to the pan. Add sliced shallots and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add remaining beef to the pan. Sear quickly. Return all beef to the pan. Add remaining soy sauce and oyster sauce. Toss rapidly for 30 seconds to coat. Remove from heat.
In a large bowl, combine lettuce, watercress, mint, cherry tomatoes, and red onion. Gently toss with a small amount of the nuoc cham dressing.
Divide cooked jasmine rice among four plates. Arrange the mint salad beside the rice.
Place seared beef chunks next to the salad. Serve immediately with remaining nuoc cham on the side for dipping.
notes: Ensure the wok or skillet is very hot before adding beef for proper searing and caramelization.
Do not overcrowd the pan when searing beef; cook in batches if necessary to maintain high heat.
Adjust the amount of chili in the nuoc cham to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Pad See Ew Gai (Thai Stir-fried Wide Rice Noodles with Chicken)
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Pad See Ew is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The wide, flat rice noodles are glossy with a deep caramel-brown hue from the dark soy sauce, gently tangled and piled centrally. Interspersed throughout are bite-sized, seared chicken chunks, displaying a light golden-brown exterior. Vibrant green Chinese broccoli pieces, with thinly sliced stems and larger wilted leaves, provide a fresh contrast. Scrambled egg pieces, in soft yellow and white, are visible amongst the noodles. The dish has a slightly charred, wok-cooked appearance. Moderate negative space surrounds the dish. Beside the plate, a pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests on a small ceramic chopstick rest. A folded grey cotton napkin is placed to the left. To the right, a small, traditional ceramic dish holds a spoonful of prik nam pla (fish sauce with sliced chilies and lime), ready for optional seasoning. The setting is a simple light wooden table surface, illuminated by natural, even lighting from the side, with a subtly blurred background suggesting a modern bistro environment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small bowl of prik nam pla (fish sauce with sliced bird's eye chilies and lime juice) for extra heat and tang.
Eat with chopsticks and a spoon.
instructions: Prepare noodles: Gently separate fresh noodles. If using dried, rehydrate per package, then drain well.
Prepare sauce: In a small bowl, combine dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, and white vinegar. Mix well.
Heat wok: Heat 30ml vegetable oil in a large wok over high heat until smoking.
Cook chicken: Add chicken chunks to the wok. Stir-fry for 4-5 minutes until cooked through and lightly browned. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from wok. Set aside.
Cook garlic and eggs: Add remaining 30ml oil to the wok. Add minced garlic. Stir-fry for 15 seconds until fragrant. Pour in beaten eggs. Scramble eggs for 30 seconds until just set.
Add broccoli: Add Chinese broccoli stems to the wok. Stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until slightly tender-crisp. Add broccoli leaves. Stir-fry for another minute until wilted.
Combine ingredients: Add cooked chicken and prepared noodles to the wok. Pour sauce mixture over everything.
Stir-fry: Toss vigorously for 2-3 minutes to coat noodles evenly and heat through. Noodles should develop a slightly charred aroma.
Serve: Transfer immediately to serving plates.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Creamy Chicken and Spinach Penne
recipes.visual_description: The Tuscan Creamy Chicken and Spinach Penne is presented in a clean, white porcelain dinner bowl. Al dente penne pasta is generously coated in a rich, creamy, off-white sauce, subtly tinted by sun-dried tomatoes. Tender, golden-brown chicken chunks are interspersed throughout the pasta. Vibrant green wilted spinach leaves provide a fresh contrast. Small pieces of bright red sun-dried tomatoes add pops of color. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of freshly chopped green parsley and finely grated pale yellow Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese. The composition is natural and flowing, with moderate negative space. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware, under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese at the table.

ingredients.name: Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese
ingredients.quantity: 60 g, grated, plus more for serving

instructions: Cut chicken breasts into 2.5 cm cubes. Season chicken with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Cook until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add minced garlic and chopped sun-dried tomatoes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth and heavy cream. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly.
Meanwhile, cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 125 ml of pasta water.
Add cooked chicken and fresh spinach to the sauce. Stir until spinach wilts, about 2 minutes.
Add drained penne pasta to the skillet. Add grated Parmigiano-Reggiano. Toss to combine. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water gradually until desired consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Do not overcook the pasta; it should be al dente.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Potato Gnocchi and Parmesan Cream
recipes.visual_description: The dish is centrally plated on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A pan-seared chicken breast, cooked to a golden-brown crust and tender interior, is the focal point. Beside it, soft, pillowy potato gnocchi are gently arranged. A rich, creamy Parmesan sauce, pale ivory, is artfully drizzled over the gnocchi and around the chicken base. Vibrant green, slightly wilted baby spinach leaves are scattered among the gnocchi, adding color and freshness. The dish is garnished with finely chopped fresh parsley and delicate thyme leaves, providing verdant green and aromatic appeal. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space, highlighting the distinct textures and harmonious colors.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts.
Sear chicken for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Cook for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from oven. Rest on a cutting board, tented with foil, for 5 minutes.
While chicken rests, bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add potato gnocchi.
Cook gnocchi according to package directions, typically 2-3 minutes, until they float to the surface. Drain well.
In the same skillet (after removing chicken), melt butter over medium heat. Add minced garlic and thyme sprigs. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese until melted and smooth. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste. Remove thyme sprigs.
Add baby spinach to the sauce. Cook for 1-2 minutes until just wilted.
