Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2-3 minutes until rice grains are translucent at the edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed by the rice.
Begin adding hot shrimp stock, one ladle at a time. Stir continuously. Wait for each ladle of stock to be almost fully absorbed before adding the next.
Continue adding stock and stirring for 18-20 minutes, or until the rice is creamy and al dente. The risotto should be fluid, not dry.
While risotto cooks, quickly sear shrimp in a separate pan with a drizzle of olive oil. Cook for 1-2 minutes per side until pink and just cooked through. Do not overcook.
Remove risotto from heat. Stir in cold butter and grated Parmigiano Reggiano until melted and creamy (mantecatura).
Gently fold in the seared shrimp.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Grate lemon zest over the risotto. Chop fresh parsley.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh parsley and additional lemon zest.
notes: The key to a good risotto is constant stirring and gradual addition of hot stock, allowing the rice to release its starches and become creamy.
Ensure shrimp are not overcooked; they should remain tender and succulent.
traditional_techniques: Mantecatura (creaming the risotto with butter and cheese)

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef & Blueberry Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Hearty Beef & Blueberry Stew is presented in a deep, rustic white ceramic bowl on a simple wooden table. The stew features large, tender 3-4 cm chunks of slow-cooked beef, showcasing a rich, dark brown exterior and a succulent interior. Interspersed among the beef are vibrant orange 2-3 cm thick carrot rounds and deep purple, slightly burst blueberries, all enveloped in a thick, glossy, reddish-brown gravy. The stew's surface is lightly dotted with fresh green chopped parsley, offering a visual contrast. A subtle steam rises from the warm dish. The setting is a modern bistro, with natural, even lighting illuminating the food. Beside the bowl, a crisp white cotton napkin and a rustic serving spoon are neatly placed. A small side plate with a slice of crusty artisan bread completes the authentic European dining experience. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, focusing all attention on the inviting stew.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping
Pair with mashed potatoes or egg noodles
Serve with a simple green salad
instructions: Cut beef chuck into 3-4 cm chunks. Pat dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add roughly chopped onions to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute to form a roux.
Gradually pour in red wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add beef broth, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 1.5 hours.
Peel carrots and cut into 2-3 cm thick rounds or large oblique cuts. Add carrots and blueberries to the pot.
Continue simmering, covered, for another 45-60 minutes, or until beef is fork-tender and carrots are soft.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste.
Ladle stew into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef with Blueberry-Onion Jam and Roasted Carrots
recipes.visual_description: The centerpiece is a single, whole piece of pan-seared beef, displaying a rich, deep brown crust and a tender, juicy interior. It is presented intact, not sliced. Adjacent to the beef, a vibrant pile of roasted carrot batons showcases their warm orange color with subtly caramelized edges, indicating their tender texture. A generous, glossy dollop of deep purple blueberry-onion jam rests beside the beef, its rich hue providing a striking contrast. The jam appears thick and slightly chunky. A few fresh thyme leaves are scattered over the beef and jam for a touch of green. The dish is served on a clean, round white porcelain plate, placed on a light wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin is positioned beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the food against a subtly blurred modern bistro background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Peel carrots. Cut into 5cm batons.
Toss carrot batons with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet.
Roast carrots 25-30 minutes until tender and slightly caramelized.
Thinly slice onions. Mince garlic.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add sliced onions. Cook 10-12 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add blueberries, beef broth, balsamic vinegar, and thyme sprigs to the saucepan. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cook 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until liquid reduces and mixture thickens into a jam. Remove thyme sprigs.
Season blueberry-onion jam with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Pat beef dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan or cast iron skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Carefully place beef in hot pan. Sear 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness.
Add butter to the pan during the last minute of cooking. Baste beef with melted butter.
Remove beef from pan. Rest 5 minutes on a cutting board.
Plate. Place roasted carrots on one side of the plate. Spoon blueberry-onion jam beside the beef. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Pasta "Fries" with Cheesy Mustard Dip
recipes.visual_description: Baked Pasta "Fries" are presented casually on a rustic wooden board or a wide, shallow ceramic platter. The pasta pieces, cut into short tubes, are golden-brown and visibly crispy on the exterior, showing the texture of baked panko breadcrumbs. They are piled loosely and naturally in the center, not in a neat stack, suggesting a generous, unpretentious portion for sharing. A small, round, ceramic ramekin holds the warm, creamy cheesy mustard dip, its surface smooth and a rich orange-yellow hue. The dip is placed slightly off-center next to the pasta. A few stray baked pasta pieces might be scattered around the main pile, enhancing the homely, casual feel. The setting is a well-used wooden dining table, possibly with a simple, slightly rumpled cloth napkin or a paper towel casually placed nearby. Lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy kitchen environment. The entire plate or board is visible, with ample negative space around the food, emphasizing its comfort food appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve on a sharing platter for casual, family-style eating.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a large baking tray with parchment paper.
Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. Do not rinse.
In a large bowl, toss drained pasta with olive oil, garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika, 0.5 teaspoon salt, and 0.25 teaspoon black pepper.
Add panko breadcrumbs and grated Parmesan cheese to the pasta. Toss until pasta is evenly coated.
Spread coated pasta in a single layer on the prepared baking tray.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy. Flip pasta halfway through for even browning.
While pasta bakes, prepare the dip. Melt butter in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Whisk in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in milk until smooth. Cook, stirring, until sauce thickens, about 3-5 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in shredded cheddar cheese, Dijon mustard, and whole grain mustard until cheese is melted and sauce is smooth.
Season dip with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve baked pasta "fries" immediately with warm cheesy mustard dip.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Watermelon "Steaks" with Turmeric Feta and Chili-Coriander Dressing
recipes.visual_description: A single seared watermelon "steak," a thick round slice, is centered on a clean white porcelain plate. Its vibrant pink-red flesh shows light caramelization from searing, appearing slightly tenderized yet retaining its form. A generous scattering of pale yellow turmeric-infused feta crumbles tops the watermelon, creating textural contrast. A vibrant green chili-coriander dressing is artfully drizzled over and around the watermelon. Fresh green coriander sprigs and thinly sliced red chili rings garnish the top, adding pops of color. The presentation is fresh, bright, and visually appealing, highlighting the savory watermelon. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface with a neutral cotton napkin beside it, under natural, even lighting.

ingredients.name: Watermelon
ingredients.quantity: 4 thick slices (approx. 2.5 cm / 1 inch thick), seedless

ingredients.name: Fresh coriander
ingredients.quantity: 50 g, roughly chopped, plus extra sprigs for garnish

instructions: Prepare watermelon. Pat watermelon slices very dry with paper towels.
Prepare turmeric feta. In a small bowl, combine crumbled feta with turmeric powder. Mix gently until feta is evenly coated.
Make chili-coriander dressing. In a separate small bowl, whisk together 30 ml olive oil, lime juice, chopped coriander, and half of the thinly sliced chili. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.

Sear watermelon. Heat a large non-stick or cast-iron pan over medium-high heat. Add a splash of olive oil. Once hot, place watermelon slices in the pan. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side, until lightly caramelized and slightly tenderized. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary.
Plate the dish. Place one seared watermelon "steak" on each plate.

Assemble. Generously top each watermelon "steak" with the turmeric feta crumble. Drizzle the chili-coriander dressing over and around the watermelon. Garnish with remaining thinly sliced chili and fresh coriander sprigs. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Herb Fritters
recipes.visual_description: A pile of golden-brown, irregularly shaped Homestyle Herb Fritters is arranged casually on an off-white ceramic plate. Each fritter, about 5-6 cm in diameter, shows a crispy, slightly textured exterior with visible flecks of vibrant green finely chopped parsley and dill. The interior is soft and airy. The fritters are stacked naturally, some touching and overlapping, creating a generous, unpretentious portion. A small, simple ceramic bowl of plain sour cream is placed beside the fritters, with a few fresh dill sprigs scattered loosely around the plate. The scene is set on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen lighting, capturing a lived-in family atmosphere.
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk eggs until light. Add milk.
In a separate bowl, combine flour, baking powder, salt, and pepper.
Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Fold in finely chopped parsley and dill.
Heat vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Oil should be about 2 cm deep.
Spoon batter (about 30 ml per fritter) into hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pan.
Fry for 2-3 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through.
Remove fritters from pan. Place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Serve warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Cod with Apple-Angelica Relish
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, simple white porcelain dinner plate, centered elegantly. A vibrant mound of golden-brown apple-angelica relish forms the base, its finely diced apples and caramelized onions creating a rich, textured foundation. Resting atop the relish is a thick, pan-seared cod fillet, its exterior boasting a beautiful, crisp, golden-brown crust contrasting with the moist, flaky white interior. The fish is presented as a whole piece. Bright green flecks of fresh chopped parsley are sprinkled artfully over the fish and around the relish, adding a fresh burst of color. A lemon wedge sits delicately beside the fish, suggesting a final squeeze of citrus. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The colors are warm and natural, highlighting the golden hues of the relish and the crisp sear of the cod. The table setting is a modern bistro style with a simple wooden surface and a clean cotton napkin.
instructions: Finely dice onions. Dice apples into small cubes. Mince angelica stem very finely.
Heat 15ml olive oil and 15g butter in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add diced onions. Cook slowly for 15-20 minutes until deeply caramelized and tender. Stir occasionally.
Add diced apples and sugar to the pan with onions. Increase heat to medium. Cook for 5-7 minutes until apples soften slightly.
Stir in minced angelica and lemon zest. Pour in vegetable broth. Simmer for 3-5 minutes until liquid reduces slightly and flavors meld. Season relish with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Pat cod fillets dry with paper towels. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter in a separate large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Once butter foams, carefully place cod fillets in the pan. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side, depending on thickness, until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 63°C).
Squeeze fresh lemon juice over cooked cod fillets.
To serve, spoon a generous portion of apple-angelica relish onto each plate. Top with a pan-seared cod fillet. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Tenderloin, Smoked Potato Puree, Mushroom Essence, Parmesan Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly seared, thick beef tenderloin medallion, cooked to a medium-rare, rests prominently on an elegant, round bone china plate with abundant white space. The beef, with its deep brown, crisp crust, is positioned to one side. Adjacent to it, a silky, light beige smoked potato puree forms a refined, organic swoosh, its surface smooth and inviting. A delicate, translucent amber mushroom essence is artfully dotted or trailed near the beef, adding a subtle, deep hue. A crisp, golden-brown Parmesan tuile, irregularly shaped, stands upright or leans gracefully against the potato. A glossy, rich brown roasted onion jus is precisely drizzled, forming a small, lustrous pool beside the beef. The composition is minimalist, sophisticated, and architectural, emphasizing precise execution. The plate sits on a premium white Carrara marble surface, complemented by a precisely folded white linen napkin and elegant modern flatware, bathed in dramatic professional lighting casting soft shadows.

ingredients.name: Russet potatoes, peeled, cut into 3 cm chunks
mixed mushrooms (cremini, shiitake), cleaned, roughly chopped

instructions: Season beef tenderloin generously with salt and pepper. Vacuum seal beef. Cook in a water bath at 54°C for 2 hours. Remove from bag, pat dry thoroughly.

In a medium saucepan, heat 15 ml olive oil over medium heat. Add chopped onion. Caramelize slowly until deep brown, about 20-25 minutes. Add beef stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce by half until thickened slightly, about 30 minutes. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids. Discard solids. Keep jus warm.

Place potato chunks in a saucepan. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook until fork-tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well. Pass potatoes through a ricer or fine-mesh sieve into a bowl. Add warmed milk, chilled butter, and smoked paprika. Whisk vigorously until smooth and creamy. Season with salt. Keep warm.

Heat 5 ml olive oil in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add shallot and garlic. Sauté until fragrant, 2 minutes. Add chopped mushrooms. Cook until softened and browned, 8-10 minutes. Add vegetable stock. Simmer for 15 minutes. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids firmly to extract liquid. Reduce liquid by half over medium heat until intensely flavored. Season with salt. Keep warm.

Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Arrange small piles (approx. 5 cm diameter) of grated Parmesan. Bake for 5-7 minutes, until golden and bubbly. Remove from oven. Let cool on parchment paper until crisp.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed skillet over high heat until shimmering. Carefully place beef tenderloin portions in the skillet. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side until a deep brown crust forms. Remove from pan. Rest for 5 minutes.

On each plate, create an artistic swoosh or quenelle of smoked potato puree. Place one seared beef tenderloin medallion beside it. Drizzle a small amount of mushroom essence around the beef or potato. Carefully place one Parmesan crisp. Finish with a generous drizzle of the warm roasted onion jus. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Hazelnut-Crusted Chicken Thighs with Lemon Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of hazelnut-crusted chicken thigh rests on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The chicken thigh is golden-brown with a visible, crispy hazelnut coating. Roasted potato wedges, cut irregularly, are casually arranged around the chicken, some slightly overlapping. The potatoes are light golden with a tender-crisp texture, showing hints of roasted lemon zest and herbs. A glossy, light brown verjus pan sauce is drizzled over the chicken and potatoes. Fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley and rosemary are sprinkled sparingly over the dish. The plate sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple, casually folded beige linen napkin and standard silver cutlery are placed beside the plate. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a comfortable home setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
Spread blanched hazelnuts on a separate small baking sheet. Toast in preheated oven for 5-7 minutes until lightly golden and fragrant. Watch carefully to prevent burning. Let cool. Coarsely chop.

Wash and cut potatoes into 2cm thick wedges. In a large bowl, toss potato wedges with 30ml olive oil, half the chopped rosemary, all thyme, salt, and pepper. Spread evenly on the prepared large baking sheet.
Bake potatoes for 20 minutes while preparing chicken.

Pat chicken thighs very dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper on all sides. Press the chopped hazelnuts firmly onto the skin side of each chicken thigh, ensuring a good coating.

Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is deep golden brown and crispy. Do not move chicken during searing.

Flip chicken thighs. Carefully transfer skillet to the oven with the potatoes. Roast chicken and potatoes for another 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and potatoes are tender-crisp.
Remove chicken and potatoes from oven. Transfer chicken to a cutting board to rest for 5 minutes. Tent loosely with foil. Keep potatoes warm.

Place the skillet (used for chicken) over medium heat on the stovetop. Add minced garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant. Pour in verjus and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer for 2 minutes until slightly reduced.

Stir in chicken broth. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 5-7 minutes, until sauce thickens slightly. Remove from heat. Stir in butter until melted and emulsified. Stir in lemon juice from half the lemon and lemon zest.

Plate one hazelnut-crusted chicken thigh per person. Arrange roasted lemon potato wedges alongside. Drizzle generously with the verjus pan sauce. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and remaining chopped rosemary. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Berry & Almond Salsa
recipes.visual_description: A single, pan-seared chicken breast, cooked to a golden-brown hue, sits as the centerpiece on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is presented whole or in thick, substantial chunks, showcasing its moist interior and seared crust. A vibrant, colorful mound of fresh berry and almond salsa is artfully placed over and beside the chicken, bursting with the deep reds of raspberries and the rich blues of blueberries, accented by finely diced red onion and bright green mint. Toasted slivered almonds are scattered over the salsa, adding a textural contrast and light brown notes. The plate has appropriate negative space. It rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin, creating a modern bistro setting under natural, even lighting. The focus is entirely on the inviting textures and colors of the dish.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. In a bowl, combine Greek yogurt, lemon juice, minced garlic, smoked paprika, ground cumin, 5g salt, and 2g black pepper. Add chicken breasts. Turn to coat. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours in refrigerator.

While chicken marinates, prepare salsa. Gently combine raspberries, blueberries, finely diced red onion, chopped fresh mint, lime juice, and honey in a medium bowl. Season with a pinch of salt. Set aside.
Toast slivered almonds in a dry pan over medium heat for 3-5 minutes until golden brown and fragrant. Watch carefully to prevent burning. Remove from pan and set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Remove chicken from marinade, letting excess drip off. Discard remaining marinade.

Place chicken breasts in hot skillet. Sear for 6-8 minutes per side, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) and chicken is golden brown and cooked through. Adjust heat as needed to prevent burning.
Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Plate one pan-seared chicken breast per serving. Spoon a generous portion of the berry and almond salsa over and beside each chicken breast. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Marinating time can be adjusted based on desired flavor intensity; longer marination enhances tenderness.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Meatball and Napa Cabbage Soup
recipes.visual_description: A comforting single serving of Pork Meatball and Napa Cabbage Soup is presented in a deep, round ceramic bowl with a subtle, earthy glaze. The clear, savory broth cradles tender, light brown pork meatballs, each approximately 2.5 cm in diameter. Large, vibrant green squares of softened napa cabbage are scattered throughout the soup, some partially submerged, others peeking above the surface. A generous sprinkle of thinly sliced bright green spring onions floats on top, adding a fresh, aromatic garnish. The bowl rests on a well-worn, natural wooden dining table. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks is placed casually beside the bowl, along with a matching ceramic soup spoon resting inside. The scene is bathed in warm, cozy kitchen lighting, creating a homely and inviting atmosphere. The overall presentation is rustic and unpretentious, reflecting a classic home-cooked Chinese meal.
instructions: Finely grate ginger. Mince garlic. Thinly slice spring onions, separating white and green parts.
Combine pork mince, grated ginger, minced garlic, 15 ml soy sauce, 5 ml sesame oil, white pepper, and corn starch in a large bowl. Mix well by hand until just combined.
Form pork mixture into small meatballs, about 2.5 cm in diameter.
Cut napa cabbage into 5 cm squares.
Heat chicken stock in a large pot over medium-high heat. Bring to a simmer.
Carefully add meatballs to the simmering stock. Cook for 8-10 minutes, or until meatballs are no longer pink and cooked through.
Add napa cabbage to the pot. Cook for 5 minutes, or until cabbage softens.
Stir in remaining 15 ml soy sauce and 10 ml sesame oil. Season with salt to taste.
Serve hot. Garnish each bowl with sliced green parts of spring onions.

recipes.recipe_name: Peruvian Corn and White Bean Soup
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant golden-yellow Peruvian Corn and White Bean Soup is presented in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl. The rich, creamy soup base cradles plump, tender whole white beans and bright yellow whole corn kernels. Subtle specks of finely diced red onion and bell pepper are integrated, adding depth. The soup is elegantly garnished with a generous sprinkle of crumbled white queso fresco and a few fresh cilantro sprigs, providing a clean green contrast. A single individual portion is displayed with thoughtful negative space. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a standard soup spoon. Beside it, a small ramekin holds toasted cancha corn for an authentic Peruvian textural accompaniment. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, set against a softly blurred modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of toasted cancha (Peruvian corn nuts)
Accompany with crusty bread for dipping

ingredients.name: White beans, cooked (canned, rinsed and drained)

instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced red onion and red bell pepper. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic, aji amarillo paste, ground cumin, and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add vegetable broth, white beans, and 300 grams of corn kernels to the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat, cover, and cook for 15 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Remove about half of the soup mixture and blend until smooth using an immersion blender or standard blender. Return blended soup to the pot.
Add the remaining 100 grams of corn kernels to the soup.
Stir in evaporated milk. Heat gently without boiling.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and crumbled queso fresco.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork and Potato Stew with Rice
recipes.special_requests: простое, диетическое, вкусное блюдо, которое готовится в мультиварке
recipes.visual_description: A comforting, homely dish presented on a simple, sturdy ceramic plate set on a well-used wooden dining table. The main focus is a generous, natural portion of rich reddish-brown pork and potato stew. The stew features tender, 3-4 cm cubes of pork and 2-3 cm cubes of soft, cooked potatoes, intermingled with diced, translucent onions, all coated in a savory, slightly thick sauce from the tomato paste and broth. Alongside the stew, a neat mound of fluffy, white long-grain rice. The dish is casually garnished with a sprinkle of vibrant green fresh dill and parsley, adding a pop of color and freshness. The overall presentation is unpretentious, inviting, and warm, as if served for a family meal. A simple fork and a folded cloth napkin rest beside the plate. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, enhancing the inviting atmosphere of a lived-in kitchen.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium (approx. 300 g), peeled and cut into 2-3 cm cubes

instructions: Pat pork cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Set multi-cooker to 'Sauté' or 'Fry' mode. Heat vegetable oil.
Add pork to the multi-cooker. Brown pork on all sides for 5-7 minutes. Remove pork and set aside.
Add diced onion to the multi-cooker. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Return browned pork to the multi-cooker. Add potato cubes, broth, and bay leaf.
Stir well. Close the multi-cooker lid.
Set multi-cooker to 'Stew' or 'Meat' mode. Cook for 45-60 minutes, or until pork and potatoes are tender.
While stew cooks, prepare rice. Rinse rice under cold water until water runs clear.
Combine rice with 300 ml water and a pinch of salt in a small pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 15-18 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Fluff with a fork.
Once stew is cooked, carefully remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve hot stew over a portion of fluffy rice. Garnish generously with fresh chopped dill or parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Pork and Potato with Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Braised Pork and Potato with Rice on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The braised pork, cut into rustic 3-4 cm cubes, and 2-3 cm potato chunks are nestled together, coated in a light, savory, clear gravy. Translucent, tender onion pieces are visible throughout. The pork is a natural brownish hue, and the potatoes are golden-yellow, showing soft edges. A separate, fluffy mound of plain white rice sits beside the braise. Freshly chopped green parsley is scattered over the braise, adding a pop of color. The dish is presented on a well-worn, natural wooden dining table. A standard metal fork and spoon are casually placed nearby. Warm, inviting kitchen light illuminates the homely meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of pickled cucumbers
Serve with a simple fresh cabbage salad

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 300 g, peeled and cut into 2-3 cm chunks

instructions: Heat oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add pork cubes. Brown pork on all sides. Remove pork from pot.
Add chopped onion to pot. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Return pork to pot. Add potato chunks, water or broth, salt, pepper, and bay leaf.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until pork is tender.
While pork braises, cook rice according to package directions.
Remove bay leaf from braise before serving.
Serve braised pork and potatoes alongside cooked rice. Garnish with fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Pork and Potato Stew with Rice
recipes.visual_description: A warm, inviting single portion of hearty pork and potato stew is presented on a simple, round ceramic bowl with a slightly chipped rim, reflecting a lived-in feel. The stew, rich with tender, rustic chunks of braised pork and soft, natural cubes of potato, sits atop a bed of fluffy white rice. The stew's gravy is a deep, comforting brown with hints of red from tomato, its surface glistening. Finely chopped fresh parsley is sprinkled casually over the stew, adding a pop of green. The arrangement is natural and unforced, with components touching. The bowl rests on a well-used, warm wooden dining table. A simple metal spoon and a casually folded cloth napkin are placed nearby. Warm, soft kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, enhancing the dish's comforting appeal.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 3 medium, peeled and cut into 2-3 cm cubes

ingredients.name: Fresh parsley
ingredients.quantity: a few sprigs, chopped, for garnish

instructions: Heat oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add pork cubes. Brown pork on all sides. Remove pork from pot. Set aside.
Add chopped onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Return pork to the pot. Add potatoes and bay leaf.
Pour in broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 45-60 minutes. Pork should be tender. Ensure internal temperature of pork reaches 75°C.
While stew simmers, cook rice. Rinse rice under cold water. Combine rice with 300ml water in a small pot. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15-18 minutes. Water should be absorbed.
Remove rice from heat. Let stand covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Season stew with salt and pepper to taste. Remove bay leaf.
Serve hot stew over fluffy rice. Garnish with fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Mexican Pork and Bean Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Hearty Mexican Pork and Bean Stew is served in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl. Diced pork chunks, tender black beans, and soft diced potatoes are suspended in a rich, reddish-brown sauce. Vibrant green bean pieces are interspersed throughout, adding a pop of color and fresh texture. The stew is naturally arranged, with components touching and overlapping. A scoop of fluffy white rice is plated alongside the stew, ready to be mixed. The scene is set on a well-used wooden dining table. An everyday, slightly imperfect ceramic plate, a simple metal spoon, and a casually draped cloth napkin complete the homely setting. Warm, inviting light illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting appeal. A small stack of warm corn tortillas rests nearby.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping.
Offer lime wedges for a fresh squeeze.
Serve with a simple side of chopped cilantro.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 3 medium, peeled and diced into 2 cm cubes

instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add diced pork. Brown pork on all sides. Remove pork from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in chili powder, cumin, and oregano. Cook 30 seconds.
Return pork to pot. Add diced tomatoes, chicken broth, and cocoa powder. Stir well.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook 60 minutes.
Add rinsed black beans and diced potatoes to pot. Stir.
Continue to simmer, covered, for another 20-25 minutes. Pork should be tender. Potatoes should be fork-tender.
Stir in green beans. Cook 5-7 minutes until tender-crisp.
Season stew with salt and black pepper to taste.
While stew simmers, cook white rice according to package directions.
Serve hearty pork and bean stew over cooked white rice.
notes: For extra depth, brown pork well to develop a good fond at the bottom of the pot.
Adjust chili powder to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Ham and Egg Salad Toasts
recipes.visual_description: A single toasted rustic bread slice is centered on a simple, round ceramic plate with a slight natural imperfection. A generous, mounded portion of creamy ham and egg salad rests on the golden-brown toast, with some of the salad gently spilling over the edges. Visible elements of the salad include coarsely chopped white and yellow egg pieces, finely diced pink ham, and tiny flecks of minced onion. A light scattering of vibrant green chopped chives provides a fresh garnish on top of the salad. The plate is placed on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, cozy lighting from a nearby kitchen fixture. A casually placed, folded cloth napkin and a simple glass of water are subtly visible in the background, creating a relaxed, lived-in family dining atmosphere. The entire plate is visible, showcasing an approachable and comforting starter portion.
instructions: Hard boil eggs. Cool eggs completely. Peel eggs.
Chop hard-boiled eggs coarsely. Place in a medium bowl.
Finely dice ham. Add to the bowl with eggs.
Finely mince onion. Add to the bowl.
Add mustard and mayonnaise to the bowl. Mix all ingredients thoroughly.
Season the egg salad mixture with salt and black pepper to taste.
Toast bread slices until golden brown and crisp.
Spoon a generous portion of the ham and egg salad onto each toasted bread slice.
Garnish each toast with fresh chopped chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Cabbage and Barley Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of rustic cabbage and barley soup is presented in a deep, earthy-toned ceramic bowl. The hearty soup features chunky pieces of smoked sausage, tender shredded cabbage, diced carrots, and soft potatoes, all suspended in a rich, savory broth. Cooked pearl barley is visible throughout the liquid, adding texture. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh chopped dill garnishes the top, providing a pop of green against the warm colors of the soup. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, suggesting a cozy, lived-in kitchen environment. A simple, slightly wrinkled linen napkin is casually placed nearby. The lighting is warm and natural, creating an inviting, comforting atmosphere typical of home cooking. A sturdy, everyday metal spoon rests beside the bowl, completing the homely setting. The entire plate is visible, showcasing the natural, unpretentious arrangement of the dish.
instructions: Rinse pearl barley under cold water. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add diced carrots and minced garlic. Cook for another 3 minutes.
Add sliced smoked sausage. Cook until lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes. Stir occasionally.
Add shredded cabbage, diced potatoes, and rinsed barley to the pot. Stir well.
Pour in the broth. Add bay leaf. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 40-50 minutes, or until barley and vegetables are tender.
Remove bay leaf. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped dill.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Ginger-Garlic Chicken with Root Vegetable Puree and Quick-Pickled Radish Greens
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of the dish is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate with a slightly organic, imperfect rim, reflecting natural textures. The plating is minimalistic, showcasing each ingredient's inherent beauty. At the center, a smooth, pale beige root vegetable puree, subtly mounded, provides a clean base. Adjacent to the puree rests a whole, golden-brown seared chicken thigh, its surface exhibiting a slight crispness from cooking. The chicken is presented as a solid, inviting piece. Neatly arranged beside the chicken, a small, vibrant pile of quick-pickled radish greens offers a contrasting pop of deep green, their texture slightly softened and glossy from the pickling process. A fresh, bright green lime wedge is placed alongside the chicken, ready to be squeezed. The overall composition features ample white space around the elements, emphasizing purity and simplicity. The colors are earthy and natural, dominated by the chicken's golden hue, the puree's soft beige, and the greens' deep verdant tones. The plate sits on a light bamboo table surface, its natural grain visible, enhancing the eco-conscious theme. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is casually folded beside the plate. Soft, natural lighting from a nearby window illuminates the scene, creating gentle shadows and highlighting the food's textures. The background is clean and uncluttered, with hints of blurred green foliage from a houseplant, maintaining a connection to nature without distracting from the dish. The presentation is unfussy, focusing on the pure beauty and sustainable origins of each ingredient.

ingredients.name: mixed root vegetables (e.g., parsnips, celeriac, carrots, potatoes), scrubbed, ends trimmed
salt and black pepper to taste (for puree)
fresh parsley or cilantro sprigs (optional garnish)

instructions: Prepare Fermented Ginger-Garlic Paste: Combine ginger, garlic, 5g sea salt, and 30ml filtered water in a blender. Blend until a smooth paste forms. Transfer paste to a clean glass jar. Cover loosely with a lid or cloth. Let stand at room temperature for 1-2 days, or until small bubbles appear and a tangy aroma develops. Stir daily. Refrigerate after fermentation. (If pressed for time, use immediately as a fresh paste.)
Marinate Chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Rub generously with 60g of the fermented ginger-garlic paste. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours.

Prepare Vegetable Stock: Place reserved root vegetable trimmings and other vegetable scraps in a saucepan. Add 500ml water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes. Strain and set aside 200ml stock for puree.
Cook Root Vegetables: Cut scrubbed root vegetables into 2cm chunks. Place in a pot. Cover with water. Bring to a boil. Cook until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well.

Make Root Vegetable Puree: Transfer cooked root vegetables to a blender or food processor. Add 200ml prepared vegetable stock and 30ml olive oil. Blend until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Prepare Quick-Pickled Radish Greens: In a small saucepan, combine 100ml water, white vinegar, 15g sugar, and 3g sea salt. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from heat. Place radish greens in a heatproof bowl. Pour hot pickling liquid over greens. Add lime zest. Let stand for 15-20 minutes until slightly wilted and tangy. Drain before serving.

Cook Chicken: Heat 15ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add marinated chicken thighs. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Reduce heat to medium-low. Cover pan. Cook for another 8-10 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove from pan and let rest for 5 minutes.

Plate: Spoon a generous portion of warm root vegetable puree onto the center of each plate. Place one whole chicken thigh beside the puree. Arrange a small portion of drained quick-pickled radish greens neatly beside the chicken. Garnish with a fresh lime wedge. Serve immediately.
notes: For deeper fermented flavor, the ginger-garlic paste can be fermented for up to 7 days, releasing gases daily.
Utilize all parts of seasonal vegetables. Root vegetable trimmings, leafy greens, and even broccoli stems can be used for vegetable stock.
This recipe emphasizes using seasonal, local ingredients. Adjust root vegetables and greens based on availability in your region.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Garlic-Ginger Chicken with Pickled Radish
recipes.visual_description: A single, individual portion of golden-skinned, pan-seared chicken thigh is centrally placed on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a creamy beige hue. The chicken, cooked to a tender finish, retains its natural whole shape with a visibly crispy, deep golden-brown skin. Thinly sliced, vibrant pink pickled radish rounds are artfully scattered around the chicken, providing a burst of contrasting color and crisp texture. A glistening, light amber pan sauce is subtly drizzled over and around the chicken. Fresh green coriander leaves are sparingly placed as a natural garnish. The plate rests on a light, textured bamboo surface. A natural, undyed linen napkin in beige and a lime wedge are placed beside the plate. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its clean lines and fresh ingredients against a clean, minimalist background.
instructions: Prepare fermented garlic-ginger paste: Finely mince garlic and ginger. Combine with 5g sea salt. Mash into a paste. Place in a small clean jar. Cover loosely. Let sit at room temperature for 24-48 hours. This develops a mild fermented flavor.

Prepare pickled radishes: Thinly slice radishes into rounds. In a small saucepan, combine rice vinegar, water, 10g sugar, and 5g sea salt. Bring to a boil. Stir until sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from heat. Pour hot brine over sliced radishes in a heatproof jar. Let cool. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or overnight.

Marinate chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Rub chicken with 20g of the fermented garlic-ginger paste. Grate zest from one lime over chicken. Squeeze juice from half a lime over chicken. Season with 5g sea salt and black pepper. Marinate for 30 minutes at room temperature, or up to 4 hours refrigerated.

Cook chicken: Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Rest chicken: Remove chicken from oven. Let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

Make pan sauce: Place skillet back on stovetop over medium heat. Add juice from remaining half lime and 50ml water to the pan. Scrape up any browned bits. Simmer for 2 minutes until slightly reduced. Stir in any remaining fermented garlic-ginger paste for extra flavor.
Plate: Place one chicken thigh on each plate. Arrange pickled radish slices around chicken. Drizzle pan sauce over chicken. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and a lime wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato and White Bean Salad with Rosemary-Verjus Dressing
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl, perhaps with a slightly irregular rim, reflecting a handmade feel. The generous portion fills the bowl naturally, with various chopped ingredients casually mixed and mounded. Halved bright red cherry tomatoes, creamy white cannellini beans, vibrant green chopped parsley, small cubes of light green cucumber, and thinly sliced purple-red red onion are visible. A light sheen from the olive oil-verjus dressing coats the ingredients. A few extra sprigs of fresh parsley are scattered on top. The bowl sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple, folded cloth napkin in a muted tone is casually placed. Lighting is soft and warm, from a kitchen window, creating a cozy atmosphere. Individual portions show a good mound of ingredients. Tomatoes are halved, cucumber diced, onion thinly sliced.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the leftover dressing.
instructions: Rinse and drain cannellini beans. Place in a large mixing bowl.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Add to the bowl.
Dice cucumber into small cubes. Add to the bowl.
Thinly slice red onion. Add to the bowl.
Chop parsley. Finely chop rosemary leaves. Add to the bowl.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, verjus, salt, and pepper to make the dressing.
Pour dressing over salad ingredients.
Gently toss to combine all ingredients.
Serve immediately or chill for flavors to meld.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Broccoli with Chili and Savory Glaze
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents roasted broccoli florets, cut into bite-sized pieces, arranged casually on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The broccoli exhibits a vibrant, deep green hue with invitingly charred edges, indicating its tender-crisp texture. Thin, bright red chili slices are scattered over the florets, adding a pop of contrasting color and a hint of heat. A subtle, savory sheen from the chicken stock glaze coats the broccoli. The plate sits on a well-worn, natural wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen light, evoking a homely atmosphere. A simple, silver fork rests beside the plate, and a casually crumpled linen napkin completes the unpretentious, comforting scene. Portions are generous, filling the plate without overcrowding, reflecting a hearty home-cooked starter.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash broccoli. Cut into bite-sized florets. Discard tough stems.
In a large bowl, toss broccoli florets with 60 ml olive oil, salt, and black pepper. Mix well.
Spread broccoli in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Roast for 15-20 minutes. Broccoli should be tender-crisp with slightly charred edges.
While broccoli roasts, prepare the glaze. Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Add minced garlic and thinly sliced chili. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently until liquid reduces by half and slightly thickens. This takes about 5-7 minutes.
Remove roasted broccoli from oven. Transfer to a serving bowl.
Pour the warm chicken stock glaze over the roasted broccoli. Toss gently to coat.
Squeeze lemon juice over the broccoli if desired.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
Serve immediately as a starter.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Supreme, Parmesan-Corn Risotto, Carrot Purée, Charred Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a large, minimalist bone china plate, allowing abundant white space. A fluid, glistening pool of creamy Parmesan-Corn Risotto is elegantly spooned to one side, forming an organic, gentle curve. Adjacent to the risotto, a vibrant, smooth swoosh of orange Carrot Purée is artfully placed. The golden-skinned, pan-seared Chicken Supreme, with its bone intact, rests majestically on the plate, slightly overlapping the risotto. A few perfectly charred, deep green broccoli florets are thoughtfully arranged around the chicken, providing textural contrast and color. The dish is finished with a delicate drizzle of bright green oregano oil, adding an aromatic sheen and a final touch of color. The overall composition is natural, flowing, and highlights precision and restraint.
instructions: Pat chicken supremes dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 20ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken, skin-side down, for 8-10 minutes until deeply golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.

Cut peeled carrots into small rounds. Place in a small saucepan, cover with water. Add a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer until very tender (15-20 minutes). Drain carrots. Transfer to a blender. Add 15g butter. Blend until silky smooth. Add a splash of water if needed for desired consistency. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Blanch broccoli florets in salted boiling water for 2-3 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well. Heat a dry skillet over high heat. Add blanched broccoli. Char lightly for 2-3 minutes, tossing occasionally. Season with salt. Keep warm.

Blanch fresh oregano in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Squeeze out excess water. Combine blanched oregano and 50ml olive oil in a blender. Blend until very smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing to extract all oil. Discard solids. Set oil aside.

In a medium saucepan, heat 15ml olive oil over medium heat. Sauté minced shallots until translucent (3-4 minutes). Add minced garlic; cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add Arborio rice. Toast rice for 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Pour in white wine. Stir until wine is fully absorbed.

Gradually add hot chicken stock, 150ml at a time, stirring constantly. Allow each addition to be almost fully absorbed before adding more. Continue for 18-20 minutes until rice is al dente and creamy.
While risotto cooks, blend fresh corn kernels with 50ml hot chicken stock until smooth. Strain the corn liquid.
Stir strained corn liquid into the risotto during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Remove risotto from heat. Stir in finely grated Parmesan cheese and remaining 45g cold butter until melted and creamy. Season with salt and pepper. Risotto should be fluid, not stiff.

recipes.recipe_name: Butternut Squash and Potato Gnocchi with Sage Butter and Poached Egg
recipes.special_requests: for breakfast, wanna make it healthy, fullful
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a generous portion of golden-brown butternut squash and potato gnocchi, subtly ridged, arranged organically on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The gnocchi pieces are irregular in shape, showcasing their handmade quality. They are coated in a glistening, light brown sage butter sauce, with visible crispy sage leaves and thin slices of garlic interspersed throughout. A perfectly poached egg, with a firm white and a visible soft yolk, rests centrally atop the gnocchi, promising a rich, flowing center. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese adds a delicate finish. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the warm tones of the gnocchi and sauce, creating an inviting, rustic yet refined presentation. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Halve butternut squash. Scoop out seeds. Place cut-side down on baking sheet. Roast 40-50 minutes until very tender.
Meanwhile, boil potato until tender. Peel and rice or mash well.
Scoop roasted squash flesh into a large bowl. Mash well.
Combine mashed squash and riced potato. Add egg, pinch of nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Mix until just combined.
Gradually add whole wheat flour, mixing until a soft, slightly sticky dough forms. Do not overmix.
Lightly flour a clean surface. Divide dough into 4 sections.
Roll each section into a long rope, about 2 cm thick.
Cut ropes into 2 cm pieces. Gently press each piece with a fork or gnocchi board for ridges.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a gentle boil.
Gently drop gnocchi into boiling water in batches. Cook until they float to the surface, about 2-3 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add thin slices of garlic and sage leaves. Cook until butter is fragrant and sage is crisp, about 2-3 minutes.
Add cooked gnocchi to skillet. Toss gently to coat.
For the poached egg, bring a small pot of water to a simmer. Add a splash of vinegar.
Crack egg into a small bowl. Gently slide egg into simmering water. Poach 3-4 minutes until white is set and yolk is runny.
Plate gnocchi. Top with poached egg.
Garnish with fresh black pepper and grated Parmesan cheese, if desired.
notes: For a healthier version, ensure gnocchi is not overcooked and absorbs minimal sauce. The poached egg adds lean protein, making it a fulfilling breakfast.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Pork and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy risotto sits on a rustic, round ceramic plate with a slightly uneven rim, showcasing its homely appeal. The risotto is pale golden, studded with tender, browned 2cm diced pork chunks and earthy, sliced cremini mushrooms. Finely minced green parsley is sprinkled over the top, providing a fresh color contrast. The risotto maintains a fluid, saucy consistency, naturally spreading slightly on the plate. The plate rests on a well-worn light wooden dining table. A simple linen napkin is casually folded beside the plate, alongside a classic silver fork and spoon. The scene is bathed in warm, soft natural light, creating a cozy and inviting family kitchen atmosphere. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a lived-in kitchen with subtle, warm tones.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while hot and creamy
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or deep pan over medium-high heat. Add diced pork. Brown pork on all sides. Remove pork from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until softened and browned, about 5-7 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir for 2 minutes until rice grains are translucent at the edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir constantly until wine is fully absorbed.

Add one ladle of warm broth to the rice. Stir continuously until broth is absorbed. Continue adding broth one ladle at a time, stirring until each addition is absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 18-20 minutes.
Return browned pork to the pot during the last 5 minutes of cooking. Stir well.
Once rice is al dente and creamy, remove from heat. Stir in butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously until creamy. This is called 'mantecatura'.
Stir in half of the fresh parsley.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley.
notes: Stirring the risotto continuously is key to achieving its creamy texture.
Ensure the broth is warm before adding to avoid cooling down the rice.
traditional_techniques: Risotto preparation (gradual broth addition and continuous stirring)
Mantecatura (finishing with butter and cheese for creaminess)

recipes.recipe_name: Aromatic Chicken and Mushroom Broth
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Aromatic Chicken and Mushroom Broth is presented in a clean white porcelain bowl. The clear, golden broth shimmers under natural, even lighting. Tender, cooked chicken breast, diced into uniform 2 cm cubes, is visible within the broth. Sliced cremini mushrooms, displaying their earthy brown tones, are interspersed throughout. Freshly chopped basil leaves are gently stirred into the soup, with a few vibrant green whole basil leaves artfully floated on top as a garnish. The arrangement is natural and uncluttered, showcasing the individual ingredients. The bowl rests on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin to its side. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere, allowing the dish to be the primary focus.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add chicken cubes. Cook until lightly browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Finely dice the yellow onion. Slice the cremini mushrooms.
Add diced onion to the same pot. Sauté until translucent, about 3-4 minutes.
Mince garlic cloves. Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are tender and lightly browned.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 10 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Return cooked chicken to the pot. Heat through for 2 minutes.
Season the soup with salt and black pepper to taste.
Roughly chop fresh basil leaves. Stir most of the basil into the soup just before serving. Reserve some for garnish.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Ginger-Lime Chicken Thighs
recipes.visual_description: A single, generously portioned baked chicken thigh rests on an everyday off-white ceramic plate. The chicken skin is deeply golden-brown and visibly crispy. Roasted potato halves, thick carrot chunks, and soft onion wedges are arranged casually around the chicken, showing their caramelized edges and tender textures. A light drizzle of pan juices coats the bottom of the plate. Freshly chopped bright green parsley is sprinkled over the chicken and vegetables. The plate sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple, slightly imperfect cloth napkin is casually placed beside the plate. A standard metal fork and knife are positioned for a meal. The scene is lit with warm, soft light, evoking a cozy family kitchen setting with minimal background clutter to highlight the hearty, comforting dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Combine minced garlic, grated ginger, lime juice, lime zest, 30 ml olive oil, salt, pepper, and optional honey in a large bowl. Mix well.
Add chicken thighs to the marinade. Turn to coat thoroughly. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours in the refrigerator.
On a large baking tray, toss halved new potatoes, carrot chunks, and onion wedges with remaining 30 ml olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper.
Arrange vegetables in a single layer on one side of the baking tray.
Place marinated chicken thighs, skin-side up, on the other side of the baking tray, ensuring space between pieces.
Bake for 35-45 minutes. Chicken skin should be golden and crispy. Vegetables should be tender.
Insert a meat thermometer into the thickest part of a chicken thigh. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from oven. Let chicken rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Serve chicken thighs with roasted vegetables. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Apple and Blackberry Galette
recipes.visual_description: A single, generously portioned slice of rustic apple and blackberry galette rests on a pristine white round dessert plate. The galette's crust is a warm, golden-brown, artfully folded and pleated at the edges, revealing a flaky, buttery texture. The vibrant fruit filling, a medley of thinly sliced, tender apples and plump, deep purple blackberries, bubbles invitingly with caramelized brown sugar and cinnamon. The apples are arranged in a slight overlap, showcasing their softened form. Beside the galette, a perfectly spherical scoop of creamy vanilla bean ice cream slowly begins to melt, creating a delicate pool. A small sprig of fresh mint provides a contrasting pop of green. The plate is positioned on a natural light wood table, accompanied by a folded cream-colored cotton napkin and a silver dessert fork. Soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors against a subtly blurred, casual bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with a scoop of vanilla bean ice cream.
instructions: Combine flour and salt in a large bowl.
Cut in cold butter with a pastry blender or your fingertips until mixture resembles coarse crumbs with pea-sized pieces of butter.
Gradually add ice water, 15ml at a time, mixing until dough just comes together. Do not overmix.
Gather dough, flatten into a disc, wrap in cling film. Chill for at least 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Peel, core, and thinly slice apples (approx. 3mm thick).
In a separate bowl, combine sliced apples, blackberries, brown sugar, cinnamon, lemon juice, and cornstarch. Toss gently to coat.
On a lightly floured surface, roll chilled dough into a 30cm (12-inch) circle.
Carefully transfer the rolled dough to the prepared baking sheet.
Spoon the fruit mixture onto the center of the dough, leaving a 4-5cm (1.5-2 inch) border around the edge.
Fold the dough edges over the fruit, pleating the dough as you go to form a rustic crust.
In a small bowl, whisk egg yolk with 15ml water to make an egg wash.
Brush the exposed pastry crust with the egg wash. Sprinkle additional brown sugar over the crust.
Bake for 40-50 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the fruit filling is bubbly and tender.
Cool on a wire rack for at least 15 minutes before slicing and serving.
notes: Ensure apples are sliced thinly for even cooking.
Adjust sugar quantity based on the sweetness of your apples and blackberries.
Dough can be made a day ahead and stored in the refrigerator.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato Terrine, Confit Tomato, Apple Fluid Gel
recipes.visual_description: A single, precisely seared rectangular portion of golden-brown potato terrine anchors the plate, its layered texture subtly visible. The terrine is positioned elegantly off-center on a pristine white bone china plate, leaving abundant negative space. Around it, three vibrant, slightly shriveled confit tomato halves, their deep red hues contrasting with the potato's warmth, are artfully placed to create a natural, organic flow. A few delicate dots or a graceful swirl of translucent, pale green apple fluid gel adds a bright, acidic visual counterpoint. The dish is finished with a whisper of fresh green microgreens, precisely placed for color and freshness. The setting features a luxurious grey-veined marble surface, with dramatic professional lighting casting soft shadows, emphasizing the dish's architectural precision and sophisticated minimalism. A crisp white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, rests nearby.

ingredients.name: Granny Smith apple, peeled, cored, diced

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Slice potatoes very thinly, 1mm rounds, ideally with a mandoline.
Lightly brush a small terrine mold or loaf pan (approx. 15x8 cm) with melted butter.
Arrange a single layer of potato slices, slightly overlapping, at the bottom of the mold.
Brush with melted butter, season with salt, pepper, and a few thyme leaves.
Repeat layers until all potatoes are used, pressing down firmly after every few layers.
Cover the mold with parchment paper, then foil.
Bake for 60-75 minutes, or until potatoes are very tender when pierced.
Remove foil and parchment. Place a weight on top. Refrigerate overnight to press and chill.
Carefully unmold the terrine. Cut into 4 equal rectangular portions, approximately 4x6 cm each.
Just before serving, sear each terrine portion in a hot pan with a little butter until golden and crispy on all sides.
Combine cherry tomato halves, olive oil, sliced garlic, thyme sprig, and sea salt in a small oven-safe dish.
Bake at 120°C for 45-60 minutes, or until tomatoes are soft and slightly shriveled but still hold their shape. Let cool slightly in the oil.
Combine diced apple and water in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Cook until apple is very soft, about 10-15 minutes.
Blend the mixture until completely smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve to remove any pulp. Discard pulp.
Return strained liquid to a clean saucepan. Whisk in agar-agar powder and a pinch of salt.
Bring to a boil, whisking constantly, and simmer for 1 minute to activate agar-agar.
Pour into a shallow dish and refrigerate until firm (about 30 minutes).
Once firm, cut the gel into cubes and transfer to a blender. Blend until a smooth, fluid gel consistency is achieved. If too thick, add a few drops of water.
Transfer to a squeeze bottle or piping bag for plating.
Place a seared potato terrine portion slightly off-center on each plate.
Arrange 3-4 confit tomato halves artistically around or on top of the terrine.
Dot or swirl the apple fluid gel elegantly on the plate around the main components.
Garnish sparingly with microgreens or a sprinkle of finely chopped chives.
notes: The potato terrine can be prepared a day in advance for optimal pressing and chilling.
Ensure the apple fluid gel is completely smooth before plating.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Chops with Caramelized Apples and Cinnamon Cream Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared pork chop, thick-cut and bone-in, rests centrally on a clean white round plate. The pork displays a deep golden-brown crust from searing, with a tender interior. Alongside the chop are artfully arranged thick wedges of caramelized apples and delicate, translucent slices of sautéed onion. The apples boast a warm, reddish-brown hue, glistening from caramelization. A rich, creamy cinnamon-infused sauce, light tan in color, is generously drizzled over the pork chop and pools elegantly around the base. A sprig of fresh thyme or sage provides a touch of vibrant green contrast. The plate features balanced negative space, allowing each element to stand out. The setting is a modern bistro, with the plate on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded white linen napkin and polished silver flatware, under natural, even lighting.

ingredients.name: Apples
ingredients.quantity: 2 large, such as Honeycrisp or Fuji

instructions: Pat pork chops dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil and 20g butter in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear pork chops for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove pork chops from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 30g butter to the skillet.
Add apple wedges and sliced onion. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened and lightly caramelized.
Stir in 15g brown sugar and 3g ground cinnamon. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in apple cider vinegar and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits.
In a small bowl, whisk flour into milk until smooth. Gradually whisk milk mixture into the simmering sauce.
Add remaining 15g brown sugar and 2g ground cinnamon to the sauce. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, stirring, until sauce thickens.
Return pork chops to the skillet with the sauce and apple mixture. Spoon sauce over chops.
Simmer for 2-3 minutes to warm through. If desired, transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 5-7 minutes to finish cooking.
Remove from heat. Let pork chops rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh thyme or sage, if using. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Grilled Chicken and Herbed Bulgur with Feta-Cucumber Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of grilled chicken and herbed bulgur is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The bulgur forms a fluffy, light brown base, subtly colored with tomato and flecked with green parsley and mint. Thick, golden-brown grilled chicken pieces, showing distinct char marks, are arranged neatly beside the bulgur. A vibrant mound of diced cucumber and crumbled white feta salad, bright green and white, sits adjacent to the chicken. A warm, lightly toasted pita bread wedge rests on the side of the plate. The dish is garnished with a fresh lemon wedge and a few delicate sprigs of fresh parsley. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface and a clean white cotton napkin placed beside the plate, all under natural, even lighting to highlight the fresh ingredients and balanced composition.
instructions: Cut chicken breast into thick, even pieces. Place in a bowl.
Add 30 ml olive oil, half lemon juice, 2 minced garlic cloves, oregano, salt, and pepper to chicken. Toss to coat. Marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Rinse bulgur under cold water. Drain well.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add finely diced red onion and remaining 2 minced garlic cloves. Sauté until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute.

Add bulgur and vegetable broth. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and bulgur is tender. Fluff with a fork. Stir in half of the chopped parsley and mint.

Dice cucumber into small cubes. In a separate bowl, combine diced cucumber, crumbled feta, remaining lemon juice, red wine vinegar, remaining 15 ml olive oil, and remaining chopped parsley and mint. Season with salt and pepper. Toss gently.
Preheat grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Grill chicken pieces for 4-5 minutes per side, or until cooked through and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Warm pita bread on the grill or in a pan for 1-2 minutes per side.

To plate, spoon a generous portion of herbed bulgur onto a white dinner plate. Arrange grilled chicken pieces beside the bulgur. Place a scoop of the feta-cucumber salad next to the chicken. Garnish with a lemon wedge and a sprinkle of fresh parsley. Serve with warm pita bread on the side.

recipes.recipe_name: Italian Braised Beef with Peppers and Carrots
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Italian braised beef is presented in a deep, rustic white porcelain bowl. The centerpiece is several large, tender chunks of braised beef, deep reddish-brown and glossy from the rich, thick tomato sauce. Nestled around the beef are vibrant pieces of red and yellow bell pepper cut into substantial wedges and thick rounds of bright orange carrots, all coated in the same savory, aromatic sauce. The sauce itself is robust, clinging to the ingredients, with a slight sheen. A sprinkle of freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley adds a pop of bright green to the top, contrasting with the warm, earthy tones of the dish. The bowl sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table. A classic silver fork and knife rest beside the bowl on a folded natural cotton napkin. The background is clean and slightly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro setting with natural, even lighting, highlighting the dish as the focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisan bread, such as ciabatta, for dipping in the sauce.
Can be served over creamy polenta or wide pasta noodles like pappardelle or rigatoni.
instructions: Cut beef into 4-5 cm thick chunks. Pat dry. Season beef generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Dice onion. Add onion to the pot and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Peel and thinly slice garlic. Add sliced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Peel carrots and cut into 1.5-2 cm thick rounds. Cut bell peppers into large wedges. Add carrots and bell peppers to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until slightly tender.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and beef broth. Add rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring mixture to a gentle boil.
Return seared beef chunks to the pot. Ensure beef is mostly submerged in liquid. If not, add a little more broth.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly. Simmer gently for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove bay leaf, rosemary, and thyme sprigs. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste.
Coarsely chop fresh parsley. Ladle braised beef and vegetables into serving bowls. Garnish with chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Grilled Rainbow Trout with Dill and Lemon
recipes.visual_description: A single grilled rainbow trout fillet, skin-on, displaying distinct char marks and a crispy, golden-brown exterior. The flaky, moist flesh is visible where the skin naturally separates. It is presented whole, not sliced. Fresh lemon slices rest atop the fish. Beside the trout, a neat pile of roasted potato wedges, golden-brown with slightly charred edges. A small dollop of creamy white dill sour cream sits on the plate, ready for dipping. The dish is served on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple light wooden table surface, a folded cotton napkin beside the plate, and subtle natural lighting creating a warm ambiance. The background is minimal, suggesting a casual restaurant environment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with additional fresh dill on the side.
Offer a side of rye bread.

ingredients.name: Fresh dill
ingredients.quantity: 2 tbsp, finely chopped, plus extra sprigs for garnish

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.quantity: 1, half sliced into rounds, half for juice

ingredients.name: Small potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 500g (e.g., new potatoes or baby potatoes), cut into wedges

instructions: Pat trout fillets dry with paper towels. Season both sides generously with salt and pepper.
In a small bowl, combine melted butter, 1 tablespoon of chopped dill, and the juice from half a lemon.
Brush trout fillets with half of the dill-lemon butter. Place lemon slices on top of each fillet.
In a separate bowl, toss potato wedges with olive oil, minced garlic, salt, and pepper.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat (approx. 200°C).
Place potato wedges directly on the grill. Grill for 15-20 minutes. Turn occasionally. Cook until tender and charred.
Place trout fillets, skin-side down, on the preheated grill. Grill for 3-4 minutes.
Flip trout carefully. Grill for another 3-4 minutes. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) and flesh flakes easily.
While trout cooks, mix sour cream with the remaining 1 tablespoon of chopped dill. Season the dill sour cream with a pinch of salt.
Transfer grilled trout and potatoes to individual serving plates.
Drizzle any remaining dill-lemon butter over the grilled trout.
Serve immediately with a dollop of the dill sour cream. Garnish with fresh dill sprigs and extra lemon wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rustic chicken cacciatore served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with minor surface imperfections. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are the centerpiece, their skin appearing dark golden and tender from braising. The chicken is partially submerged in a thick, chunky tomato sauce featuring visible pieces of softened translucent onions and whole black olives. A single fresh rosemary sprig is placed casually on top. The bowl sits on a weathered dark wood kitchen table. Beside the bowl is a thick piece of torn crusty bread. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft overhead kitchen lighting, creating a cozy, authentic Italian home-dining atmosphere. A simple linen napkin and a stainless steel fork are placed to the left of the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread to soak up the tomato sauce
Pair with a side of simple polenta or rustic mashed potatoes
Traditional family-style dining involves placing the skillet in the center of the table
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, and the rosemary sprig.
Place chicken back into the skillet, nestled into the sauce.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internally.
Stir in the olives 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs for maximum flavor and protein content
Ensure the sauce reduces until thick to concentrate the savory tomato profile
Always check the thickest part of the chicken for a safe internal temperature of 75°C

recipes.recipe_name: Grilled Rainbow Trout with Lemon and Dill
recipes.visual_description: A single whole grilled rainbow trout, its skin crisped to a golden-brown, lies centrally on a modest, off-white ceramic plate. The flaky, moist flesh is subtly visible where the skin naturally parts. Adjacent to the fish, a generous portion of small, boiled potato chunks, lightly tossed with melted butter and finely chopped fresh dill, forms a comforting side.
