Bright green dill sprigs are casually scattered over both the fish and potatoes, adding a fresh visual accent. Two thick lemon wedges are positioned for squeezing. The arrangement is natural and unpretentious, reflecting home cooking. The colors are warm and inviting: golden-brown fish, pale yellow potatoes, and vibrant green dill. The plate is adequately filled, leaving subtle negative space. It rests on a well-used wooden kitchen table, suggesting a relaxed, homely family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with fresh dill and lemon.
Often accompanied by simple boiled potatoes or a light, fresh cucumber salad.
A dollop of sour cream on the side is a common accompaniment.

ingredients.name: Lemons
ingredients.quantity: 2, one sliced thin, one cut into wedges

ingredients.name: Fresh Dill
ingredients.quantity: 1 large bunch, half chopped, half sprigs

instructions: Rinse trout under cold water. Pat dry thoroughly with paper towels. Score each side of the fish 2-3 times with a sharp knife.
Season the inside and outside of each trout with salt and pepper. Stuff the cavities with thin lemon slices, fresh dill sprigs, and minced garlic.
Brush each trout generously with olive oil.
Preheat a grill to medium-high heat (approx. 200°C).
Grill the trout for 5-7 minutes per side, or until the skin is crispy and golden-brown, and the internal temperature reaches 63°C (145°F). The flesh should flake easily with a fork.
While fish grills, boil potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well.
Toss hot potatoes with butter and chopped fresh dill.
Serve grilled trout immediately with the dill potatoes and extra lemon wedges.
notes: This recipe emphasizes simple, fresh ingredients and straightforward grilling techniques, perfect for a comforting weeknight meal.

recipes.recipe_name: Grilled Rainbow Trout, Pea & Mint Puree, Champagne-Dill Beurre Blanc
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of meticulously plated Grilled Rainbow Trout rests on a pristine white bone china plate. The composition is elegantly minimalist, featuring abundant negative space. A vibrant, verdant green pea and mint puree is artfully smeared in a fluid, organic shape across one side of the plate, providing a rich color contrast. A perfectly grilled rainbow trout fillet, with its skin crisped to a golden-amber and displaying precise char marks, is positioned gracefully atop or beside the puree. The flesh of the trout is a delicate pink-orange. A luminous, pale yellow Champagne-Dill Beurre Blanc is gently pooled around the base of the trout, its creamy texture a subtle counterpoint. A few scattered, delicate microgreens provide a final touch of fresh green. The entire dish is bathed in dramatic, professional lighting, casting soft shadows that enhance its architectural precision. The setting features a luxurious, light grey veined marble surface, a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle, and minimalist background elements, emphasizing the dish as the sole focal point.
instructions: Prepare Pea & Mint Puree: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add green peas. Blanch for 2 minutes. Drain immediately and transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.
In a small saucepan, heat 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add half of the minced shallots and minced garlic. Sauté until fragrant, about 1 minute. Do not brown.

Add blanched peas and mint leaves to a high-speed blender with 50ml water. Add sautéed shallots and garlic. Blend until very smooth. Pass puree through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate silkiness. Season with salt and white pepper. Keep warm.

Prepare Champagne-Dill Beurre Blanc: In a small saucepan, combine remaining minced shallots and Champagne. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce liquid until only 1-2 tablespoons remain. This creates a concentrated reduction.

Remove saucepan from heat. Gradually whisk in cold butter cubes, one at a time. Whisk constantly until each cube is incorporated before adding the next. Sauce should emulsify and thicken. Return briefly to very low heat if needed to maintain warmth, but do not boil. Boiling will break the emulsion.
Stir in chopped fresh dill and 1 tablespoon lemon juice. Season with salt and white pepper. Keep warm, off heat, whisking occasionally.
Prepare Rainbow Trout: Pat trout fillets very dry with paper towels. This ensures crispy skin. Score the skin side of each fillet 2-3 times with a sharp knife. Be careful not to cut into the flesh.
Brush both sides of trout fillets lightly with olive oil. Season generously with sea salt and white pepper.

Preheat a grill or grill pan to medium-high heat. Place trout fillets skin-side down on the grill. Grill for 3-4 minutes, or until skin is crispy and distinct grill marks appear. Do not move fish during this time.
Carefully flip trout fillets. Grill for another 2-3 minutes, or until fish is cooked through and flakes easily. Internal temperature should reach 63°C (145°F). Do not overcook.
To Plate: Spoon a generous, artistic smear of warm pea and mint puree onto one side of each serving plate. Create a natural, organic shape. Do not use a ring mold.
Carefully place one grilled trout fillet, skin-side up, on top of or slightly next to the puree. Position it to showcase the crispy skin and grill marks.
Spoon a delicate pool or drizzle of Champagne-Dill Beurre Blanc around the trout, allowing it to flow naturally on the plate's negative space. Do not drown the fish.
Garnish with a few delicate microgreens if using. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Confit Rainbow Trout with Cauliflower Textures and Hazelnut Brown Butter
recipes.visual_description: The dish is a study in sophisticated minimalism, presented on a round, matte white bone china plate. A generous, organic swirl of velvety, pale ivory cauliflower puree forms the base, its smooth texture contrasting with the other elements. Centered slightly off-kilter atop the puree is a single, beautifully delicate confit rainbow trout fillet. Its skin, lightly crisped and golden, shimmers against the tender, flaky pink flesh. Around the trout, a few precisely placed, small florets of roasted purple cauliflower add subtle color and textural intrigue, their edges lightly caramelized. A glistening drizzle of golden-amber hazelnut brown butter vinaigrette sweeps across the plate, catching the light and connecting the components. A sparse scattering of vibrant green micro-herbs provides a final, precise accent. The plate is surrounded by abundant negative space, emphasizing the clean lines and artistic composition. The setting features a polished grey marble surface, a pristine white linen napkin folded crisply, and a single, elegant piece of modern flatware, under dramatic, focused lighting.

ingredients.name: Rainbow Trout fillets, skin on, pin-boned
Cauliflower, purple or Romanesco, small florets

instructions: Pat trout fillets very dry. Season generously with sea salt and black pepper. Place in a deep, oven-safe dish.
Add garlic, thyme, and bay leaf. Pour olive oil over trout to fully submerge.
Preheat oven to 120°C. Cook trout in oil for 25-30 minutes, or until just cooked through and flaky but still moist. Remove from oven. Let cool slightly in oil.
Carefully remove trout from oil with a slotted spatula. Drain well on paper towels.
Steam or boil white cauliflower florets until very tender. Drain well. Transfer to a high-speed blender.
Add milk, 50g butter, and a pinch of nutmeg. Blend until perfectly smooth and silky. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate smoothness. Keep warm.
Toss purple or Romanesco cauliflower florets with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast in a 200°C oven for 10-15 minutes, until tender-crisp and lightly caramelized.
Melt 80g butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Cook, stirring occasionally, until butter turns golden brown and smells nutty. Immediately remove from heat.
Stir in chopped hazelnuts, lemon juice, and chopped parsley. Season with salt and pepper.
Ladle a generous, flowing pool of cauliflower puree onto the center of each plate. Carefully place one confit trout fillet on top of the puree, slightly off-center.

Artfully scatter a few roasted cauliflower florets around the trout. Drizzle the hazelnut brown butter vinaigrette over the trout and around the plate. Garnish sparingly with microgreens. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Rainbow Trout with Lemon-Dill Butter Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared rainbow trout fillet is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, positioned slightly off-center. The trout skin is golden-brown and crispy, contrasting with the flaky, opaque flesh. Alongside the trout, a neat cluster of golden-brown roasted potato halves or quarters is arranged. Bright green, tender-crisp whole green beans are elegantly placed beside the potatoes. A pale yellow, emulsified lemon-dill butter sauce is generously drizzled over the trout and around the plate, creating a subtle sheen. A vibrant yellow lemon wedge rests near the trout, and a small sprig of fresh green dill garnishes the fish. The scene is set on a simple wooden table, with standard silver flatware and a neatly folded white cotton napkin positioned to the side. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, with a softly blurred, unobtrusive modern bistro background.

ingredients.name: Small potatoes (e.g., new potatoes or fingerlings)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash and halve or quarter the small potatoes. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and golden.
While potatoes roast, bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add green beans. Cook for 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain immediately and plunge into ice water to stop cooking. Drain again.
Pat rainbow trout fillets very dry with paper towels. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Place trout fillets skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 3-4 minutes until skin is crispy and golden.
Flip trout carefully. Cook for another 2-3 minutes, or until fish is opaque and flakes easily. Remove trout from skillet and set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same skillet. Once melted, add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Squeeze juice from one lemon into the butter. Stir in chopped fresh dill. Cook for 30 seconds.

Arrange roasted potatoes and green beans on four white porcelain plates. Place one pan-seared trout fillet next to the vegetables on each plate. Spoon lemon-dill butter sauce generously over the trout and around the plate. Garnish each plate with a fresh lemon wedge and a sprig of fresh dill. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Rainbow Trout Spread
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion of Smoked Rainbow Trout Spread is presented in a rustic, shallow ceramic bowl with natural imperfections. The spread is light pink with visible flakes of trout and specks of green dill. Its texture appears creamy yet slightly chunky, inviting and comforting. The bowl sits slightly off-center on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. Beside the bowl, a small stack of golden-brown, lightly toasted baguette slices and a few plain crackers are casually arranged. A small sprig of fresh dill garnishes the top of the spread. The scene is bathed in warm, soft lighting, typical of a cozy family kitchen. A casually placed, light-colored cloth napkin is visible in the background, adding to the lived-in atmosphere. The entire plate and surrounding elements are visible, showcasing a homely, approachable presentation. The trout is flaked, showcasing its tender, moist consistency.
instructions: Remove skin and bones from smoked trout fillets. Flake the trout meat into a medium bowl.
Add softened cream cheese, sour cream, chopped fresh dill, and lemon juice to the bowl with the flaked trout.
Mix all ingredients until well combined. Do not overmix; a slightly chunky texture is desirable.
Season with salt and black pepper. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed.
Cover the bowl. Chill the spread in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes. This allows flavors to meld.
Serve chilled with a selection of crackers or toasted baguette slices.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Dijon Chicken and Rice
recipes.special_requests: Not dry, chicken breast witout bones and skin, harvard plate
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy Dijon chicken and rice is artfully plated on a clean, round white porcelain 'harvard plate'. The golden-brown seared chicken breast, cut into distinct 2 cm chunks, is nestled within the moist, slightly yellow-hued rice. Vibrant green peas and small, evenly diced orange carrots are visibly dispersed throughout the creamy rice, offering color contrast and texture. A generous sprinkle of freshly chopped bright green parsley garnishes the top, adding a pop of freshness. The dish has a natural, flowing mound, not overly sculpted, showcasing its comforting yet refined quality. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin and polished silver flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred background suggesting a casual, inviting restaurant ambiance.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken cubes until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Dice onion and carrot into small cubes. Add to the same pan. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Mince garlic. Add to pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rice to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes to lightly toast the grains.
Stir in Dijon mustard. Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pan. Add green peas. Stir gently.
Cover the pan and reduce heat to low. Cook for 15-18 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Stir in heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Cook for 2-3 minutes until heated through and the sauce slightly thickens. The rice should be moist and creamy, not dry.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Chop fresh parsley. Garnish each serving generously with fresh parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Mustard Chicken with Vegetable Pilaf
recipes.special_requests: Chicken breast, without skin and bones, without using broth, not dry, harvard plate rule, Canned peas
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Mustard Chicken with Vegetable Pilaf is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A neat mound of fluffy rice pilaf, studded with small, evenly diced bright orange carrots, translucent onion pieces, and vibrant green canned peas, sits on one side of the plate. Beside the pilaf, a pan-seared chicken breast, showcasing a golden-brown crust and suggesting a moist interior, is nestled. The chicken is generously coated with a silky, pale yellow creamy mustard sauce that pools slightly at its base. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped dark green parsley garnishes the chicken and sauce, adding a pop of fresh color. The scene is set on a simple wooden table with natural, even lighting, featuring standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin placed beside the plate, creating a casual bistro atmosphere. The plate is not overcrowded, leaving appropriate negative space.
instructions: Dice carrots into small cubes. Finely dice onions. Mince garlic. Chop fresh parsley.
For the rice pilaf: Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add half the diced onions and half the minced garlic. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add half the diced carrots. Sauté for 2 minutes. Add long-grain rice. Stir for 1-2 minutes until lightly toasted.
Pour in 1.2 litres water. Add 10 g salt. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover the pot. Simmer for 15-18 minutes until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Do not lift lid.
Remove pot from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff rice with a fork. Stir in drained canned green peas just before serving.
For the chicken and sauce: Season chicken breasts generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Place chicken breasts in the hot pan. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
In the same pan, add remaining diced onions, diced carrots, and minced garlic. Sauté over medium heat for 5-7 minutes until vegetables are softened.
Stir in Dijon mustard. Cook for 1 minute, scraping up any browned bits from the pan.
Pour in heavy cream. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Return cooked chicken breasts to the pan. Spoon sauce over the chicken. Simmer for 2 minutes to warm chicken through and coat with sauce.

To plate: Place a portion of vegetable pilaf rice on one side of a white round porcelain plate. Place one chicken breast beside the rice. Spoon creamy mustard sauce generously over the chicken. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato and Vegetable Olivier Salad
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual serving of Russian Potato and Vegetable Olivier Salad is presented on an everyday round ceramic plate with a subtle blue rim, resting on a well-used light wooden kitchen table. The salad is casually mounded, showcasing its diverse diced components: soft white potato cubes, vibrant orange carrot cubes, creamy yellow egg pieces, small pinkish sausage cubes, bright green peas, and translucent green pickled cucumber pieces. The ingredients are uniformly diced and gently mixed, fully coated in a rich, creamy white mayonnaise dressing. A scattering of fresh, finely chopped green dill provides a fresh, aromatic garnish on top. The plate fills the frame adequately, allowing for natural negative space around it. A simple metal fork rests beside the plate. Warm, soft light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a comforting, homely atmosphere. The background is slightly blurred, hinting at a lived-in family kitchen setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled as a side dish or appetizer.
Often enjoyed during festive gatherings or family meals.
Traditionally accompanied by dark rye bread.
instructions: Boil potatoes and carrots in separate pots until tender. Let cool completely.
Hard-boil eggs. Peel and cool.
Remove casing from sausage. Dice cooled potatoes, carrots, eggs, sausage, and pickled cucumbers into small, uniform cubes (about 0.5-1 cm).
In a large bowl, combine diced potatoes, carrots, eggs, sausage, pickled cucumbers, and drained green peas.
Add mayonnaise, salt, and pepper. Gently mix until all ingredients are well coated.
Chill salad for at least 1 hour before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped dill just before serving.
notes: For best flavor, prepare the salad a few hours in advance to allow flavors to meld, and keep it chilled.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Dijon Sauce and Herb Rice
recipes.special_requests: Chicken breast, without skin and bones, without using broth, not dry, harvard plate rule
recipes.visual_description: A single, professional portion of pan-seared chicken with creamy Dijon sauce, herb rice, and glazed vegetables is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, following the Harvard plate rule for balanced composition. The golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast is whole, glistening with a rich, pale yellow creamy Dijon sauce. Beside it, a neat mound of fluffy white long-grain rice is speckled with vibrant green chopped parsley. Adjacent to the rice and chicken, a colorful medley of bright orange glazed carrot batons and vivid green peas adds a fresh contrast. The arrangement is organized yet natural, with moderate negative space highlighting each component. The scene is set on a simple wooden table, featuring a white cotton napkin and classic flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating a modern bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple side salad dressed with vinaigrette
Offer crusty baguette for dipping in the sauce
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through to 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Dice one onion finely. Mince 4 garlic cloves.
In the same skillet, add 15 g butter. Sauté diced onion and minced garlic for 3 minutes until softened. Deglaze the pan with white wine. Scrape up any browned bits.

Stir in Dijon mustard. Cook for 1 minute. Pour in heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Season sauce with salt and pepper. Return chicken to the skillet. Coat chicken with sauce. Keep warm over low heat.
Rinse rice under cold water until water runs clear.
Dice the remaining onion finely. Mince the remaining 4 garlic cloves.
In a large saucepan, melt 15 g butter with 30 ml olive oil over medium heat. Add diced onion and minced garlic. Sauté for 3 minutes until fragrant.

Add rinsed rice to the saucepan. Stir to coat. Pour in 1.6 liters of water. Season with salt. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15-18 minutes, until water is absorbed and rice is tender.
Chop fresh parsley finely. Fluff cooked rice with a fork. Stir in 30 g butter and half of the chopped parsley.
Peel carrots. Cut carrots into 1 cm batons. Blanch carrots in boiling salted water for 3 minutes. Drain well.
In a separate pan, melt 15 g butter over medium heat. Add blanched carrots and green peas. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp and heated through. Season with salt and pepper.
Plate each chicken breast centrally. Spoon creamy Dijon sauce over chicken. Portion herb rice beside chicken. Arrange glazed carrots and green peas alongside. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
This recipe avoids broth by building flavor directly from pan drippings, wine, and cream, resulting in a rich, non-dry dish.
Adjust mustard quantity to your preference for pungency.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato and Haricots Verts Salad with Dijon Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant French-inspired salad is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Sliced boiled waxy potatoes form a structured base. Bright green blanched haricots verts, halved crimson cherry tomatoes, thin purple red onion slivers, and dark Niçoise olives are interspersed, lightly coated in a golden Dijon vinaigrette. Two jammy egg halves, with rich yellow yolks, are prominently placed atop. A scattering of golden-brown, finely crumbled crispy sausage adds savory texture. The dish is garnished with fresh chopped flat-leaf parsley. Plating is balanced with moderate negative space, highlighting fresh ingredients. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting emphasizes the dish's fresh appeal and inviting composition.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crusty baguette to sop up the dressing.
Pair with a light, crisp white wine, such as Sauvignon Blanc or Rosé.

ingredients.name: Savory sausage (e.g., breakfast sausage or mild Italian)

instructions: Wash potatoes thoroughly. Place in a large pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer until tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain. Let cool slightly. Slice potatoes into 1 cm thick rounds or halves, depending on size.
Trim haricots verts. Bring a pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add green beans. Cook for 2-3 minutes until crisp-tender. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.
Bring a small pot of water to a boil. Gently lower eggs into boiling water. Cook for 6-7 minutes for jammy yolks. Transfer to an ice bath. Once cool, carefully peel eggs. Halve each egg lengthwise.

Remove sausage from casing if applicable. Crumble sausage into a cold skillet. Cook over medium heat, breaking it into small pieces, until browned and very crispy. Drain on paper towels to remove excess fat.
In a small bowl, whisk together Dijon mustard, red wine vinegar, salt, and pepper. Slowly drizzle in olive oil while whisking constantly until emulsified.

In a large mixing bowl, combine cooled sliced potatoes, blanched haricots verts, halved cherry tomatoes, thinly sliced red onion, and pitted olives. Pour dressing over salad. Gently toss to coat all ingredients.

Divide salad among four plates. Arrange potato slices and green beans artfully. Place two jammy egg halves on each plate. Sprinkle crispy sausage crumble evenly over the salad. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: For best results, use small, firm waxy potatoes that hold their shape well after cooking.
Ensure the green beans are crisp-tender, not mushy, for optimal texture.

recipes.recipe_name: French Mustard Chicken with Rice and Glazed Vegetables
recipes.special_requests: Chicken breast, without skin and bones, without using broth, not dry
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown with a tender interior, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. It is generously draped with a creamy, pale yellow Dijon mustard sauce, glistening softly. Beside the chicken, a neat mound of fluffy white long-grain rice provides a neutral counterpoint. Vibrant orange carrot rounds and bright green peas are artfully arranged next to the rice, showcasing their natural colors and textures. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped parsley garnishes the chicken and sauce, adding a pop of green. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and classic silverware, creating a refined yet approachable bistro setting under soft, natural lighting.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 5 medium, peeled, cut into 1cm thick rounds

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 30ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken and set aside. Keep warm.
In the same skillet, add remaining 30ml olive oil and butter. Add diced onions and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the pan. Reduce liquid by half.
Whisk in Dijon mustard until smooth. Stir in heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 5-7 minutes, until sauce thickens slightly.
Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste. Return chicken breasts to the skillet, coating them in the sauce. Simmer gently for 2 minutes.

While chicken cooks, prepare rice. Rinse rice thoroughly. Combine rice with 1200ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Fluff with a fork.
In a separate small saucepan, combine carrot rounds with 100ml water and a pinch of salt. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook until tender-crisp, about 7-10 minutes. Drain any excess water.
Add frozen green peas to the carrots. Cook for 2-3 minutes until heated through. Drain any remaining water.
Serve each chicken breast with a generous portion of rice and a side of glazed carrots and peas. Spoon extra mustard cream sauce over the chicken. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet à la Moutarde avec Riz Pilaf aux Légumes
recipes.special_requests: Chicken breast, without skin and bones, without using broth, egg-noodle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of golden-seared chicken breast, halved lengthwise, rests centrally on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, cooked to a tender finish, is generously coated with a creamy, pale yellow Dijon mustard sauce, its richness evident. Adjacent to the chicken is a vibrant mound of fluffy rice pilaf, studded with bright green peas and finely diced orange carrots, their colors contrasting beautifully with the white rice. Each grain of rice is distinct, indicating a perfect pilaf texture. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green parsley provides a final touch of color and freshness. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and polished European flatware, under soft, natural light, creating an inviting casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette
Offer crusty baguette slices to absorb the sauce
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Cook in batches if necessary. Do not overcrowd pan.

Transfer chicken to a plate. Insert a meat thermometer into the thickest part. If internal temperature is below 75°C (167°F), finish cooking in a preheated oven at 180°C until temperature is reached. Set aside.
In the same skillet, add remaining 30 ml olive oil. Add diced onions and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and diced carrots. Cook for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in Dijon mustard and 150 ml water. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Cook for 2 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet, coating them in the mustard sauce. Keep warm over very low heat or in a warm oven.
For the pilaf, rinse rice under cold water until water runs clear. Drain well.
In a separate pot, heat a small amount of oil or butter. Add a quarter of the diced onion and cook until translucent.
Add rinsed rice and stir for 2 minutes to lightly toast.
Pour in 1.2 litres of water. Season with salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed.
Stir in green peas and remaining diced carrots into the cooked rice. Cover and let stand for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Adjust seasoning.

To serve, place a portion of rice pilaf on a plate. Halve a chicken breast lengthwise and place it beside the rice. Spoon generous amount of mustard sauce over chicken. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato, Sausage, and Green Bean Salad
recipes.visual_description: A hearty Warm Potato, Sausage, and Green Bean Salad is presented in a simple, rustic ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden kitchen table. The salad features generous portions of tender, diced 2cm potatoes, vibrant green beans, and savory crumbled sausage. Hard-boiled eggs, quartered lengthwise, are nestled among the vegetables. Thinly sliced red onion adds a pop of color and sharpness. The ingredients are loosely tossed, allowing some dressing to pool slightly at the bottom, indicating its comforting warmth. The colors are natural and inviting: creamy whites of potato and egg, deep greens of beans, and golden browns of sausage. The textures are varied, promising a satisfying bite. The scene is lit with warm, cozy kitchen light, creating an inviting, homely atmosphere. A simple cloth napkin and everyday flatware are casually placed beside the bowl, reinforcing the comfort food aesthetic.
instructions: Place eggs in a saucepan. Cover with cold water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer 10 minutes. Drain. Cool in ice water. Peel and quarter eggs.
Dice potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Place in a large pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook 10-15 minutes until tender. Drain well.
Blanch green beans in boiling salted water for 3-5 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain immediately. Plunge into ice water to stop cooking. Drain well.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add crumbled sausage. Cook, breaking up with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Drain excess fat.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper for the dressing.
In a large bowl, combine warm diced potatoes, green beans, cooked sausage, and thinly sliced red onion. Pour dressing over. Toss gently to coat.
Gently fold in quartered hard-boiled eggs just before serving. Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Mustard Chicken with Rice and Egg Noodles
recipes.special_requests: Chicken breast, without skin and bones, without using broth, egg-noodle
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Creamy Mustard Chicken with Rice and Egg Noodles is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple light wooden table. The dish forms a cohesive mound of golden-brown chicken cubes, each about 2.5 cm, nestled among tender, light-yellow egg noodles and distinct grains of white long-grain rice. Bright orange carrot batons, cut to 1 cm, and vibrant green peas are evenly distributed throughout the creamy, light golden-yellow sauce, which coats all ingredients. A generous sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green parsley provides a final pop of color and freshness on top. The composition is balanced and uncrowded, with moderate negative space. A folded white cotton napkin and standard silver cutlery are neatly arranged beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, highlighting the dish's comforting textures and appealing colors in a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Cut chicken breasts into 2.5 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Cook rice according to package directions. Set aside.
Cook egg noodles according to package directions until al dente. Drain and set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet or pot over medium-high heat.
Add diced chicken cubes. Sear chicken until golden brown on all sides and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Dice onions into small cubes. Mince garlic. Cut carrots into 1 cm batons.
Add onions and carrots to the same skillet. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in Dijon mustard and heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 2-3 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Add frozen green peas to the sauce. Cook for 2 minutes.
Return cooked chicken to the skillet. Stir to coat with sauce.
Add cooked rice and egg noodles to the skillet. Gently toss to combine all ingredients with the sauce.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Sausage and Egg Hash
recipes.visual_description: A hearty individual portion of Sausage and Egg Hash is presented on a simple, well-used ceramic plate with natural imperfections, placed on a warm wooden dining table. The dish features golden-brown, pan-fried potato cubes, roughly diced cooked pork sausage chunks, and tender, sautéed diced red bell pepper and onion. Two perfectly cooked sunny-side-up eggs, with bright yellow yolks and firm white edges, are nestled into the hash. The ingredients are naturally piled in the center of the plate, allowing for adequate negative space. A sprinkle of fresh chopped green parsley adds a touch of color. A standard fork rests beside the plate. Warm, cozy lighting from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, suggesting a relaxed family dining atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with hot sauce on the side.
Serve with toast or biscuits.
instructions: Peel potatoes. Dice potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes. Set aside.
Dice onion and red bell pepper into 1 cm pieces. Mince garlic.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Add sausage. Break up sausage into chunks. Cook until browned and cooked through. Remove sausage from skillet. Drain excess fat, leave 1 tablespoon in skillet.
Add remaining 1 tablespoon oil to skillet if needed. Add potato cubes. Cook, stirring occasionally, until tender and golden brown, about 15-20 minutes.
Add diced onion, bell pepper, and minced garlic to skillet with potatoes. Cook until vegetables soften, about 5-7 minutes.
Return cooked sausage chunks to skillet with vegetables. Stir to combine. Season with salt and black pepper.
Create 4 wells in the hash mixture. Crack one egg into each well.
Cover skillet with a lid or foil. Cook until egg whites are set and yolks are to desired doneness, about 5-8 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Mustard-Glazed Roasted Chicken with Herbed Rice & Noodle Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of golden-brown roasted chicken, a bone-in thigh or leg, rests prominently on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken skin is crisp and glossy from the mustard glaze. Beside it, a neatly mounded portion of herbed rice and noodle pilaf displays fluffy grains of rice and delicate strands of thin noodles, subtly flecked with chopped green parsley. Alongside, a vibrant cluster of glazed carrot batons, roughly 5 cm long, and bright green peas add a pop of color and freshness. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. The dish is set on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and polished silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish.

ingredients.name: Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs or legs

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken pieces dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Prepare mustard glaze: In a bowl, whisk together Dijon mustard, honey, 50ml olive oil, 3 minced garlic cloves, and chopped fresh thyme.
Coat chicken: Place chicken on a baking sheet. Brush chicken liberally with mustard glaze.
Roast chicken: Roast for 35-45 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C and skin is golden brown and crisp. Baste occasionally with pan juices.
Start pilaf: While chicken roasts, heat 30ml olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic and noodles: Add remaining 3 minced garlic cloves and broken egg noodles. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until noodles are lightly golden.
Toast rice: Add basmati rice. Stir and toast for 2 minutes.
Cook pilaf: Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15-18 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender.
Finish pilaf: Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork. Stir in chopped fresh parsley, salt, and pepper to taste.
Cook vegetables: While pilaf rests, heat 15ml olive oil and butter in a large pan over medium heat. Add carrot batons, a pinch of sugar, salt, and pepper. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until tender-crisp.
Add peas: Stir in green peas. Cook for 2-3 minutes until heated through.
Plate: Serve a roasted chicken piece with a generous portion of herbed rice and noodle pilaf. Garnish with glazed carrots and green peas.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Soy Chicken with Caramelized Onion and Parmesan
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spicy Soy Chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Thick chunks of pan-seared chicken, glazed with a rich soy and chili sauce, are piled naturally atop golden, soft caramelized onion slices. The chicken pieces exhibit a reddish-brown hue, flecked with red chili. Melted, bubbly grated Parmesan cheese generously covers the chicken and onions, adding creamy, light yellow contrast. Bright green sliced spring onions and toasted sesame seeds provide a vibrant garnish. The plate rests on a simple wooden table in a modern bistro setting. Elegant chopsticks and a small side bowl are arranged beside the plate. Natural lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich colors and inviting textures. Moderate negative space ensures focus on the food's appealing presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Steamed white rice
Kimchi
Pickled radishes
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 4 cm chunks. Place in a bowl.
Add soy sauce, 1 tsp chili flakes, minced garlic, grated ginger, sesame oil, honey, and rice vinegar to the chicken. Mix well. Marinate for at least 20 minutes, or up to 2 hours in the refrigerator.
Slice onions thinly. Heat 15 ml cooking oil in a large pan over medium-low heat.
Add sliced onions to the pan. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 20-25 minutes until deeply caramelized and very soft. Remove onions from pan and set aside.
Increase heat to medium-high. Add remaining 15 ml cooking oil to the same pan.
Add marinated chicken chunks to the hot pan in a single layer. Do not overcrowd. Cook in batches if necessary.
Sear chicken for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Return all cooked chicken to the pan. Add caramelized onions. Toss to combine and coat the chicken.
Sprinkle grated Parmesan cheese over the chicken and onions. Cover the pan for 1-2 minutes until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Transfer the chicken and onion mixture to serving plates. Garnish generously with sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Garlic Chicken with Cannellini Beans
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly braised, bone-in chicken thigh, its skin golden-brown and slightly crisped, rests as the focal point on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Around the chicken, a generous portion of creamy cannellini beans, diced carrots, diced celery, and diced tomatoes are bathed in a rich, rustic, herb-infused tomato sauce. The sauce is glossy, clinging to the ingredients, showcasing warm red, orange, and creamy white tones. Freshly chopped vibrant green parsley is generously sprinkled over the entire dish, providing a burst of color and freshness. A bright yellow lemon wedge sits neatly on the rim of the plate, ready for squeezing. The overall presentation is inviting and abundant, with moderate negative space. The dish is set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and traditional flatware, under soft, natural lighting, evoking a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread for dipping in the sauce.
A side of simple green salad with vinaigrette.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 8-10 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-5 minutes. Remove chicken.
Add diced onion, diced carrots, and diced celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic, chopped rosemary, and chopped thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth and canned diced tomatoes. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Add bay leaves and return chicken to the pot. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Cover and transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Braise for 45 minutes.
Remove from oven. Stir in rinsed cannellini beans.
Return to oven, uncovered, and continue to braise for another 15-20 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) and sauce has slightly thickened.
Discard bay leaves. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve with lemon wedges.
notes: This dish is naturally gluten-free if no cross-contamination occurs.
Can be made ahead and reheated gently. Flavors deepen overnight.

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet à la Moutarde with Creamy Potato and Cheddar Gratin
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain plate, resting on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A golden-brown, seared chicken thigh sits prominently, coated in a creamy, pale yellow mustard sauce flecked with finely chopped green parsley. Beside the chicken, a generous rectangular portion of golden-crusted potato and cheddar gratin is carefully placed. The gratin features thinly sliced, tender potatoes peeking through the bubbly, caramelized cheese topping. A light drizzle of the mustard sauce from the chicken slightly pools at the base of the chicken, connecting the elements. A folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The composition is balanced and inviting, with warm yellows, whites, and green accents, under natural, even lighting that highlights the textures and colors of the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer crusty baguette slices for dipping into the sauce.
Pair with a dry white wine like Sauvignon Blanc or Chardonnay.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Peel potatoes. Slice thinly, about 2-3mm thick.
Slice half an onion thinly. Mince 2 cloves garlic.
Grease a gratin dish with butter.
Arrange a layer of potato slices in the dish. Season with salt and pepper.
Sprinkle some sliced onion and minced garlic. Add a third of the grated cheddar.
Repeat layering until all potatoes are used, ending with a layer of potato.
Warm 400ml milk in a saucepan. Pour milk over potatoes in the gratin dish.
Top with remaining cheddar cheese.
Bake for 50-60 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and top is golden brown.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown. Cook to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add remaining half onion, diced, to the skillet. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Mince remaining 2 cloves garlic. Add to skillet. Sauté 1 minute.
Whisk flour into the pan drippings and onion mixture. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in remaining 200ml milk until sauce is smooth.
Stir in Dijon mustard. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to the skillet. Coat chicken with sauce.
Transfer skillet to the oven with the gratin, if space allows, or cook on stovetop on low heat, covered, for 10-15 minutes, until chicken is cooked through and tender.
Chop fresh parsley. Stir half into the chicken sauce. Garnish with remaining parsley.
notes: For best results, use a good quality Dijon mustard.
Ensure potatoes are sliced uniformly for even cooking in the gratin.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Garlic Chicken with White Beans
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, wholesome main course presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The dish features tender, golden-brown chicken chunks, each approximately 3-4 cm, nestled among creamy white beans and bright red diced tomatoes. A light, herbed broth-based sauce coats the ingredients, showcasing speckles of green from fresh oregano and thyme. The chicken pieces are irregularly shaped, reflecting a natural, rustic cut. The creamy white beans provide a textural contrast to the tender chicken and the slight acidity of the tomatoes. A generous sprinkling of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley crowns the dish, adding a burst of color and freshness. A bright yellow lemon wedge is placed alongside the dish, offering a visual cue of its citrus notes. The plating is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and classic, polished silverware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's fresh ingredients and appealing textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty whole-grain bread for dipping into the sauce.
Offer a simple green salad dressed with lemon and a touch of olive oil (on the side, not part of the fat-free dish).

ingredients.name: White beans (cannellini or great northern), canned, rinsed

instructions: Cut chicken breasts into 3-4 cm thick chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat a large, non-stick pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add a splash of fat-free chicken broth or water.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add more broth/water if needed to prevent sticking.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Add chicken chunks to the pot. Cook until lightly browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Chicken will not be fully cooked through.
Pour in diced tomatoes (undrained) and fat-free chicken broth. Stir in chopped oregano and thyme.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Stir in rinsed white beans and half of the chopped fresh parsley. Cook for another 5 minutes to heat through the beans.
Remove from heat. Stir in lemon juice. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve hot. Garnish each serving with remaining fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.
To keep it strictly fat-free, avoid adding any oil during cooking or as garnish.

recipes.recipe_name: Apple and Herb Cream Cheese Crostini
recipes.visual_description: A collection of inviting Apple and Herb Cream Cheese Crostini is casually arranged on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. The crostini are golden-brown toasted baguette rounds, each generously spread with a creamy, off-white herb cream cheese. The cream cheese is speckled with vibrant green flecks of finely chopped chives and parsley. Small, crisp cubes of red-skinned apple are scattered on top, adding a fresh contrast. The overall arrangement is unpretentious and natural, with some crostini slightly overlapping, suggesting a relaxed family gathering. A simple, slightly crumpled off-white linen napkin is casually placed beside the platter. The scene is bathed in warm, soft kitchen lighting, highlighting the natural textures and colors of the ingredients. The focus is entirely on the food, presented as a comforting, approachable snack on a rustic ceramic serving platter with natural imperfections. The entire plate is visible, showcasing ample negative space around the food.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Slice baguette into 1.5 cm thick rounds. Arrange on a baking sheet.
Drizzle bread slices with olive oil. Bake for 8-10 minutes until lightly golden and crisp. Remove from oven.
Rub one side of each toasted bread slice with the cut garlic clove for flavor.
In a small bowl, combine softened cream cheese, chopped chives, chopped parsley, salt, and black pepper. Mix well until smooth.
Wash and core the apple. Dice the apple into small, 0.5 cm cubes.
Spread a generous amount of herb cream cheese onto each toasted baguette slice.
Top each crostini with a small spoonful of diced apple. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Sous Vide Chicken Breast, Black Garlic Emulsion, Fermented Chili Oil
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of meticulously plated Sous Vide Chicken Breast on a pristine white bone china plate, resting on a premium white Carrara marble surface. The golden-seared chicken breast is sliced into two thick, angled pieces, revealing its succulent interior. Beside it, a vibrant black garlic emulsion is precisely swiped as an elegant, slightly curved arc, deep charcoal in color. Bright crimson fermented chili oil is artfully drizzled in delicate pools and lines around the chicken and emulsion. A single, irregularly shaped, golden-brown crispy chicken skin tuile shard stands upright, adding architectural height and texture. A few vibrant green micro cilantro leaves are placed with precision for a subtle pop of color. Abundant negative space surrounds the components, emphasizing the minimalist and artistic composition. Professional, dramatic lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the textures and rich colors. A perfectly folded, crisp white linen napkin rests nearby on the marble.

ingredients.name: Fermented Chili Paste (e.g., Gochujang or Calabrian Chili Paste)

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Place chicken breasts in a vacuum-sealable bag. Seal completely.
Cook chicken in a sous vide water bath at 63°C for 90 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from bag. Carefully peel off skin. Reserve skin.
Chill chicken breasts immediately in an ice bath. Once chilled, refrigerate until ready to sear.
For the Crispy Chicken Skin Tuile: Place reserved chicken skin between two sheets of parchment paper. Press with a heavy pan.
Bake skin at 180°C for 15-20 minutes until deeply golden and crisp. Drain on paper towels. Break into irregular shards.
For the Black Garlic Emulsion: Combine black garlic, egg yolk, and lemon juice in a tall container.
Blend with an immersion blender. Slowly drizzle in grapeseed oil until a thick, smooth emulsion forms. Season with salt.
For the Fermented Chili Oil: Combine fermented chili paste, sliced fresh garlic, and extra virgin olive oil in a small saucepan.
Heat gently over low heat for 10 minutes. Do not boil. Let cool completely. Strain if desired, reserving the chili-infused oil.
To serve: Pat chilled chicken breasts dry again. Heat a cast iron pan over medium-high heat with a small amount of grapeseed oil.
Sear chicken breasts for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and heated through. Do not overcook.
Slice each chicken breast into two thick, angled pieces.
Plate: Arrange two chicken pieces on a pristine white plate. Swipe a generous arc of black garlic emulsion beside the chicken.
Drizzle chili oil artfully over and around the chicken. Place a crisp chicken skin tuile shard on the plate.
Garnish with a few micro cilantro leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mixed Vegetable Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Chicken and Mixed Vegetable Stir-fry is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centrally composed. The dish showcases tender, golden-brown chicken chunks, not fanned, interspersed with brightly colored vegetables. Red and yellow bell pepper diamond shapes add pops of color. Thinly sliced carrot rounds and crisp-tender bok choy quarters provide textural contrast. Sliced mushrooms are evenly distributed. The chicken and vegetables are coated in a glossy, savory amber sauce. A scattering of diagonally sliced fresh green onions garnishes the top, adding a final touch of green. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table surface. To the left, a small white rice bowl filled with fluffy steamed jasmine rice and a pair of dark wooden chopsticks rest beside the plate. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro atmosphere with natural, even lighting. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space around the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice
Use chopsticks for eating

ingredients.name: Chicken breast
ingredients.quantity: 600 g, cut into 2 cm bite-sized pieces

ingredients.name: Bell pepper (red or yellow)
ingredients.quantity: 1 large, deseeded, cut into 2 cm diamond shapes

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium, peeled, thinly sliced into rounds

instructions: Prepare chicken: In a bowl, combine chicken pieces with 15 mL soy sauce, 10 mL rice vinegar, 10 g cornstarch, and 5 mL sesame oil. Mix well. Set aside for 15 minutes.
Prepare stir-fry sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together 45 mL soy sauce, 60 mL chicken stock, 15 mL rice vinegar, 5 g sugar, 5 g cornstarch, and 5 mL sesame oil. Set aside.
Heat wok or large skillet over high heat. Add 15 mL cooking oil.
Add marinated chicken to hot wok. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until chicken is cooked through and lightly browned. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from wok and set aside.
Add remaining 15 mL cooking oil to wok. Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add carrots and bell pepper to wok. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until slightly tender-crisp.
Add mushrooms and bok choy to wok. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until bok choy is bright green and slightly wilted.
Return cooked chicken to wok.
Give stir-fry sauce a quick whisk. Pour sauce over ingredients in wok. Stir quickly to coat everything as sauce thickens. Cook for 1 minute until sauce is glossy and thickened.
Remove from heat. Serve immediately over steamed jasmine rice. Garnish with sliced green onions.
notes: Ensure wok or skillet is very hot before adding ingredients for proper stir-frying.
Do not overcrowd the pan; cook chicken in batches if necessary.
Adjust spice level by adding a pinch of chili flakes or a dash of chili oil if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Loin with Apple Potato Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A pan-seared pork loin, sliced into thick, juicy medallions, anchors the white porcelain dinner plate. Each medallion displays a golden-brown crust and moist interior. Beside it, a generous square portion of apple potato gratin rises with a golden, bubbly Gruyère crust, revealing creamy, layered potatoes and tender apple slices. Blistered, vibrant red cherry tomatoes are scattered artfully around the pork and gratin, adding bursts of color. Fresh thyme sprigs provide a final green accent. The dish sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and classic flatware, under soft, natural lighting, creating a modern bistro ambiance.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Peel and thinly slice potatoes and apples. Use a mandoline for even slices.
Lightly grease a gratin dish, approximately 20x20 cm.
Layer potatoes and apples in the dish. Season each layer with salt, pepper, and fresh thyme leaves.
Pour heavy cream over layers. Sprinkle with grated Gruyère.
Bake gratin for 45-55 minutes. Gratin is golden brown and tender.
Pat pork loin dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil and butter in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat.
Sear pork loin on all sides until golden brown. This takes about 8-10 minutes total.
Add whole cherry tomatoes to the pan.
Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast for 15-20 minutes. Internal temperature should reach 75°C.
Remove pork from oven. Rest for 10 minutes on a cutting board.
Slice pork into thick medallions.
Serve pork medallions alongside a portion of apple potato gratin. Garnish with blistered tomatoes and fresh thyme sprigs.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Pork Loin, Pomme Puree, Confit Tomato, Apple Gel
recipes.visual_description: A single, precisely seared pork loin medallion, golden-brown with a delicate crust, rests as the focal point. Adjacent, a lustrous, creamy swirl of bright white pomme purée creates an elegant, organic curve. Scattered artfully around are a few vibrant, slow-roasted cherry tomatoes, their skins slightly shriveled, revealing their concentrated sweetness. Delicately placed dots of a smooth, pale green apple purée provide a subtle contrast. A glistening, deep amber pork jus is spooned sparingly, creating a harmonious pool. The minimalist plating features abundant negative space on a premium white bone china plate, set against a pristine white Carrara marble surface. A single sprig of vibrant microgreens adds a fresh, precise touch. Dramatic, focused lighting casts subtle shadows, enhancing depth and texture.
instructions: Prepare Pork Jus (optional): Roast pork bones and mirepoix at 200°C for 30 minutes. Transfer to a pot. Deglaze roasting pan with red wine; add to pot. Cover bones with chicken stock and 500ml water. Simmer gently 2-3 hours, skimming impurities. Strain through a fine sieve. Reduce liquid over medium heat until thickened to a light coating consistency. Season.

Prepare Pomme Purée: Peel and cut potatoes into uniform 2cm pieces. Place potatoes in a pot, cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Simmer 15-20 minutes until fork-tender. Drain thoroughly. Pass hot potatoes through a ricer or fine sieve into a clean pot. Heat milk in a separate pan until hot. Gradually whisk hot milk into potatoes until smooth. Cut cold butter into cubes. Whisk butter into potato mixture, one cube at a time, until fully incorporated and purée is glossy. Season with salt to taste. Keep warm.

Prepare Confit Cherry Tomatoes: Preheat oven to 130°C. Toss cherry tomatoes, sliced garlic, thyme sprigs, and 30ml olive oil in a small baking dish. Season lightly with salt. Roast 45-60 minutes, until tomatoes are tender and slightly shriveled but not burnt.

Prepare Smooth Apple Purée: Peel, core, and roughly chop green apples. Place chopped apples, 50ml water, and sugar in a small saucepan. Simmer over medium-low heat 15-20 minutes, until apples are very soft. Blend mixture until perfectly smooth. Pass apple purée through a fine mesh sieve. Chill until set to a thick purée consistency.

Cook Pork Loin: Season pork loin medallions generously with salt and pepper. Heat a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat with remaining olive oil. Sear pork medallions 3-4 minutes per side until deeply golden. Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 180°C. Roast 8-10 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 68-70°C. Rest pork on a wire rack 5 minutes. Do not slice for serving.

Plate the Dish: Spoon a generous, organic swirl of pomme purée onto each plate. Place a single, whole seared pork loin medallion next to the purée. Artfully arrange 3-4 confit cherry tomatoes around the pork and purée. Delicately dot small amounts of smooth apple purée onto the plate. Spoon a pool of reduced pork jus beside the pork. Garnish sparingly with microgreens.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Pork Loin with Truffle Potato Pave and Balsamic Jus
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a sophisticated, minimalist composition on a large, pristine white bone china plate. Two thick, perfectly roasted pork loin medallions, exhibiting a golden-brown crust and juicy interior, are naturally arranged slightly off-center. Beside them, a precisely cut rectangular block of golden-edged truffle potato pave stands tall, its layers subtly visible. A rich, glossy, dark amber balsamic jus is artfully spooned around the elements, creating organic lines and pools on the white space. A single, crisp, deep green fried sage leaf rests delicately on the pork, providing a textural and color contrast. The abundant negative space emphasizes the precise execution and premium quality of each component. The setting features a polished light grey marble surface, a folded white linen napkin, and elegant silver flatware, all under dramatic, focused lighting creating soft shadows.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of robust Italian red wine, such as a Barolo or Chianti Classico.
Offer crusty Italian bread to sop up the delicious jus.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Season pork loin with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe pan. Sear pork loin on all sides until deeply golden.
Add crushed garlic and rosemary sprigs to the pan.
Transfer pan to oven. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 68-70°C.
Remove pork from oven. Rest on a cutting board, tented with foil, for 10 minutes. Internal temperature will rise to 75°C.
Peel potatoes. Slice very thinly using a mandoline.
In a saucepan, combine cream, 50g butter, salt, and pepper. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Layer potato slices tightly in a greased 20x10cm baking dish. Grate fresh truffle evenly over each layer.
Pour cream mixture over potatoes. Press down firmly. Cover with foil.
Bake at 180°C for 45-50 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
Remove foil. Bake for 10-15 minutes more until the top is golden brown.
Remove from oven. Place a weight on top of the potato pave for at least 1 hour, or refrigerate overnight for best results.
For the balsamic jus, deglaze the pork roasting pan with stock. Scrape up any browned bits.
Add balsamic vinegar to the pan. Simmer gently.
Reduce the liquid until it thickens to a light syrupy consistency. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Keep warm.
Melt remaining 50g butter in a small pan. Add sage leaves. Fry until crispy. Remove sage leaves and drain on paper towel.
Cut the rested pork loin into thick, even medallions.
Cut the chilled potato pave into precise rectangles for plating.
Arrange 1-2 potato pave rectangles on each plate. Place pork medallions naturally beside the pave.
Spoon balsamic jus artfully around the elements on the plate.
Garnish with crispy sage leaves.
notes: For best results with the potato pave, prepare it the day before and press it overnight in the refrigerator. This allows for clean, precise cuts.
Using fresh black truffle elevates the dish significantly. High-quality truffle oil can be a substitute but use sparingly.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken and Vegetable Traybake
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Roasted Chicken and Vegetable Traybake is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh, roasted to perfection, is placed centrally. Alongside are tender, golden potato wedges, their skins slightly blistered and interiors fluffy. Bright green, slightly charred broccoli florets are nestled amongst the chicken and potatoes, adding a vibrant contrast. The components are arranged casually, touching and slightly overlapping, creating an inviting, homely appearance. A few chopped fresh parsley leaves are scattered over for a touch of freshness. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen lighting, reflecting a relaxed family meal atmosphere. A simple metal fork and knife are placed beside the plate, with a casually folded cloth napkin. The scene is uncluttered, focusing entirely on the comforting, hearty meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Wash potatoes. Cut into 2cm thick wedges. Place in a large bowl.
Wash broccoli. Cut into bite-sized florets. Set aside.
Add 30ml olive oil, 3g salt, 1g black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and smoked paprika to the potatoes. Toss to coat evenly.
Place chicken thighs in the same bowl. Add remaining 30ml olive oil, 2g salt, 1g black pepper, and dried rosemary. Rub seasonings into chicken.
Arrange seasoned chicken thighs and potato wedges in a single layer on a large baking tray. Ensure skin side of chicken is up.
Roast for 25 minutes.
Remove tray from oven. Add broccoli florets to the tray, tossing gently with the pan juices and vegetables.
Return tray to oven. Continue roasting for another 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and vegetables are tender and slightly charred.
Remove from oven. Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Potato & Onion Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Rustic Potato & Onion Skillet sits on a simple, cream-colored ceramic plate with a subtle, rustic rim. Golden-brown potato wedges, some showing crispy, roasted exteriors and soft interiors, are naturally arranged with tender, deeply caramelized onion slices. The potatoes are cut into thick, irregular chunks, and the onions are thinly sliced. Flecks of fresh green parsley are scattered over the dish, adding a pop of color. The arrangement is casual and organic, filling the plate without overcrowding it. The plate rests on a well-used, light-toned wooden dining table. A simple, folded cloth napkin and basic, everyday flatware are casually placed nearby. Warm, inviting light illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in kitchen atmosphere. The background is softly blurred, keeping the focus on the hearty, comforting food.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Peel potatoes. Cut into thick, irregular chunks.
Peel and thinly slice onions.
Mince garlic cloves.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium heat.
Add sliced onions. Cook until softened and caramelized, about 10-12 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add potato chunks, rosemary, thyme, paprika, salt, and pepper to the skillet. Stir to combine.
Pour in vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer.
Cover the skillet. Transfer to the preheated oven.
Bake for 30 minutes.
Uncover the skillet. Continue baking for another 20-25 minutes, until potatoes are tender and liquid has reduced.
Remove from oven. Discard rosemary and thyme sprigs.
Chop fresh parsley. Stir into the skillet or use as garnish.
Serve hot directly from the skillet or individual portions.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Sherry-Thyme Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Chicken with Sherry-Thyme Sauce is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown seared chicken breast, appearing whole and plump, rests slightly off-center. A rich, deep amber sherry-thyme sauce is generously spooned over the chicken, pooling attractively around its base. Beside the chicken, roasted new potato halves, with slightly browned, rustic skins, are neatly arranged. Vibrant, crisp-tender green beans are placed alongside the potatoes. The dish features a balanced palette of warm browns, deep greens, and earthy tones. A fresh sprig of thyme and a sprinkle of chopped fresh parsley garnish the chicken and sauce. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a professional, approachable arrangement with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table, a folded cotton napkin, and standard silverware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add diced shallot to the skillet. Sauté 2 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze skillet with dry sherry. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Reduce liquid by half, about 2 minutes.
Pour in beef stock and add 3 thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken breasts to the skillet. Cover and simmer 10-12 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Keep warm.
Continue to simmer sauce uncovered for 5-7 minutes. Reduce sauce until slightly thickened. Remove thyme sprigs. Stir in butter until melted and glossy. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
While chicken cooks, toss halved new potatoes with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast in a preheated oven at 200°C for 25-30 minutes until tender and golden.
Blanch green beans in boiling salted water for 3-4 minutes until crisp-tender. Drain well.
Plate one chicken breast per person. Spoon generous amount of sherry-thyme sauce over chicken. Arrange roasted potato halves and blanched green beans neatly beside the chicken.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley and remaining fresh thyme sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Lighter Chicken Garlic Alfredo Pasta
recipes.special_requests: for dinner, wanna make it healthy, something like alfredo, do your best
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lighter Chicken Garlic Alfredo Pasta presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden table surface. Whole wheat pasta, coated in a creamy, off-white garlic Alfredo sauce, forms a natural mound. Thick, golden-brown seared chicken breast chunks are nestled on top of the pasta. A generous sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley provides a fresh contrast. The dish exhibits balanced colors and textures: tender chicken, al dente pasta, and a smooth, light sauce. Moderate negative space surrounds the dish. The setting is a modern bistro, with a cotton napkin placed beside the plate and a fork positioned to the right. Natural, even lighting illuminates the food, highlighting its appealing presentation and professional yet approachable quality. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Boil salted water in a pot. Add whole wheat pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. Reserve 30ml pasta water.
Pat chicken breast dry. Season with salt and pepper. Slice chicken breast into 2-3 thick medallions.

Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken medallions. Sear 4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet. Rest on a cutting board.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same skillet. Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 3 minutes, reducing liquid slightly.

Stir in low-fat milk and low-fat Parmesan cheese. Whisk constantly until cheese melts and sauce thickens slightly. If needed, add reserved pasta water for desired consistency. Season sauce with salt and pepper.
Add drained pasta to the skillet with the sauce. Toss to coat evenly.
Slice chicken medallions into smaller, thick chunks if desired.
Transfer pasta to a serving plate. Arrange chicken chunks over the pasta. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Tropical Mango Passion Mini Entremets
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly formed Tropical Mango Passion Mini Entremet sits elegantly centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The entremet, a smooth dome or cylinder approximately 7 cm in diameter, is coated in a vibrant, glossy mirror glaze of sunny yellow-orange, reflecting light beautifully. Its surface is pristine and unblemished, indicating a smooth, even pour. Atop or beside the entremet, a small, artfully arranged cluster of finely diced fresh mango gleams with its natural juicy texture. A delicate scattering of golden-brown toasted coconut flakes adds a subtle textural contrast and warmth. A single, fresh edible flower, such as a purple pansy or yellow viola, provides a pop of complementary color and refined detail. The overall presentation is clean, balanced, and professional, with ample negative space on the plate to highlight the dessert. The setting features a simple wooden table surface and natural, even lighting, creating a modern bistro atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Yellow or orange gel food coloring

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a 20x20 cm baking sheet with parchment paper. Sift almond flour, icing sugar, and all-purpose flour into a bowl.

Lightly whisk egg whites until frothy. Gently fold egg whites into dry ingredients. Fold in melted butter. Spread batter thinly on the prepared baking sheet. Bake for 10-12 minutes, until lightly golden and set. Let cool completely. Using a 4-5 cm round cutter, cut out 4 sponge discs.

For Passion Fruit Gelée: Gently heat passion fruit puree and 20g sugar in a small saucepan until sugar dissolves. Remove from heat. Squeeze excess water from bloomed gelatin and stir into warm puree until dissolved. Pour into 3-4 cm silicone molds or onto a small tray to a thickness of about 0.5 cm. Freeze for at least 2 hours, or until solid.

For Mango Mousse: Gently heat mango puree and 40g sugar in a saucepan until sugar dissolves. Remove from heat. Squeeze excess water from bloomed gelatin and stir into warm puree until dissolved. Let mixture cool to room temperature.
In a separate bowl, whip heavy cream until soft peaks form. Gently fold the cooled mango puree mixture into the whipped cream until fully incorporated. Add lime juice.

Assemble Mini Entremets: Have 4 individual 6-7 cm entremet molds ready. Pipe a layer of mango mousse into the bottom of each mold. Place a frozen passion fruit gelée insert in the center of the mousse.

Cover with more mango mousse, filling the mold completely. Gently press an almond sponge disc onto the top of the mousse, ensuring it's level with the mold's edge. Smooth the top. Freeze entremets for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, until completely solid.

For Neutral Mirror Glaze: Combine water, 150g sugar, and glucose syrup in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then immediately remove from heat. Stir in sweetened condensed milk. Add chopped white chocolate and bloomed, squeezed gelatin sheets. Let sit for 1 minute, then blend with an immersion blender until smooth, avoiding air bubbles. Add food coloring and blend again. Pass the glaze through a fine-mesh sieve. Let the glaze cool to 30-35°C, stirring occasionally.

Place frozen entremets on a wire rack set over a tray. Pour the mirror glaze evenly over each frozen entremet. Let excess glaze drip off. Carefully transfer glazed entremets to individual serving plates.
Garnish each entremet with finely diced fresh mango, toasted coconut flakes, and one edible flower. Serve immediately or refrigerate until ready to serve.

recipes.recipe_name: Chanterelle and Lovage Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of creamy, free-flowing Chanterelle and Lovage Risotto is presented in a shallow white porcelain bowl. The risotto is a rich, warm golden-yellow, flecked with vibrant green specks of fresh lovage and small pieces of sautéed onion and garlic. Nestled on top are several golden-brown, earthy chanterelle mushroom halves and quarters, some lightly caramelized. A light dusting of freshly grated Parmesan cheese graces the surface. The dish exhibits a natural, organic arrangement, avoiding any rigid patterns. It is set on a simple light-colored wooden table, with a silver soup spoon resting on the bowl's rim. A folded white cotton napkin lies beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by natural, even light, creating a clean, inviting restaurant ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while hot.
Traditionally enjoyed as a 'primo piatto' or main course.
Pairs well with a simple green salad and a crisp dry white wine.
instructions: Clean chanterelle mushrooms. Trim tough ends. Halve or quarter larger mushrooms.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil and 20g butter in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or deep skillet over medium heat.
Add finely diced onion. Cook until softened and translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Add chanterelle mushrooms. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened and lightly browned. Remove half of the cooked mushrooms. Set aside for garnish.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir well to coat rice with oil and butter. Toast rice 2 minutes until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir constantly until wine is fully absorbed.
Add hot stock, one ladleful at a time. Stir continuously. Wait for each ladleful to be almost fully absorbed before adding the next.
Continue adding stock and stirring for 18-20 minutes. Risotto should be creamy and al dente.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 40g butter and 80g freshly grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously for 1 minute to create a creamy texture.
Stir in most of the roughly chopped lovage. Season with sea salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately.
notes: Maintain hot stock for consistent cooking.
Constant stirring is essential for creamy risotto texture.
Taste and adjust seasoning frequently during cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Green Papaya and Confit Chicken Salad with Pomelo
recipes.visual_description: The salad is meticulously presented on an elegant bone china plate with a subtle pattern, resting on a premium white Carrara marble surface.
