recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken thigh, skin-on and deeply golden-brown, sits centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Its skin is visibly crispy from the high-heat searing. Beside it, a cluster of three to four irregularly shaped, golden-edged crispy smashed potatoes are artfully arranged, showcasing their rustic texture. A rich, glossy, dark amber onion gravy, with soft caramelized onion strands, generously pools around the chicken and potatoes, creating a visually appealing contrast. The dish is adorned with a scattering of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley, providing a fresh, aromatic lift and color pop. The plating maintains moderate negative space, highlighting the food as the main subject. The scene is set on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded grey cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, with a softly blurred background hinting at a relaxed bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Often served with a simple green salad or steamed seasonal vegetables.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (small, waxy, like Yukon Gold or baby potatoes)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash potatoes. Boil potatoes in salted water until fork-tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well.
Place cooked potatoes on a baking sheet. Using a fork or potato masher, gently smash each potato until flattened but still holding together.
Drizzle smashed potatoes with 30ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Roast in preheated oven for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season chicken generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet.
Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Flip chicken.
Add rosemary, thyme, and minced garlic to the skillet.

Transfer skillet with chicken to the preheated oven. Cook for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Rest on a cutting board, covered loosely with foil.
Reduce heat under skillet to medium. Add sliced onions to the skillet with remaining pan drippings. Cook onions, stirring occasionally, until softened and caramelized, about 10-15 minutes.
Add butter to the skillet. Once melted, stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to create a roux.
Gradually whisk in chicken broth, stirring until gravy thickens and is smooth. Season gravy with salt and pepper to taste. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Plate chicken thighs. Arrange crispy smashed potatoes beside chicken. Spoon generous amount of onion gravy over chicken and potatoes. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Pat chicken thighs very dry before searing to achieve crispy skin. Do not overcrowd the pan.

recipes.recipe_name: Marmite Glazed Beef Short Ribs
recipes.visual_description: A single, substantial portion of tender, dark brown braised beef short rib rests centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. The beef, a whole, succulent chunk, is coated in a rich, glossy, deep amber marmite glaze, reflecting the ambient light. Beside the beef, a generous dollop of creamy, smooth parsnip puree forms a gentle mound, its pale, almost white color contrasting with the deep tones of the meat and sauce. A small cluster of bright green, blanched broccolini florets is arranged neatly next to the puree, adding a vibrant pop of color and fresh texture. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space around the elements. The plate sits on a simple, light wooden table surface. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors, creating an inviting, professional bistro aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with traditional root vegetable purees or mashed potatoes.
Accompanied by a robust ale or red wine.

ingredients.name: Parsnip puree or mashed potatoes, for serving

instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Pat beef ribs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef ribs on all sides until deeply browned. Remove ribs from pot.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Cook until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in beef stock, marmite, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves. Bring to a boil.
Return seared beef ribs to the pot. Ensure ribs are mostly submerged. Add more stock if needed.
Cover the pot. Transfer to the preheated oven.
Braise for 3 to 3.5 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove ribs from pot. Strain braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a saucepan. Discard solids.
Skim fat from the surface of the strained liquid.
Bring sauce to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce until slightly thickened and glossy. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve beef ribs with the reduced marmite glaze, alongside parsnip puree or mashed potatoes and blanched broccolini.
notes: Slow braising ensures exceptionally tender beef.
The marmite adds a unique, savory depth (umami) to the glaze.

recipes.recipe_name: Sourdough Berry Tartlets
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine delicate miniature tartlets are meticulously arranged on a light, reclaimed wood board. Each tartlet features a rustic, golden-brown sourdough discard crust, approximately 6 cm in diameter. The crusts are filled with a generous swirl of pristine white, lightly sweetened whipped cream. Vibrant, plump fresh blackberries and raspberries are carefully placed atop the cream, showcasing their natural colors and irregular shapes. Some berries are whole, others may be halved to reveal their juicy interiors. The natural deep purples and reds of the berries contrast beautifully with the creamy white and earthy crust. The arrangement is clean and minimalistic, with ample negative space between each tartlet, emphasizing their individual beauty. A single undyed linen napkin in natural beige is subtly placed to the side. The scene is bathed in soft, natural lighting, highlighting the textures of the wood, the smoothness of the cream, and the juiciness of the fruit, creating an eco-conscious and inviting presentation.
instructions: Combine flour, sugar, salt in a bowl. Cut in cold butter until pea-sized crumbs form. Add sourdough discard. Mix until dough just comes together. Add ice water if dry.
Form dough into a disc. Wrap in cling film. Refrigerate 30 minutes.

Roll dough on a lightly floured surface to 3mm thickness. Cut out circles using a cutter larger than tartlet molds. Press dough into miniature tartlet molds (approx. 5-6 cm diameter). Prick bottoms with a fork.

Line tartlet shells with parchment paper. Fill with pie weights or dried beans. Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 10-12 minutes. Remove weights and parchment. Bake 5-7 more minutes until golden. Cool completely on a wire rack.
In a cold bowl, whip cold heavy cream, powdered sugar, and vanilla extract until medium-stiff peaks form. Do not over-whip.
Gently wash and dry blackberries and raspberries. If desired, halve some berries.
Spoon or pipe whipped cream into cooled tartlet shells. Arrange fresh blackberries and raspberries decoratively on top of the cream. Garnish with a small mint leaf.
Serve immediately on a platter.
notes: This recipe utilizes sourdough discard, promoting zero-waste in baking. Focus on using seasonal, fresh berries for best flavor and sustainability.
For an added layer of flavor, a small portion of berries can be lightly macerated with a touch of sugar for 15-20 minutes before assembling.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Cheddar Macaroni with Crispy Bacon
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Creamy Cheddar Macaroni is presented in a clean, shallow white porcelain bowl. The macaroni, coated in a rich, golden-orange cheddar cheese sauce, fills the bowl. The sauce is creamy and glossy, clinging to each elbow macaroni piece. Scattered generously over the top are irregular, crisp pieces of golden-brown bacon lardons, providing a textural contrast. Bright green, finely chopped chives are sprinkled over the bacon and sauce, adding a fresh color pop. The dish exhibits a warm, inviting glow. The background is a simple wooden table surface, with a folded white cotton napkin placed to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's comforting appeal. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a well-portioned, professional yet approachable presentation.
instructions: Cook macaroni according to package directions. Cook until al dente. Drain well. Set aside.

Cut bacon into 1 cm lardons. Cook bacon in a large saucepan over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Place on paper towels to drain. Reserve 1 tablespoon bacon fat in the pan.
Melt butter in the same saucepan over medium heat. Add flour. Whisk constantly for 2 minutes to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in warm milk until smooth. Cook, stirring, until sauce thickens, about 5-7 minutes. Do not boil.
Remove saucepan from heat. Add grated cheddar cheese. Stir until cheese is fully melted and sauce is smooth. Season with nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Add cooked macaroni to the cheese sauce. Stir to coat evenly.
Serve hot. Garnish each portion with crispy bacon lardons and fresh chopped chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Corn Financier Bites
recipes.visual_description: A pristine light bamboo cutting board serves as the base. Arranged on it are 6-8 perfectly uniform, golden-hued Fermented Corn Financier Bites. Each miniature cake, approximately 4cm in diameter, has a slightly domed top and a subtle texture from the cornmeal, with visible specks of sweet corn kernels. They are baked to a light golden brown. Each financier is topped with a glistening, deep ruby-red dollop of fermented berry preserve, showcasing natural fruit pulp and a jam-like consistency. The bites are spaced evenly, allowing ample negative space around each piece. The presentation is clean and minimalistic, emphasizing the natural colors and textures. A natural beige undyed linen napkin is subtly placed to the side. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the delicate crumb and the vibrant preserve. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of natural wood or stone texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve at room temperature.
Offer with a light, unsweetened herbal tea.
Present on a reclaimed wood board or handcrafted ceramic platter.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a mini financier or mini muffin pan.
In a bowl, whisk together cornmeal, all-purpose flour, almond flour, brown sugar, baking powder, and salt.
In a separate bowl, combine plant-based milk, neutral oil, and vanilla extract.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Gently fold in sweet corn kernels.
Fill each mold cavity 2/3 full.
Bake 12-15 minutes, or until golden brown and a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool financiers in the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
Top each cooled financier bite with a small dollop of fermented berry preserve.
notes: This recipe prioritizes sustainable, plant-forward ingredients and utilizes corn in a sweet application, aligning with the requested dish type of delicate miniature sweets and eco-conscious preparation.
The use of fermented berry preserve incorporates preservation techniques and natural sweetness.
Adjust sugar level to your preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Berry & Ricotta Sourdough Bites
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist presentation of 6-9 individual Fermented Berry & Ricotta Sourdough Bites arranged neatly on a smooth, light beige handcrafted ceramic serving platter. Each bite features a small, perfectly toasted sourdough cube, golden-brown and crisp. On top, a generous dollop of whipped, creamy white ricotta. A vibrant spoonful of deep ruby-red fermented berries, glistening slightly, is placed atop the ricotta. A very fine, almost imperceptible sprinkle of dark, crispy ham dust provides a subtle savory counterpoint. The composition emphasizes natural textures and colors, with ample white space between each piece, showcasing the purity of ingredients. A few small, fresh mint leaves are strategically placed for a pop of green, adhering to natural garnishes. The setting features a light, natural wood table surface, an undyed linen napkin in a complementary beige tone, and soft, diffused natural lighting.
instructions: Prepare fermented berries: Combine mixed berries with 2 tablespoons of maple syrup in a clean jar. Stir gently. Cover loosely. Let sit at room temperature for 1-2 days until lightly bubbly and tangy. Refrigerate.

Prepare crispy ham: Preheat oven to 180°C. Arrange thinly sliced ham on a baking sheet. Bake for 10-15 minutes until very crispy and browned. Let cool completely. Crush or finely chop into a very fine dust.
Prepare toasted sourdough: Cut sourdough bread into 2 cm cubes. Toast in a dry pan over medium heat or in the oven until golden brown and crisp on all sides. Let cool.
Prepare ricotta cream: In a bowl, combine ricotta, remaining maple syrup, lemon zest, and a pinch of salt. Gently fold in the heavy cream until just combined and creamy. Do not overmix.

Assemble bites: Place a toasted sourdough cube on the serving platter. Top each cube with a dollop of ricotta cream. Spoon a small amount of fermented berries over the ricotta. Finish with a very light sprinkle of crispy ham dust.
Garnish: Add a tiny fresh mint leaf to each bite. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Sicilian Rigatoni with Pistachio Pesto and Sausage
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of ridged rigatoni pasta, coated in a vibrant, rich green pistachio pesto, is piled naturally in a rustic, shallow ceramic bowl. Irregularly shaped, crumbled and browned Italian sausage pieces are generously mixed throughout, visible among the pasta. The pesto adheres well to the ridged pasta, creating a rich, cohesive look. A scattering of coarsely chopped, bright green pistachios and finely grated Pecorino Romano cheese garnishes the top. A few fresh basil leaves are casually placed. The dish showcases warm, earthy tones from the pasta and sausage, contrasting with the bright green pesto. The texture is hearty and inviting. The bowl sits on a well-worn wooden kitchen table, next to a simple, traditional silver fork. Soft, warm kitchen light illuminates the scene, evoking a comforting Sicilian family dinner.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for soaking up the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Enjoy with a glass of robust Sicilian red wine.
instructions: Prepare Pistachio Pesto: In a food processor, combine pistachios, garlic, and basil. Pulse until finely chopped. Add grated Pecorino Romano and 100 ml of olive oil. Process until a thick, somewhat chunky pesto forms. Season with salt and pepper. Add 20 ml more olive oil if needed for desired consistency. Set aside.
Cook Sausage: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add sausage meat, breaking it up with a spoon. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes. Drain excess fat. Set aside.
Cook Pasta: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add rigatoni. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120 ml of pasta cooking water before draining.

Combine: Return cooked pasta to the pot. Add the pistachio pesto and cooked sausage. Add reserved pasta cooking water, 60 ml at a time, stirring until the pasta is well coated and the sauce reaches desired consistency. Stir in red pepper flakes if using.
Serve: Divide pasta among four bowls. Garnish each serving with extra grated Pecorino Romano and a drizzle of olive oil. Serve immediately.
notes: For a smoother pesto, blanch pistachios for 1 minute, then remove skins before processing.
Adjust pesto consistency by adding more olive oil or pasta water.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Pistachio Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A modest, comforting single serving of creamy pistachio pasta rests on an everyday ceramic plate. The pasta, perhaps rigatoni, is generously coated in a light green, velvety sauce, showing its creamy texture. Some pasta pieces are slightly overlapping, creating a natural, unforced arrangement. Sprinkled over the pasta are roughly chopped, toasted pistachios, adding a contrasting texture and a deeper green hue. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese is visible, along with a few small, fresh green parsley leaves. The colors are natural and inviting: creamy light green from the sauce, flecks of darker green from the pistachios and herbs, and hints of pale yellow from the pasta and cheese. The plate is placed on a well-used wooden dining table, revealing its natural grain. A simple, plain cloth napkin is casually folded beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by warm, cozy light from kitchen fixtures, suggesting a relaxed family meal.
instructions: Boil water for pasta. Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 200ml pasta water.
While pasta cooks, prepare pistachios. Toast 50g pistachios lightly in a dry pan. Roughly chop for garnish.
Finely chop remaining 100g pistachios.
Finely chop garlic and shallot.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Sauté shallot until soft, about 3 minutes. Add garlic and sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add finely chopped pistachios to the pan. Sauté for 2-3 minutes, stirring, until lightly toasted.
Pour in heavy cream and 100ml vegetable broth or reserved pasta water. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Stir in grated Parmesan cheese. Cook, stirring, until sauce thickens slightly. If too thick, add more reserved pasta water.
Drain cooked pasta. Add pasta to the pan with the sauce. Toss well to coat.
Season with salt, black pepper, and lemon zest. Stir to combine.
Serve immediately. Garnish with chopped toasted pistachios, extra Parmesan, and fresh parsley or basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Italian Sausage and Pistachio Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A modest, comforting portion of Italian Sausage and Pistachio Pasta is presented on a simple, slightly off-white ceramic plate. The rigatoni pasta, cooked al dente, is generously coated in a rich, rustic tomato-based sauce, flecked with browned, crumbled Italian sausage. The sausage pieces are irregularly shaped, showcasing their hearty texture. Sprinkled throughout and over the top are roughly chopped pistachios, providing a vibrant green contrast and textural crunch. A light dusting of grated Parmesan cheese melts subtly into the warm dish. Fresh, flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped, is scattered over for a touch of freshness. The overall color palette is warm and inviting, with reds, browns, and greens. The plate sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table, illuminated by soft, natural kitchen light. A simple linen napkin and a fork rest casually beside the plate, emphasizing a relaxed, family meal setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra grated Parmesan cheese on the side.
Accompany with a simple green salad.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.

ingredients.name: Italian sausage (mild or hot, casing removed)

instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add rigatoni pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta. Reserve 100ml of pasta cooking water.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add Italian sausage, casing removed. Break sausage into small, irregular chunks with a spoon. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove sausage from pan. Set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the pan. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring the sauce to a simmer. Cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly. Season with salt and black pepper.
While sauce simmers, roughly chop the pistachios.
Add cooked sausage back to the pan with the sauce. Stir to combine.
Add cooked pasta to the sauce. Add grated Parmesan cheese. Add reserved pasta water as needed to achieve a saucy consistency. Toss well to coat all ingredients.
Stir in most of the chopped pistachios and fresh parsley.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining pistachios and fresh parsley. Offer extra Parmesan cheese at the table.
notes: Adjust red pepper flakes to your preferred spice level.
Use good quality Italian sausage for best flavor.
The reserved pasta water helps emulsify the sauce and pasta.

recipes.recipe_name: Pistachio Pesto Pasta with Blistered Cherry Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of spaghetti tossed in vibrant green pistachio pesto, arranged naturally on a simple, round ceramic plate. The pasta is loosely twirled, allowing some strands to fall casually. Scattered generously over and around the pasta are blistered, bright red cherry tomatoes, some slightly collapsed from heat, revealing their juicy interiors. A light drizzle of olive oil coats the dish, adding a subtle sheen. The green of the pesto is deep and rich, contrasting with the warm red of the tomatoes and the pale yellow of the pasta. A few whole basil leaves are casually placed on top as a fresh garnish. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen light. A simple metal fork rests beside the plate, and a casually folded cloth napkin is nearby. The background is a soft blur of a lived-in kitchen, suggesting a comforting home meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to sop up any remaining pesto.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook spaghetti according to package directions until al dente.
While pasta cooks, prepare the pistachio pesto. In a food processor, combine pistachios, basil, peeled garlic cloves, and grated Parmesan. Pulse until coarsely chopped.
Slowly drizzle in 100ml of olive oil while processing until a smooth pesto forms. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Set aside.
Heat the remaining 20ml of olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add whole cherry tomatoes to the hot skillet.
Cook tomatoes for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they begin to blister and burst. Remove from heat.
Drain the cooked spaghetti, reserving about 120ml of pasta water.
Add the drained spaghetti directly to the skillet with the blistered cherry tomatoes. Add the pistachio pesto.
Toss everything together, adding reserved pasta water a little at a time, until the pasta is well coated and sauce reaches desired consistency.
Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust pesto consistency with more olive oil or pasta water as needed.
For a richer flavor, toast the pistachios lightly before making the pesto.

recipes.recipe_name: Pasta con Gamberi, Zucchine e Pistacchio
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pasta, perhaps paccheri, is elegantly arranged on a clean white porcelain plate. Tender, light green zucchini half-moons and plump, perfectly cooked pink-orange shrimp are intertwined with the pasta. A delicate, emulsified sauce lightly coats all ingredients, reflecting the pasta's al dente texture. Vibrant green, roughly chopped pistachios are scattered generously, offering a pleasing textural contrast. Fresh, finely chopped parsley provides a final burst of color and aroma. The plating is organized yet natural, with ample negative space. The dish rests on a simple wooden table, complemented by traditional flatware and a crisp white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, capturing the fresh ingredients and inviting textures. A subtle, blurred background suggests a relaxed bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with a glass of crisp, dry Sicilian white wine, such as an Inzolia or Grillo.

ingredients.name: Fresh medium shrimp, peeled and deveined

instructions: Bring a large pot of generously salted water to a rolling boil for the pasta.
Toast pistachios in a dry pan over medium heat for 3-4 minutes until fragrant. Let cool. Roughly chop half of the pistachios. Finely chop the remaining half for garnish.
Wash zucchini. Trim ends. Cut zucchini into uniform half-moon slices.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet or wide pan over medium heat. Add minced garlic and chili flakes (if using). Sauté until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add zucchini slices to the pan. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until tender-crisp. Do not overcook.
Add shrimp to the pan. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring occasionally, until shrimp begin to turn pink.
Pour in white wine. Increase heat to medium-high. Bring to a simmer. Cook until wine reduces slightly, about 2 minutes.
Cook pasta in the boiling salted water according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 150ml of the pasta cooking water before draining.
Drain pasta. Add directly to the skillet with the shrimp and zucchini mixture.

Add the roughly chopped pistachios and most of the fresh parsley to the skillet. Toss vigorously to combine all ingredients and emulsify the sauce. Add reserved pasta water gradually as needed to achieve a light, cohesive sauce that coats the pasta.
Season with sea salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately, garnished with the finely chopped pistachios and remaining fresh parsley.
notes: In traditional Italian cuisine, especially with seafood, some purists avoid adding cheese. You may omit Pecorino or Parmigiano Reggiano if you prefer a strictly traditional approach with this dish.
traditional_techniques: Mantecare (tossing pasta with sauce to create a creamy emulsion)

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Leche (Mexican Rice Pudding)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy Arroz con Leche is presented in a rustic, earth-toned ceramic bowl with a slightly chipped rim, reflecting a well-loved kitchen. The rice pudding, cooked to a fluid, tender consistency, is a natural off-white, speckled with tiny, soft rice grains. A generous dusting of warm brown ground cinnamon creates a gentle swirl on top, providing visual contrast. The pudding fills about two-thirds of the bowl, leaving comfortable negative space around the edges. A simple metal spoon with a slightly worn handle rests beside the bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The setting is a homely family kitchen with soft, warm light from an overhead fixture, casting gentle shadows. A casually placed, folded beige linen napkin sits nearby. The overall impression is one of comforting simplicity and homemade warmth.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm or chilled.
Garnish with ground cinnamon.
Can be served with a sprinkle of raisins or grated lime zest.
instructions: Rinse rice under cold water. Drain well.
Combine rice and water in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover. Simmer 10 minutes, or until water is absorbed.
Add milk, sugar, cinnamon sticks, and salt to the saucepan. Stir.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat. Do not boil vigorously.
Cook, stirring frequently, for 25-35 minutes. Rice should be tender. Pudding should thicken.
Remove cinnamon sticks. Stir in vanilla extract.
Serve warm or chilled.
notes: Stir frequently to prevent sticking and ensure creaminess.
Adjust sugar to desired sweetness.
Pudding will thicken further as it cools.

recipes.recipe_name: Halloumi Saganaki with Salted Lemon Drizzle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of golden-brown, pan-fried Halloumi cheese is elegantly presented on a round, clean white porcelain plate. The Halloumi is cut into thick, rectangular batons, seared to a beautiful crisp exterior with a soft, warm interior. A generous, glistening drizzle of amber honey infused with finely minced salted lemon and vibrant green chopped fresh oregano coats the cheese. The Halloumi batons are arranged organically, slightly overlapping in the center of the plate, creating a balanced, inviting mound. A sprinkle of fresh green parsley adds a final pop of color. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, a folded white cotton napkin placed beside the plate, and a small, rustic ceramic bowl containing a few plump Kalamata olives. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich textures and warm colors against a softly blurred, casual bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm crusty bread for dipping.
Can be part of a larger mezze platter.
instructions: Finely mince the salted lemon half. Remove any seeds.
Combine minced salted lemon, honey, and chopped fresh oregano in a small bowl. Stir well to create the drizzle.
Cut the Halloumi block into 1.5 cm thick rectangular batons.
Heat olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Place Halloumi batons in the hot pan. Do not overcrowd the pan. Fry for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and crisp.
Remove Halloumi from pan. Arrange seared Halloumi batons neatly on a serving plate.
Spoon the salted lemon-honey mixture evenly over the Halloumi.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley and a pinch of black pepper.
Serve immediately.
traditional_techniques: Saganaki (pan-frying cheese until crisp and golden)

recipes.recipe_name: Chipotle Garlic Chicken with Roasted Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chipotle Garlic Chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Two golden-brown, seared chicken thighs, cooked whole, are positioned centrally. They exhibit a rich, caramelized crust from the chipotle marinade. Beside the chicken, vibrant roasted bell peppers in thick slices—red, orange, and green—are artfully arranged with tender red onion wedges. The vegetables show slight charring and a tender-crisp texture. A scattering of bright green chopped cilantro and a few thin slices of red chili provides a fresh garnish, contrasting the deep, earthy tones of the chicken and vegetables. The plate sits on a simple, light wooden table surface, with a folded white cotton napkin placed to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish’s texture and color, set against a subtly blurred modern bistro background. A small, traditional Mexican molcajete or a ceramic salsa bowl in the background subtly reinforces the cultural context.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for building tacos.
Offer a side of fresh pico de gallo or salsa verde.
Pair with a simple lime-cilantro rice.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
In a blender, combine chipotle chiles, adobo sauce, 4 minced garlic cloves, lime juice, cumin, and oregano. Blend until smooth. This is your marinade.
Place chicken in a bowl. Pour marinade over chicken. Toss to coat evenly. Marinate for at least 30 minutes at room temperature, or up to 4 hours refrigerated.
Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Cut bell peppers into thick slices. Cut red onion into large wedges. Toss vegetables with 30 ml olive oil, remaining 2 minced garlic cloves, salt, and pepper.
Spread vegetables on a baking sheet. Roast for 20 minutes.
Heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear marinated chicken thighs for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Cook in batches if necessary. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Once chicken is seared, transfer skillet to the oven with the roasted vegetables. Cook for another 10-15 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and vegetables are tender-crisp.
Remove from oven. Let chicken rest for 5 minutes. Chop cilantro. Slice fresh red chili.
Serve chicken with roasted vegetables. Garnish with fresh cilantro and sliced red chili.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust chipotle quantity based on desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Burst Cherry Tomatoes and Basil
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown pan-seared chicken thigh, left whole, is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. It is generously topped with vibrant, burst cherry tomatoes, their skins split and juices mingling with a light, glossy sauce. Some tomatoes remain plump and whole, adding varied texture. Fresh, torn basil leaves, a rich green, are scattered over the chicken and tomatoes, providing a fragrant garnish and color contrast. The dish exhibits natural, organic arrangement, avoiding geometric shapes. The overall impression is one of fresh, rustic elegance. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, with a softly blurred bistro-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the sauce.
Serve alongside a simple side of pasta or roasted potatoes.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs for 6-8 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the pan. Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes. Sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add cherry tomatoes to the pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes burst and release their juices.
Pour in chicken broth and balsamic vinegar. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 2-3 minutes, scraping up any browned bits from the pan.
Return chicken to the pan. Spoon tomato sauce over chicken.
Tear fresh basil leaves. Stir most basil into the sauce.
Cook for 1-2 minutes more, ensuring chicken is heated through.
Garnish with remaining fresh basil. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Sausage, Macaroni & Tomato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A hearty individual portion of Sausage, Macaroni & Tomato Bake rests on a simple, round ceramic plate, showcasing a comforting, rustic appearance. The dish features tender elbow macaroni coated in a rich, reddish-orange tomato sauce, generously studded with browned, irregular chunks of savory pork sausage and small, soft cubes of carrot. A thick, bubbly layer of golden-brown melted cheddar cheese forms a delectable crust on top. The cheese is slightly caramelized in places, revealing some of the sauce and macaroni underneath. The dish is presented on a well-used, light wooden dining table, with natural, warm kitchen lighting. A slice of crusty, rustic bread sits casually beside the plate. The overall scene conveys a relaxed, homely family meal atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook macaroni according to package directions. Drain well.
Remove sausage from casings if using links. Break into irregular chunks.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or skillet over medium-high heat. Add sausage chunks. Cook until browned and cooked through. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion and carrots to the pot with sausage. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Stir in hot sauce, salt, black pepper, and dried oregano. Bring mixture to a simmer. Cook 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir cooked macaroni into the sauce. Add 100g shredded cheese. Stir until cheese begins to melt.
Spread mixture evenly in the pot or transfer to a 2L baking dish. Top with remaining 100g shredded cheese.
Bake 20-25 minutes, until cheese is bubbly and golden brown.
Serve hot with crusty bread.
notes: Adjust hot sauce quantity to suit your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Macaroni with Spicy Sausage and Roasted Tomato
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Baked Macaroni with Spicy Sausage and Roasted Tomato is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table. The baked macaroni forms a cohesive mound, showcasing its rich red-orange hue from the tomato sauce, interspersed with golden-brown crumbled sausage and melted, bubbly cheddar cheese. A light, crisp layer of golden breadcrumbs covers the top. Beside the macaroni, vibrant orange roasted carrot batons and halved, slightly charred roasted cherry tomatoes are artfully arranged. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley provides a final, verdant garnish. The composition is professional yet approachable, with moderate negative space. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors. Standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin are neatly placed beside the plate, completing the modern bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).

Cut carrots into 1 cm thick batons. Halve cherry tomatoes. Toss carrots and cherry tomatoes with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 20-25 minutes, until tender and slightly caramelized. Set aside.
Cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain and set aside.

Remove sausage from casings. In a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven, heat 15 ml olive oil over medium-high heat. Add sausage. Break up with a spoon. Cook until browned and cooked through. Drain excess fat. Remove sausage and set aside. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, hot sauce, dried oregano, salt, and pepper. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Stir in chopped fresh basil.

While sauce simmers, prepare cheese sauce. In a separate saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Whisk in flour. Cook for 1 minute to form a roux. Gradually whisk in milk until smooth. Bring to a simmer, whisking constantly, until thickened. Remove from heat. Stir in 150 g shredded cheddar cheese until melted and smooth.
Add cooked macaroni and cooked sausage to the tomato sauce in the skillet. Stir to combine.
Pour cheese sauce over the macaroni mixture. Stir gently to incorporate.
Sprinkle remaining 50 g shredded cheddar cheese and all Parmesan cheese over the top. Blitz stale bread into coarse breadcrumbs. Sprinkle breadcrumbs over the cheese.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, until cheese is bubbly and breadcrumbs are golden brown and crispy.
Serve hot. Garnish each portion with roasted carrot batons, roasted cherry tomatoes, and fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Spicy Sausage Macaroni with Tomato Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous individual portion of Baked Spicy Sausage Macaroni with Tomato Crumble is presented in a deep, clean white ceramic oval gratin dish. The dish showcases a rich, creamy, orange-tinted cheese sauce coating tender elbow macaroni. Visible within the golden-brown baked pasta are irregular chunks of browned sausage, vibrant red diced tomatoes, and small specks of orange grated carrot. A crisp, golden-brown crust of cheesy Panko breadcrumbs covers the top, providing textural contrast. The dish is lightly garnished with fresh green chopped parsley, adding a pop of color. The gratin dish rests on a simple wooden table surface, characteristic of a modern bistro setting. A white cotton napkin is neatly placed beside the dish, with a silver fork resting on it. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish as the focal point, with a subtly blurred background suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Lightly grease a 2.5-liter baking dish.
Cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add sausage, breaking it into small chunks. Cook until browned and cooked through. Drain excess fat. Remove sausage from skillet. Set aside.
In the same skillet, add diced onion and grated carrot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes and hot sauce. Bring to a simmer. Return cooked sausage to the skillet. Reduce heat to low. Keep warm.
In a separate large saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Whisk in flour to form a roux. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in warm milk until smooth. Continue whisking until sauce thickens, about 5-7 minutes. Remove from heat.
Stir in shredded cheddar cheese and half of the grated Parmesan cheese until melted and smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Combine cooked macaroni, sausage-tomato mixture, and cheese sauce in the prepared baking dish. Stir gently to combine.
In a small bowl, combine Panko breadcrumbs and remaining grated Parmesan cheese. Sprinkle evenly over the macaroni mixture.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and bubbly. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Warm Chicken and Tomato Penne Starter
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion of warm penne pasta is presented in a modest, round ceramic bowl with natural imperfections, set on a well-used wooden dining table. The pasta is naturally mounded in a casual arrangement. Diced chicken pieces, seared to a light golden brown, are interspersed throughout. Bright red halved cherry tomatoes are scattered among the penne, some slightly softened. Minced garlic bits are visible. Roughly chopped fresh green basil leaves are generously mixed in, adding a pop of color. The pasta has a slight sheen from olive oil. A dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese rests on top. The scene is lit by warm, cozy kitchen lighting, creating a relaxed, lived-in atmosphere. A simple cloth napkin and standard fork are casually placed beside the bowl.
instructions: Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain. Reserve 50ml pasta water.
Dice chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Sear chicken for 5-7 minutes until cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from pan.
Add minced garlic to the same pan. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add halved cherry tomatoes to the pan. Cook for 3-4 minutes until slightly softened.
Return cooked chicken to the pan. Add cooked penne pasta and chicken broth. Stir to combine.
Cook for 2-3 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. If too dry, add reserved pasta water.
Stir in chopped fresh basil.
Serve immediately. Garnish with grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: This starter is designed to be hearty yet not overly filling, preparing the palate for a main course.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Red Lentil and Chicken Pasta with Roasted Broccoli and Bell Pepper
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Spicy Red Lentil and Chicken Pasta is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The penne pasta is coated in a rich, rustic red lentil and tomato sauce, forming a loose, inviting mound in the center. Tender, golden-brown chicken chunks are placed atop and around the pasta, offering a hearty focal point. Vibrant green roasted broccoli florets and orange-red bell pepper strips are scattered artfully throughout the dish, adding pops of color and textural contrast. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese and a sprinkle of fresh green parsley garnish the top. The plate rests on a simple, light wooden table, accompanied by a neatly folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, emphasizing its balanced composition and appealing textures. The background is subtly blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut broccoli into small florets. Slice bell pepper into 1 cm wide strips.
Toss broccoli and bell pepper with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes, until tender-crisp and slightly charred. Set aside.

Rinse red lentils. In a medium pot, combine lentils with 500 ml chicken stock. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until lentils are tender and liquid is absorbed. Stir occasionally. Set aside.
While lentils cook, cut chicken breast into 2-3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear for 5-7 minutes, turning often, until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Dice the onion. Mince garlic. Heat remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil in the same skillet over medium heat.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook for 3-4 minutes, until softened. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more, until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and remaining 200 ml chicken stock. Add sliced pickled jalapenos. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Add cooked lentils to the tomato sauce. Stir well. Add fresh spinach and cook for 2-3 minutes, until wilted.
Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120 ml of pasta cooking water before draining.
Add drained pasta to the lentil-tomato sauce. Toss to combine. If sauce is too thick, add a splash of reserved pasta water until desired consistency is reached.
Fold in the seared chicken chunks.
Divide pasta among four plates. Top each serving with roasted broccoli florets and bell pepper strips.
Garnish with grated Parmesan cheese and fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Apple & Banana Preserve with Pecan Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of warm, rustic dessert in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl, off-white or beige. The bowl rests on a light-toned, unpolished wood or stone surface. The 'Fermented Apple & Banana Preserve' is a soft, chunky mixture with natural golden-brown hues from caramelized fruits, showing visible apple chunks and softened banana. A scattering of toasted pecan crumble provides textural contrast on top. A delicate, glossy drizzle of banana skin syrup cascades over the preserve, catching soft, natural light. The presentation is minimalistic with ample white space. A simple, undyed linen napkin in natural beige is beside the bowl. The background is softly blurred, hinting at natural elements, maintaining an eco-conscious, serene aesthetic. Focus is on the pure beauty of ingredients and natural textures.

ingredients.name: Firm Apples (e.g., Honeycrisp or Granny Smith)

instructions: Prepare apples: Wash apples thoroughly. Do not peel. Cut apples into 2 cm cubes, removing cores. Reserve cores and peels for later use.

Ferment apples: Place apple cubes in a clean glass jar. Dissolve 3 g sea salt in 100 ml filtered water. Pour brine over apples, ensuring apples are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight if needed. Cover with an airlock lid or tight lid (burp daily). Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Taste daily. Once fermented, store in refrigerator.

Make banana skin syrup: Thoroughly wash banana peels. Cut peels into 1 cm pieces. Place peels in a small saucepan with 100 ml filtered water and 30 ml maple syrup. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 15-20 minutes, until peels soften and liquid slightly thickens. Strain liquid, pressing solids to extract all syrup. Discard solids (compost if possible). Set syrup aside.

Prepare apple core pectin stock: Place reserved apple cores and peels in a small saucepan. Add 100 ml filtered water. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 15 minutes to extract natural pectin. Strain and reserve liquid. Discard solids.

Make preserve: Drain fermented apples, reserving fermentation liquid. In a saucepan, combine fermented apple cubes, fresh bananas (peeled, cut into 2 cm slices), remaining 30 ml maple syrup, reserved pectin stock, and cinnamon stick. Simmer gently over medium-low heat for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until fruit softens and mixture thickens to a preserve consistency. Remove cinnamon stick. Let cool slightly.

Make pecan crumble: Preheat oven to 160°C. In a bowl, combine pecans, rolled oats, and melted coconut oil. Mix well. Spread mixture onto a baking sheet. Bake for 10-12 minutes, until golden brown and fragrant. Let cool completely.
Assemble: Spoon the warm or chilled fruit preserve into individual serving bowls. Sprinkle with pecan crumble. Drizzle banana skin syrup over each portion. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe embraces zero-waste by utilizing apple cores, peels, and banana skins, transforming them into valuable components.
Fermentation enhances flavor complexity and aids in natural preservation.
Adjust sweetness to taste; the natural sugars from the fruits are prominent.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Chicken and Rice Patties
recipes.visual_description: Golden-brown chicken and rice patties are arranged casually on an off-white ceramic plate with a slightly uneven rim, resting on a well-worn light wooden table. The patties, roughly circular and about 2 cm thick, have a crisp, textured surface from pan-frying. Flecks of red diced tomato and green parsley are visible within the creamy white rice and shredded chicken interior, peeking from any slight cracks. A few additional fresh parsley leaves are scattered loosely on the plate for a touch of green. The setting is a cozy, lived-in kitchen with warm, diffused lighting. A simple, folded cloth napkin in a muted color lies beside the plate. The overall presentation is unpretentious, highlighting the comforting, homemade nature of the snack.
instructions: Combine shredded chicken and cooked rice in a large bowl.
Heat a small amount of oil in a pan. Sauté minced onion until soft. Add minced garlic and diced tomato. Cook for 3 minutes.
Add sautéed mixture to the chicken and rice bowl.
Add beaten egg, 50g breadcrumbs, chopped parsley, salt, and pepper to the bowl. Mix all ingredients thoroughly.
Form the mixture into 8-10 small patties, approximately 2 cm thick.
Lightly coat each patty with extra breadcrumbs.
Heat olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Cook patties for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Serve warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet & Savory Fermented Tomato-Onion Crisps
recipes.visual_description: A collection of small, irregularly shaped crispy rice crackers forms the base, each boasting a pale golden-beige hue from the chicken fat. Upon each crisp sits a generous dollop of deep reddish-brown, glossy compote, its texture invitingly jammy. A subtle sprinkle of finely ground umami chicken dust adds a hint of savory depth, complementing the sweet-sour compote. Delicate green microgreens or tiny herb leaves provide a fresh color contrast. The composition is natural and unforced, with ample white space. The crisps are arranged on pale, unglazed ceramic plates, resting on a light-toned wood surface. An undyed linen napkin is casually draped nearby. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the pure beauty and natural textures of each ingredient.

ingredients.name: Natural sweetener (e.g., date syrup, maple syrup)
Rendered chicken fat (from skin or trimmings)
Chicken trimmings or small piece of chicken breast/thigh (for Umami Chicken Dust)
Microgreens or small herb leaves (for garnish)

instructions: Ferment Tomatoes: Combine chopped tomatoes and 10g sea salt in a clean jar. Weigh down to keep submerged. Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days until bubbly and sour. Skim any surface mold. Strain liquid; reserve for other uses. Blend fermented tomato pulp into a rough puree.

Caramelize Aromatics: In a pan, melt a small amount of chicken fat. Add thinly sliced onions and garlic. Cook over low heat for 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply golden brown and very sweet.

Make Compote: Add blended fermented tomato pulp, natural sweetener, apple cider vinegar, and black pepper to the caramelized onions and garlic. Simmer gently for 20-30 minutes, stirring often, until thickened to a jam-like consistency. Adjust sweetness and sourness to taste.

Prepare Umami Chicken Dust: Poach chicken trimmings/piece in water until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Shred very finely. Dehydrate or toast in a dry pan until crispy and dry. Grind into a fine powder or floss.
Make Rice Crisps: In a bowl, mash cooked rice with rendered chicken fat and a pinch of salt until well combined.

Form & Bake Crisps: Spread the rice mixture very thinly (1-2mm) onto a parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake at 150°C for 30-40 minutes, or until completely dry and crispy. Break into irregular snack-sized pieces.

Assemble & Serve: Arrange rice crisps on a serving platter. Dollop a spoonful of the Sweet & Savory Fermented Tomato-Onion Compote onto each crisp. Sprinkle with Umami Chicken Dust and dried tomato skin powder (from fermented tomato process). Garnish with microgreens. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Sichuan-Style Peanut Chicken with Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sichuan-Style Peanut Chicken with Mushrooms is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Golden-brown seared chicken chunks are nestled among earthy, sautéed thick mushroom slices, all generously coated in a glossy, rich peanut-sesame sauce. The sauce creates a cohesive, appealing sheen. Thinly sliced green spring onions are scattered over the top, providing a vibrant color contrast, alongside a sprinkle of white toasted sesame seeds and a few red chili threads for visual interest. The arrangement is organic and balanced, allowing moderate negative space on the plate. The setting features a simple wooden table, with chopsticks resting on a small ceramic rest beside the plate. A small white rice bowl filled with fluffy steamed white rice is positioned slightly behind the main dish. A folded cotton napkin rests to the side. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors, with a soft, blurred restaurant-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with steamed white rice.
Offer a small dish of chili oil on the side for those who prefer extra heat.
Traditionally eaten with chopsticks.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2.5 cm thick chunks. Toss chicken with 5g cornstarch and 15ml soy sauce. Set aside.
Slice mushrooms thickly. Mince garlic and grate ginger.
Whisk together peanut butter, remaining soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, honey, water or stock, and remaining 15g cornstarch in a bowl. Add chili flakes if using. Set aside.

Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or deep pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add mushrooms to the hot pan. Sauté until softened and browned, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Return cooked chicken to the pan with the mushrooms. Stir the prepared sauce and pour over chicken and mushrooms. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens and coats all ingredients, about 2-3 minutes.
Garnish with thinly sliced spring onions and toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust honey or sugar to taste for desired sweetness in the sauce.
For extra spice, increase dried chili flakes or add a dash of Sichuan peppercorn oil to the sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Pea Risotto with Crispy Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant starter portion of fluid, pale green risotto is centrally placed on a round, matte white or light beige handcrafted ceramic plate. The risotto's natural green hue from fresh and fermented peas shows individual rice grains. Irregular, golden-brown crispy chicken skin shards are artfully arranged on top, providing textural contrast. A small, delicate cluster of bright green pea shoots adds height and freshness. Ample negative space emphasizes the dish's minimalistic beauty. The plate rests on a natural wood or stone surface. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish. A neutral beige linen napkin is casually folded beside the plate. The clean background is subtly textured, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Peas (2-3 days prior): Dissolve 7g salt in 250ml filtered water to make brine. Place 200g fresh green peas in a clean jar. Pour brine over peas, ensuring full submersion. Seal jar with an airlock lid or burp daily. Ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days until slightly tangy. Refrigerate after fermentation.
Prepare Chicken Stock: Heat 1 litre chicken stock in a saucepan. Keep it simmering gently.

Make Crispy Chicken Skin: Place 100g chicken skin in a cold, dry pan. Cook over medium-low heat. Render fat slowly until skin is golden and crispy. Remove skin, drain on paper towel. Season lightly with salt. Break into small shards.

Cook Risotto: Heat 30g butter or olive oil in a wide, heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. Add diced shallot. Cook until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.

Add 200g Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until grains are translucent at edges. Pour in one ladle of hot chicken stock. Stir until absorbed. Continue adding stock, one ladle at a time, stirring constantly. Wait until each addition is almost absorbed before adding the next. This takes about 18-20 minutes. The rice should be creamy and al dente.

Stir in 50g fresh green peas and 100g of drained fermented green peas. Cook for 2-3 minutes until fresh peas are tender. Remove from heat. Season with salt and pepper. The risotto should be fluid and flowing. If too thick, add a little more hot stock.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing chicken skin and homemade stock from bones.
Adjust fermentation time for peas based on desired tanginess.
For a plant-based version, omit chicken skin, use vegetable stock, and substitute butter with olive oil.

recipes.recipe_name: Miso Glazed Tofu with Shiitake Udon
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Miso Glazed Tofu with Shiitake Udon is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl, resting on a simple wooden table surface. Chewy, pale cream udon noodles form the base, artfully arranged. Irregularly shaped, golden-brown seared tofu cubes are nestled amongst the noodles, glistening with a dark, glossy miso glaze. Tender, dark brown sliced shiitake mushrooms are scattered alongside. The dish is garnished with vibrant green, thinly sliced scallions and a sprinkle of light brown toasted sesame seeds, providing a subtle color contrast. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. A neatly folded cotton napkin and a pair of dark wooden chopsticks are placed beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich, savory colors in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of pickled ginger (gari).
Offer a small bowl of miso soup as an accompaniment.
Provide shichimi togarashi (Japanese seven-spice blend) for those who prefer extra heat.
instructions: Press tofu: Wrap tofu in paper towels. Place heavy object on top. Press 20 minutes to remove excess water. Cut tofu into 3 cm cubes.
Prepare miso glaze: In a bowl, whisk miso paste, soy sauce, mirin, rice vinegar, and toasted sesame oil. Set aside.
Sear tofu: Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add tofu cubes. Sear until golden brown and crispy on all sides, about 8-10 minutes. Remove tofu from pan. Set aside.
Cook shiitake: Add sliced shiitake mushrooms to the same pan. Sauté until tender, about 5 minutes.
Add aromatics: Mince garlic and grate ginger. Add to the pan with shiitake. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Glaze tofu: Pour half of the miso glaze into the pan. Bring to a simmer. Return seared tofu to the pan. Toss gently to coat tofu with glaze. Simmer 2-3 minutes until glaze thickens slightly.
Cook udon: Meanwhile, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add udon noodles. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Combine udon: Add drained udon noodles to the pan with remaining miso glaze. Toss to coat noodles evenly.

Plate and serve: Divide udon noodles among four individual serving bowls. Arrange miso-glazed tofu cubes and shiitake mushrooms over the noodles. Garnish with thinly sliced scallions and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork and Mushroom Donburi
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Japanese Pork and Mushroom Donburi is presented in a deep, dark brown ceramic donburi bowl. The base holds a generous mound of steaming, fluffy short-grain white rice. Thinly sliced pork loin, simmered until tender, is arranged over one half of the rice. Adjacent to the pork, thinly sliced shiitake mushrooms, cooked to a rich dark brown, are nestled. Both the pork and mushrooms glisten with the savory, amber-hued donburi sauce. A scattering of vibrant, thinly sliced green onions provides a fresh green contrast atop the dish. The overall composition is clean and balanced, showcasing the comforting nature of the dish. The bowl sits on a simple light wooden table. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks rest on a ceramic chopstick holder beside the bowl. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with a side of miso soup.
Offer pickled ginger (gari) as an optional accompaniment.
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear. Cook rice according to package directions. Set aside.
Thinly slice pork loin into bite-sized pieces.
Slice shiitake mushrooms thinly.
Thinly slice the onion.
Prepare dashi stock if not using pre-made.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or shallow pot over medium heat.
Add sliced onion to the skillet. Sauté until soft and translucent, about 3 minutes.
Add sliced shiitake mushrooms. Cook for 3-4 minutes until tender.
Add pork slices to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until pork is no longer pink.
Pour in dashi stock, soy sauce, mirin, sake, and granulated sugar. Stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 5-7 minutes, or until pork is tender and sauce has slightly reduced.
While simmering, thinly slice green onions for garnish.
Divide cooked rice evenly among four deep donburi bowls.
Spoon the pork and mushroom mixture generously over the rice in each bowl.
Garnish each serving with a scattering of fresh green onions. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Skillet Chicken with Roasted Potatoes and Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rustic Skillet Chicken is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh is the focal point, positioned slightly off-center. Around the chicken, a generous scattering of roasted potato chunks, some with lightly crisped edges, are intermingled with browned cremini mushroom halves and vibrant red, softened cherry tomato halves. The vegetables are naturally arranged, some overlapping, creating a comforting and abundant feel. Small flecks of green from fresh chopped parsley are sprinkled over the dish, adding a touch of freshness. The chicken meat appears tender and juicy. The overall color palette is warm and inviting, dominated by golden browns, earthy reds, and deep greens. The plate sits on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table, showing subtle grain and character. A simple, folded cloth napkin in a neutral tone is casually placed next to the plate. Lighting is soft and warm, suggesting a cozy kitchen ambiance.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt, black pepper, and 3g of smoked paprika.
Wash potatoes. Cut potatoes into 2.5 cm thick chunks. Halve larger mushrooms. Halve cherry tomatoes.
Peel and thinly slice garlic cloves.

Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 6-8 minutes until skin is golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear for 2 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Add potato chunks to the same skillet. Toss with remaining oil and season with salt, pepper, and dried herbs. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5-7 minutes until lightly browned.
Stir in sliced garlic, mushrooms, and cherry tomatoes. Cook for 2-3 minutes.
Return seared chicken thighs to the skillet, nesting them among the vegetables. Pour chicken broth into the skillet.

Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are tender. Stir vegetables once halfway through roasting.
Remove skillet from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley if desired. Serve directly from the skillet or plate individually.

recipes.recipe_name: Tofu and Mung Bean Sprout Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Tofu and Mung Bean Sprout Stir-fry is presented in a large, shallow ceramic bowl with a slight rim, resting on a well-used wooden dining table. The dish features substantial 2cm golden-brown seared tofu cubes, bright julienned carrots, thin slices of red bell pepper, and crisp mung bean sprouts, all coated in a glossy, light brown sauce. Spring onion pieces are scattered throughout, adding fresh green accents. The arrangement is natural and casual, with ingredients piled generously in the center, allowing some components to slightly overlap. The overall color palette is warm with pops of orange and red from the vegetables and white from the sprouts. The texture is a mix of crisp vegetables and tender tofu. A pair of simple wooden chopsticks rests on the table beside the bowl, along with a small, plain white rice bowl filled with steamed white rice. A folded, beige linen napkin is casually placed nearby. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere. The background is minimal, focusing on the food and simple table elements.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice.
Offer a side of chili oil or a light soy sauce for dipping.
instructions: Press tofu for 20 minutes. Cut into 2cm cubes.
Mix soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, water, and cornstarch in a small bowl. This is the stir-fry sauce.
Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or pan over medium-high heat.
Add tofu cubes. Cook until golden brown on all sides. Remove tofu from pan. Set aside.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger to the same pan. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add julienned carrot and thinly sliced bell pepper. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until slightly tender-crisp.
Return cooked tofu to the pan.
Add mung bean sprouts and spring onions cut into 3cm lengths. Stir-fry for 1-2 minutes. Do not overcook sprouts.
Stir the prepared sauce mixture. Pour over the vegetables and tofu.
Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens and coats ingredients. This takes about 1 minute.
Season with white pepper and salt if needed. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust the amount of sauce ingredients to your taste.
Ensure the wok or pan is very hot before adding ingredients for best stir-fry results.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Chicken and Cheese Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy, vibrant orange-hued penne pasta is artfully arranged on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Tender, browned 2cm cubes of chicken are nestled throughout the pasta, coated in the rich, cheesy sauce. Specks of finely diced red chili and minced garlic are visible within the sauce, adding subtle color. A generous sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley provides a contrasting pop of color and freshness over the top. The pasta is moist and well-coated, not dry, with a gentle sheen from the creamy sauce. There is appropriate negative space on the plate, allowing the dish to breathe. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin positioned beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting from above, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere. The background is subtly blurred, hinting at a casual restaurant or bistro setting.

ingredients.name: Red chili (e.g., Fresno), deseeded and thinly sliced

instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add penne pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 100ml pasta water.

While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add diced chicken. Season with salt and pepper. Sear chicken until browned on all sides and cooked through, about 6-8 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced red chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in chili powder and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer for 5 minutes to reduce slightly.
Stir in heavy cream. Bring back to a gentle simmer.
Gradually add grated cheddar and parmesan cheese, stirring until melted and sauce is smooth. If sauce is too thick, add a little reserved pasta water.
Return cooked chicken to the pan with the sauce. Add drained pasta. Toss to coat everything evenly.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Pea Pasta with Smoked Cheddar
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a single individual portion. Thick medallions of golden-brown seared chicken breast are neatly arranged atop a generous mound of penne pasta. The pasta is coated in a rich, creamy, pale yellow sauce, highlighting its smooth texture. Vibrant green peas are artfully scattered throughout the pasta, providing contrasting pops of color. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped parsley adds a bright green garnish. The chicken exhibits a perfectly seared exterior and juicy interior. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple light wooden table surface, a neatly folded white cotton napkin beside the plate, and a minimalist restaurant-style background, all under natural, even lighting.
instructions: Cook pasta: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 120ml of the pasta water.

Prepare chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan. Let rest 5 minutes. Slice into thick medallions.
Sauté aromatics: In the same pan, melt butter with remaining olive oil over medium heat. Add diced shallots. Cook 3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze and reduce: Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes, reducing the liquid slightly.
Create sauce: Stir in heavy cream. Add grated smoked cheddar. Stir until cheese melts and sauce thickens slightly.
Combine ingredients: Add cooked pasta and green peas to the sauce. Toss to coat evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water gradually until desired consistency.
Finish and serve: Gently fold in the sliced chicken medallions. Stir in chopped fresh parsley. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Chicken and Pea Pasta Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Homestyle Chicken and Pea Pasta Bake rests on a sturdy, slightly imperfect white ceramic plate, set on a warm, well-worn wooden kitchen table. The dish presents a comforting, rustic appearance: a golden-brown, bubbly crust of melted cheddar cheese covers the top, showing crispy edges. Beneath, substantial chunks of seared chicken, approximately 2cm cubes, are nestled among al dente penne pasta and vibrant green peas. The pasta is coated in a thick, creamy, off-white sauce, with specks of dried thyme visible. The components are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping, reflecting a casual, home-style plating. The scene is illuminated by soft, inviting kitchen light. A simple, folded linen napkin lies beside the plate. The background hints at a cozy, lived-in family kitchen, emphasizing the dish's homely comfort.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served family-style directly from the baking dish.
Often accompanied by a simple green salad or crusty bread.
instructions: Cook pasta. Boil water. Add pasta. Cook until al dente. Drain. Set aside.
Prepare chicken. Dice chicken breast into 2cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.

Cook chicken. Heat olive oil in large oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Sauté aromatics. Add butter to pan. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Make sauce. Sprinkle flour over onion and garlic. Stir 1 minute. Slowly whisk in chicken broth and milk. Bring to simmer. Cook, stirring, until sauce thickens.
Combine ingredients. Stir cooked chicken, green peas, and cooked pasta into sauce. Add thyme. Stir gently to combine. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Top with cheese. Transfer mixture to a 20x30cm baking dish if not using oven-safe pan. Sprinkle grated cheddar cheese evenly over top.
Bake. Bake in preheated oven at 190°C (375°F) for 20-25 minutes. Bake until cheese is melted and bubbly, and top is golden brown.
Rest. Let pasta bake rest 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Herb-Roasted Chicken and Vegetables
recipes.special_requests: low calories (1000 a day for 3-4 meals)
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of roasted chicken breast and vegetables rests on a simple, round ceramic plate. The chicken is whole, golden-brown from roasting, placed slightly off-center. Roasted potato 2cm cubes, bell pepper 2cm chunks, onion 2cm wedges, and halved cherry tomatoes are scattered naturally around the chicken, some touching, some slightly overlapping. A few fresh thyme leaves are visible among the vegetables. The plate rests on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple, folded cloth napkin in a neutral color is casually placed beside the plate. A small, unpeeled lemon wedge is placed next to the chicken on the plate. Lighting is warm and cozy, suggesting natural light from a kitchen window or soft overhead fixtures. The background is minimal, perhaps a blurred glimpse of a home kitchen.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut potato into 2cm cubes. Cut bell pepper into 2cm chunks. Cut onion into 2cm wedges. Mince garlic. Halve cherry tomatoes.
In a bowl, combine potatoes, bell pepper, onion, garlic, cherry tomatoes, thyme, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Toss to coat.
Place vegetables in a single layer on a small baking sheet.
Season chicken breast with salt and pepper. Place chicken on the baking sheet among the vegetables.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and vegetables are tender and lightly browned.
Serve immediately with a lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Sheet Pan Lemon Herb Chicken with Roasted Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of roasted chicken and vegetables is presented on an everyday ceramic plate. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table in a homely family kitchen. Three thick chunks of roasted chicken breast are golden-brown and nestled among vibrant roasted vegetables. Bell pepper strips in various colors (red, yellow, green) are softened with slightly caramelized edges. Onion wedges show a tender texture. Burst cherry tomatoes are scattered throughout, adding pops of red and a hint of sweetness. The ingredients are casually arranged, overlapping naturally. A few fresh thyme leaves are sprinkled over the dish for a functional garnish. The scene is illuminated by warm, cozy lighting, creating a relaxed, lived-in atmosphere. A simple fork and knife are placed beside the plate. The entire plate is visible, showcasing the modest, home-style portion with appropriate negative space.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut chicken breast into 2-3 thick chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice bell pepper into thick strips. Slice onion into wedges.
Mince garlic.
On a sheet pan, combine chicken chunks, bell pepper strips, onion wedges, cherry tomatoes, minced garlic, and fresh thyme sprigs.
Drizzle with olive oil. Toss all ingredients gently to coat evenly.
Squeeze lemon half over ingredients. Place squeezed lemon half on the pan.
Roast for 25-30 minutes. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C. Vegetables should be tender-crisp with slight charring.
Remove from oven. Discard lemon half and thyme sprigs.
Serve immediately on a single plate.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Potato Bake
recipes.visual_description: The Hearty Beef and Potato Bake is presented in a rustic, well-used cast-iron skillet, still slightly bubbling. The base consists of tender, roasted potato cubes, some with skins, interspersed with savory diced onions and softened bell pepper pieces. Generous chunks of browned beef, each about 2.5 cm, are nestled among the vegetables, showcasing a rich, caramelized exterior. Melted, golden-orange cheddar cheese forms a bubbly, slightly browned crust over the top. Specks of fresh green thyme leaves are visible throughout, adding color. The color palette is warm, with deep browns, reds, and yellows. The texture is varied, from soft potatoes to firm beef and gooey cheese. The skillet is placed on a simple, worn wooden dining table. A plain ceramic plate with a modest single portion is ready beside it, with a standard fork and knife. Warm, natural lighting illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve family style directly from the skillet.
instructions: Cut beef into 2.5 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Cut potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Dice onion. Mince garlic. Cut bell pepper into 2 cm pieces. Dice tomatoes.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Brown beef cubes in batches until seared. Remove beef.
Add onion to skillet. Cook 5 minutes until softened. Add garlic and bell pepper. Cook 2 minutes.
Return beef to skillet. Add potatoes, diced tomatoes, 30 g butter, and 5 g fresh thyme. Stir well.
Cover skillet. Bake at 180°C for 45 minutes.
Uncover. Sprinkle 150 g cheddar cheese over the top. Bake uncovered for another 15-20 minutes, until potatoes are tender and cheese is melted and bubbly.
Rest 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken and Root Vegetable Medley with Fermented Garlic-Thyme Yogurt
