Add corn kernels to the skillet. Cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally. Remove corn mixture from skillet and set aside.
Melt butter in the same skillet over medium heat. Whisk in flour to form a roux. Cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in milk and heavy cream until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens.
Remove from heat. Stir in shredded Gruyère cheese until melted and smooth. Season with salt and black pepper.
Fold the cooked corn mixture and crumbled crispy bacon into the cheese sauce.
Pour the mixture into the prepared baking dish. Top evenly with the Parmesan breadcrumbs.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until bubbly and the topping is golden brown.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chives.
notes: For best results, use fresh corn. If unavailable, frozen corn kernels can be used; thaw and drain well before adding to the skillet.

recipes.recipe_name: Ham and Swiss Potato Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous rectangular portion of Ham and Swiss Potato Gratin is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The gratin reveals distinct layers of thinly sliced, tender, pale yellow potatoes, interspersed with savory pink ham cubes, all bound by a creamy white bechamel sauce. The top crust is a rich golden brown, with visible melted Swiss cheese and toasted, irregular breadcrumbs providing a textural contrast. A small sprig of fresh green thyme leaves garnishes the top. On the side of the plate, a small dollop of whole grain mustard or a drizzle of mustard oil offers a subtle color accent. The dish is set on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by polished traditional flatware and a neatly folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish’s inviting textures and colors, with a soft, unobtrusive restaurant-style background creating a casual bistro ambiance.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Lightly grease a 20x30 cm baking dish with olive oil.
Peel potatoes. Slice thinly into 2-3 mm rounds using a mandoline or sharp knife.
Dice cooked ham into 1.5 cm cubes.
For the bechamel: Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add flour. Cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in milk and cream. Cook, stirring, until sauce thickens and coats the back of a spoon. Do not boil vigorously.
Remove from heat. Stir in Dijon mustard, minced garlic, half of the fresh thyme, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Arrange one-third of the potato slices in a single layer in the prepared baking dish. Top with half of the diced ham.
Pour one-third of the bechamel sauce evenly over the ham and potatoes. Sprinkle with one-third of the grated Swiss cheese.
Repeat layering: potatoes, remaining ham, sauce, cheese. Finish with a final layer of potatoes, covered with remaining sauce.
For the topping: Tear day-old bread into small crumbs or pulse in a food processor. Combine breadcrumbs with remaining Swiss cheese and fresh thyme.
Sprinkle breadcrumb mixture evenly over the top of the gratin.
Bake for 45-55 minutes, or until potatoes are tender when pierced and topping is golden brown and bubbly. If topping browns too quickly, cover loosely with foil.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 10 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken Thighs with Dark Beer and Rosemary
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Braised Chicken Thighs with Dark Beer and Rosemary is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. One whole, plump, seared chicken thigh, deeply caramelized, rests centrally. Rustic chunks of roasted potatoes, vibrant orange carrots, red bell pepper, and halved cremini mushrooms are artfully arranged around the chicken. A glossy, rich dark beer sauce generously coats the chicken and vegetables. A fresh rosemary sprig garnishes the dish. Colors are warm: deep browns, rich reds, and bright oranges. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table, clean white napkin, and standard European flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, which appears professional yet approachable, with moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty rustic bread to soak up the rich sauce.

ingredients.name: Red bell pepper
ingredients.quantity: 1, deseeded and cut into large pieces

ingredients.name: Dark beer (e.g., Belgian Dubbel or Stout)

instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Lightly dredge in flour, shaking off excess.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until deep golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear other side for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add chopped onion, carrots, and bell pepper to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add mushrooms and sauté for another 3 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in dark beer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half.
Stir in chicken broth, Worcestershire sauce, and Dijon mustard. Add two rosemary sprigs. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the liquid. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Cover the pot tightly with a lid. Transfer to the preheated oven.
Braise for 45 minutes. Add potato chunks to the pot. Stir gently.
Continue braising for another 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C. Potatoes should be fork-tender.
Remove pot from oven. Discard rosemary sprigs. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve hot, garnished with a fresh rosemary sprig.
notes: Braising slowly tenderizes the chicken, making it succulent and flavorful.
The dark beer adds depth and complexity to the sauce, balancing savory notes with subtle bitterness.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Loin with Cherry-Raspberry Gastrique
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared pork loin is centered on a round white porcelain plate. Two thick, golden-crusted pork medallions, each 2.5 cm, are slightly overlapped, revealing a tender, light pink interior. A glossy, deep ruby-red cherry-raspberry gastrique is spooned over the pork and around the plate, providing vibrant contrast. Alongside, golden-brown roasted apple and pear wedges are neatly arranged, their edges caramelized. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of toasted slivered almonds for crunch and a fresh thyme sprig. The composition is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple light wooden table surface and a white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's rich colors and textures.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Season pork loin generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear pork loin on all sides until golden brown. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 68°C.

While pork roasts, prepare apples and pears. Core apples and pears. Cut into 8 wedges each. Toss apple and pear wedges with remaining 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Arrange on a baking sheet. Roast in oven with pork for the last 10-15 minutes, or until tender and slightly caramelized.
For the gastrique, remove pork from skillet. Set aside to rest, tented with foil. Discard excess fat from skillet, leaving 1-2 tablespoons.
Add minced shallots to skillet. Sauté over medium heat until softened, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more.
Pour in red wine vinegar and sugar. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Add pitted cherries and 100g raspberries to skillet. Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 8-10 minutes, mashing fruits slightly, until sauce thickens.
Strain gastrique through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan, pressing solids to extract liquid. Discard solids.
Return strained gastrique to low heat. Whisk in butter until melted and incorporated. Stir in lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Slice rested pork loin into 2.5 cm thick medallions.

To plate, place two pork medallions on each plate. Arrange roasted apple and pear wedges alongside. Spoon cherry-raspberry gastrique over pork and around the plate. Garnish with toasted slivered almonds and a fresh thyme sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Sausage and Potato Bake with Roasted Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of a rustic European bake is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Golden-brown roasted potato wedges are artfully scattered, alongside vibrant green, tender-crisp roasted broccoli florets. Three to four substantial, seared smoked sausage chunks, with browned and slightly crispy edges, are nestled among the vegetables, serving as the focal point. A light dusting of finely grated smoked Gouda cheese melts subtly over the warm components. Freshly chopped bright green parsley is sprinkled for color and freshness. The plating is organized yet approachable, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, a folded white cotton napkin, and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish. A slice of rustic bread rests beside the plate, completing the authentic dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of whole grain mustard or stone-ground mustard.
Accompany with a crisp green salad with a simple vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
Wash potatoes. Cut into 2cm thick wedges. Place on baking sheet. Drizzle with 30ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat.
Roast potatoes for 20 minutes.
While potatoes roast, wash broccoli. Cut into medium florets. Cut sausage into 3cm thick chunks.
After 20 minutes, remove baking sheet. Add broccoli florets to the sheet. Drizzle broccoli with remaining 30ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss with potatoes.
Return baking sheet to oven. Roast for another 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are golden and tender, and broccoli is tender-crisp.
While vegetables roast, heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add sausage chunks. Sear for 5-7 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned and slightly crispy on all sides. Remove from heat.
Grate smoked Gouda cheese.
Chop fresh parsley.

To serve, arrange roasted potato wedges, roasted broccoli florets, and seared sausage chunks on individual plates. Sprinkle generously with grated smoked Gouda. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately with rustic bread slices.
notes: Use a high-quality smoked sausage for best flavor.
Adjust roasting times based on your oven and desired crispness of vegetables.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Sausage and Corn Bread Pudding with Crispy Bacon
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Savory Sausage and Corn Bread Pudding is centrally placed on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a simple restaurant-style presentation. The bread pudding is cut into a neat, rustic square, revealing a golden-brown crust on top and soft, moist interior. Visible within the pudding are distinct pieces of browned, diced pork sausage, vibrant yellow whole corn kernels, and specks of fresh green chives. The texture is invitingly soft, contrasted by the crispy, reddish-brown bacon crumbles generously sprinkled over the top. The overall color palette is warm and inviting, dominated by golden browns, yellows, and the deep green of the garnish. The plate features moderate negative space, allowing the dish to be the clear focal point. The setting is a modern bistro, with the plate resting on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside a crisp green salad or steamed green beans for a balanced meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Lightly butter a 23x33 cm baking dish.
Cook diced bacon in a large skillet over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Drain all but 30ml bacon fat from the skillet. Crumble cooked bacon and set aside.
Add crumbled sausage to the same skillet. Cook over medium-high heat, breaking up with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Drain excess fat. Remove sausage from skillet.
Add diced onion to the skillet with remaining bacon fat. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.
Stir in corn kernels and cooked sausage. Cook for 2-3 minutes to combine flavors. Remove from heat.
In a large bowl, whisk together eggs, milk, heavy cream, chicken broth, Dijon mustard, chopped fresh thyme, salt, and black pepper.
Add bread cubes to the egg mixture. Gently toss to coat all bread. Let stand for 10 minutes, allowing bread to absorb liquid.
Fold in the sausage, corn, and onion mixture. Fold in grated cheddar cheese.
Pour the mixture into the prepared baking dish. Press down gently to ensure even distribution.
Bake for 35-45 minutes, or until the bread pudding is golden brown and a knife inserted into the center comes out clean.
Let stand for 5-10 minutes before serving. Garnish with reserved crispy bacon crumbles and fresh chives.
notes: This dish can be prepared ahead and baked just before serving for convenience.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Sausage and Cheese Toasts
recipes.visual_description: The Hearty Sausage and Cheese Toasts are presented on a simple, well-used wooden cutting board, or a rustic ceramic platter. Each toast features a thick slice of sturdy bread, golden-brown and slightly crisp at the edges. Generous portions of crumbled, browned sausage are spread across the bread, showing rich, savory tones. A thick layer of melted, bubbly cheddar cheese covers the sausage, with some areas golden and lightly charred from baking, highlighting its rich texture. The cheese flows naturally over the sausage and bread, creating an inviting, comforting appearance. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped green chives adds a pop of vibrant color and freshness. The arrangement is casual and unpretentious, as if just pulled from the oven for a family snack. The entire board or platter is visible, showing natural, homely portions. The scene is set on a warm kitchen table, with soft, natural lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while warm.
Offer with a side of ketchup or mustard for dipping.
Pair with a simple green salad or a bowl of tomato soup.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Remove sausage from casings. Crumble sausage into a large pan.
Add olive oil to the pan. Cook sausage over medium heat until browned and cooked through. Break up any large pieces.
Add diced onion to the pan with the sausage. Cook until onion is softened, about 5 minutes.
Drain excess fat from the pan. Season sausage mixture with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Arrange bread slices on a baking sheet.
Spoon the cooked sausage and onion mixture evenly over each bread slice.
Top generously with grated cheddar cheese.
Bake for 8-12 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and bread is lightly toasted.
For extra crispiness, broil for the last 1-2 minutes, watching carefully to prevent burning.
Remove from oven. Garnish with fresh chopped chives.
notes: Use a sturdy bread like sourdough or country white bread for best results.
Ensure sausage is fully cooked to 75°C (167°F) internal temperature.
Adjust seasoning to your preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Spiced Coconut-Peanut Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken thigh, rich golden-brown, rests centrally on a white porcelain dinner plate. It is generously coated in a glossy, deep reddish-brown coconut-peanut sauce. The sauce pools gently around the chicken, showcasing its creamy texture. A small, vibrant green cluster of fresh cilantro leaves is placed atop the chicken. Beside it, a tiny, jewel-like spoonful of bright orange tobiko fish roe adds a pop of color and texture. The chicken's golden crust contrasts with the dark, smooth sauce. The cilantro provides fresh green, and the roe offers a vivid orange. The plate is set on a light wooden table surface. A neatly folded plain white cotton napkin is positioned to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro atmosphere. Chicken is presented as a whole boneless thigh.
instructions: Combine yogurt, half of the grated ginger, salt, and pepper in a bowl. Add chicken thighs. Toss to coat. Marinate for 30 minutes.

Heat cooking oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on both sides. Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the same skillet. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add minced garlic and remaining grated ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in ground cumin, ground coriander, ground turmeric, and chili powder. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Pour in coconut milk. Stir in peanut butter, grated dark chocolate, and brewed coffee. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer the sauce for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it thickens slightly.
Return the seared chicken thighs to the skillet with the sauce. Simmer gently for 5 minutes, ensuring chicken is fully cooked through.
Stir in lime juice. Taste the sauce and adjust salt and pepper as needed.
Plate each chicken thigh with a generous portion of sauce. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and a small dollop of tobiko fish roe.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Pork Ssam Bites
recipes.visual_description: The Spicy Pork Ssam Bites are presented on a rustic, well-used wooden board. Eight to twelve vibrant green lettuce cups are arranged casually, some slightly overlapping, filling the platter without overcrowding. Each crisp lettuce leaf cradles a generous spoonful of rich, reddish-brown spicy pork mixture, stir-fried until tender and slightly caramelized. The pork is mixed with translucent slivers of onion and bright green flecks of chili and scallion, showcasing a medley of textures. A small mound of glistening white short-grain rice peeks from beneath the pork in each bite. The entire dish is adorned with delicate julienned green scallions, adding a fresh, verdant contrast. The scene is set on a simple, homely kitchen table, illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen light, evoking a comfortable family dining atmosphere. The ceramic plates underneath the board, if visible, are simple, off-white, and slightly imperfect, reflecting everyday use.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Traditionally eaten by hand.
Can be served with a small side of ssamjang or kimchi for additional flavor.
Often part of a larger Korean meal with various banchan (side dishes).

ingredients.name: Lettuce leaves (e.g., red leaf, green leaf, or perilla leaves)
Green chili (e.g., Korean green chili or serrano)

instructions: Prepare pork. Thinly slice pork shoulder or belly into bite-sized pieces. Alternatively, mince pork.
Make marinade. In a bowl, combine gochujang, soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, minced ginger, and black pepper.
Marinate pork. Add pork to the marinade. Mix well. Let marinate for 15-20 minutes.
Prepare vegetables. Thinly slice onion. Mince garlic. Thinly slice or mince green chili. Julienne green parts of scallions for garnish. Chop white parts of scallions.
Cook pork. Heat a large pan or wok over medium-high heat. Add marinated pork. Stir-fry until pork is cooked through and lightly caramelized. This takes 5-7 minutes.
Add aromatics. Add sliced onion, minced garlic, chopped white scallions, and green chili to the pan. Continue stir-frying for 3-4 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Assemble ssam bites. Lay out individual lettuce leaves. Place a small spoonful of cooked rice (if using) in the center of each leaf. Top with a spoonful of the spicy pork mixture.
Garnish. Garnish each ssam bite with julienned green scallions.
Serve immediately.
traditional_techniques: Bokkeum (stir-frying) technique for cooking the pork and vegetables
Ssam (wrapping food in leaves) as a serving and eating method

recipes.recipe_name: Rigatoni with Roasted Pepper & Tomato Sauce, Ricotta Malfatti, and Crispy Sausage
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rigatoni pasta is presented in a handcrafted, matte ceramic bowl in an earthy beige tone. The pasta is generously coated in a rich, rustic roasted bell pepper and tomato sauce, showcasing deep reds and oranges. Nestled within the pasta are several irregular, cloud-like ricotta malfatti, their creamy white contrasting against the vibrant sauce. Scattered over the dish are golden-brown, crispy chunks of Italian sausage. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are artfully placed for a pop of color. The setting features a light, textured reclaimed wood table surface. A simple, undyed linen napkin rests beside the bowl. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from the side, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the textures. The background is minimalist and clean, allowing the dish to be the focal point. The plate is not overcrowded, leaving ample negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar
A glass of dry red wine, such as Chianti or Montepulciano d'Abruzzo

ingredients.name: Fresh basil
ingredients.quantity: 1 large bunch (leaves picked, some for garnish)

ingredients.name: Brine from pickled vegetables (e.g., sauerkraut, pickled peppers)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve bell peppers. Remove seeds. Place cut-side down on a baking tray. Drizzle with olive oil. Roast 25-30 minutes until skin blackens. Place roasted peppers in a bowl. Cover tightly with cling film 10 minutes. Peel skins. Roughly chop roasted pepper flesh.

For Malfatti: Combine ricotta, grated Parmesan, flour, egg, salt, and pepper in a bowl. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix. Chill dough 15 minutes. Lightly flour a surface. Spoon small, irregular portions of dough. Roll gently into rustic, oblong shapes (about 2 cm).
Heat a large pot of salted water to boil for pasta and Malfatti.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add Italian sausage, crumbled. Cook, breaking up with a spoon, until crispy and browned. Drain excess fat. Set sausage aside. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
In the same skillet, add a little more olive oil if needed. Add diced red onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and chili flakes (if using). Cook 1 minute until fragrant.

Add roughly chopped fresh tomatoes and chopped roasted bell peppers to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, 10-12 minutes until tomatoes break down. Stir in brine from pickled vegetables. Season with salt and black pepper. Simmer sauce 5 minutes.

Drop Malfatti into boiling water. Cook 3-4 minutes until they float to the surface. Remove with a slotted spoon. Add Rigatoni to the same boiling water. Cook according to package directions until al dente.

Drain pasta, reserving 120 ml pasta water. Add pasta to the skillet with the sauce. Add Malfatti. Toss gently to combine. Add reserved pasta water as needed to achieve desired sauce consistency. Stir in most fresh basil leaves.
Serve hot. Garnish each portion with crispy Italian sausage chunks and fresh basil leaves.
notes: Using brine from fermented vegetables introduces a complex, tangy flavor that aligns with preservation and zero-waste principles.
This recipe emphasizes seasonal vegetables and uses ricotta as a plant-forward protein source.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Medallions with Herb Mushroom Sauté
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Seared Beef Medallions with Herb Mushroom Sauté is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Two thick, seared beef medallions, perfectly crusted and unsliced, are placed centrally. A generous portion of sautéed vegetables, including golden caramelized onion strips, vibrant 2cm diced red and yellow bell peppers, and richly browned sliced cremini mushrooms, is arranged around the beef. A glossy, dark amber pan sauce is drizzled over the dish. Fresh, chopped parsley garnishes the plate, adding a bright green contrast. The plating is balanced with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table, a white cotton napkin beside the plate, and natural, even lighting, creating a modern bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Pat beef medallions dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear beef medallions 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to desired doneness. Do not overcrowd pan. Sear in batches if necessary.
Remove beef from skillet. Set aside on a plate, tent with foil.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter to the same skillet. Reduce heat to medium.
Add sliced onion. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened and lightly caramelized.
Add diced bell peppers. Cook 3-4 minutes until slightly tender-crisp.
Add sliced mushrooms and minced garlic. Cook 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are browned and tender.
Stir in fresh oregano.
If using, deglaze pan with red wine. Scrape up any browned bits. Cook 2 minutes until reduced slightly.
Pour in beef broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5-7 minutes, reducing sauce by about one-third.
Stir in remaining 15g butter until melted and sauce is slightly thickened and glossy. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve beef medallions immediately, topped with the mushroom-pepper sauté and pan sauce. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Consider serving with roasted potatoes or creamy polenta to complete the meal.

recipes.recipe_name: Stuffed Lumaconi with Sausage, Ricotta, and Bell Pepper Sugo
recipes.visual_description: Two to three generously stuffed lumaconi shells are arranged on a pristine white round plate, resting on a vibrant red bed of rustic tomato and diced bell pepper sugo. The creamy white ricotta and golden-brown crumbled Italian sausage filling peeks invitingly from the openings of the large pasta shells. A light drizzle of the rich sugo lightly coats the top of the shells. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are artfully placed on and around the pasta, providing a pop of contrasting color and freshness. A delicate dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese completes the dish. The bell peppers are diced into small, even cubes, showcasing precise knife work. The plating is clean and professional, with moderate negative space. The dish is presented on a simple light wooden table with a folded beige linen napkin and a silver fork beside the plate, under soft, natural lighting, highlighting the dish as the centerpiece.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Cook lumaconi pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain and rinse with cold water to prevent sticking.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add Italian sausage. Cook, breaking it into crumbles, until browned. Drain excess fat. Set aside to cool slightly.
In a large bowl, combine cooled sausage, ricotta cheese, 15 g chopped basil, 30 g grated Parmesan, salt, and black pepper. Mix well.
Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in the same skillet over medium heat.
Add chopped onion and diced bell peppers. Sauté until softened, about 7-8 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes. Add a pinch of sugar if tomatoes are acidic. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer sauce for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Season with salt and black pepper.
Spread a thin layer of tomato-bell pepper sugo in the bottom of a 23x33 cm baking dish.
Carefully stuff each lumaconi shell with the sausage-ricotta mixture.
Arrange stuffed shells in a single layer over the sauce in the baking dish.
Spoon remaining sugo over the stuffed shells. Ensure shells are mostly covered.
Sprinkle remaining 50 g grated Parmesan cheese over the shells.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and sauce is hot.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with remaining fresh basil before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Sausage and Ham Toasts
recipes.visual_description: A single rustic bread slice, lightly toasted to a golden hue, sits casually on a round, off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections. The bread is generously topped with a savory mixture of crumbled, browned Italian sausage and small, lightly crisped cubes of cooked ham. Interspersed within the meat are translucent, softened diced onions and flecks of minced garlic. The mixture has a rich, reddish-brown color from the hot sauce, which is visibly coating the ingredients. A scattering of bright green, freshly chopped parsley is sprinkled over the top, providing a vibrant color contrast. The components on the toast are naturally piled and slightly overlapping, indicating a hearty, comforting portion. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, showing natural grain and a few faint marks. A simple, casually folded cream-colored cloth napkin is placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft kitchen lighting, creating a cozy and inviting atmosphere. The entire plate is visible, showcasing the homemade, approachable style of the starter.
instructions: Remove sausage casings. Crumble sausage into a large pan. Cook over medium heat until browned and cooked through. Drain excess fat.
Dice cooked ham into small cubes. Add diced ham to the pan with the cooked sausage. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring, until lightly crisped.
Dice the onion into small pieces. Mince the garlic. Add diced onion and minced garlic to the pan with sausage and ham. Sauté until onion is softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in hot sauce. Season with salt and black pepper. Mix well. Remove from heat.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Arrange bread slices on a baking sheet. Drizzle lightly with olive oil. Bake for 5-7 minutes, or until lightly toasted and golden.
Spoon the sausage and ham mixture generously onto each toasted bread slice. Chop fresh parsley. Garnish each toast with chopped parsley.
Serve warm immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo en Salsa de Chocolate y Chile
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Pollo en Salsa de Chocolate y Chile is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two generous, whole seared chicken thigh pieces, rich golden-brown, are generously coated in a glossy, deep reddish-brown chocolate-chili sauce. The sauce is thick and smooth, clinging to the chicken, with a subtle sheen. Bright green, roughly chopped fresh cilantro leaves and pale, toasted sesame seeds are scattered over the sauce. The chicken is positioned centrally, leaving moderate negative space. Beside the plate, a stack of warm corn tortillas is neatly arranged. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple light wooden table surface and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich colors and textures against a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Accompany with a side of Mexican rice
Serve with refried beans
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Cook to internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the pan. Sauté diced onion 5 minutes until soft. Add minced garlic, cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly, to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in milk and chicken broth. Stir until smooth and slightly thickened.
Add crushed tomatoes, chili powder, cumin, and oregano. Stir well.
Break chocolate into pieces. Add to sauce. Stir until melted and smooth.
Stir in cream cheese until fully incorporated and sauce is creamy.
Return chicken to the pan. Coat with sauce. Simmer gently 10-15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve hot. Garnish with fresh cilantro and toasted sesame seeds.
traditional_techniques: Slow simmering to develop deep flavors
Building a roux for sauce thickening

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Shrimp & Ham Fritters
recipes.visual_description: Warm, golden-brown fritters are casually arranged on a rustic, well-used wooden cutting board or an everyday cream-colored ceramic plate. Each fritter is irregularly shaped, showing its homemade charm, with visible browned edges from frying. The surface reveals hints of crispy, diced bacon, small pink shrimp pieces, and melted, bubbly cheese. Some fritters are loosely stacked, others spread out naturally. A few vibrant green specks of finely chopped chives are sprinkled over the top for a fresh accent. The interior reveals a tender, savory mix of cooked shrimp (chopped), diced ham, finely chopped onion, and creamy, melted cheese, interspersed with dark, chopped olives. The overall impression is comforting home cooking. The scene is set on a simple kitchen table with warm, inviting light, suggesting a relaxed family snack time.
instructions: Dice bacon into small pieces. Cook in a large pan over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Reserve 15ml bacon fat in the pan.
Finely chop the onion. Add to the pan with bacon fat. Sauté until soft and translucent, about 5 minutes.
Chop shrimp into small pieces. Add chopped shrimp to the pan. Cook until pink, about 2-3 minutes. Remove from heat.
Dice ham into small cubes. Pit and chop olives.
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, salt, and pepper.
In a separate bowl, whisk the egg and heavy cream.
Add the egg mixture, cooked onion and shrimp, diced ham, chopped olives, shredded cheese, and crispy bacon to the flour mixture. Mix until just combined to form a thick batter.
Heat remaining 15ml vegetable oil in the same pan over medium heat.
Drop spoonfuls of batter into the hot oil. Flatten each fritter slightly with the back of the spoon.
Cook fritters for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through.
Remove fritters from pan and drain on paper towels to remove excess oil.
Serve warm. Garnish with finely chopped chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Francesinha with Spicy Tomato Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A robust Francesinha sandwich anchors the center of a clean white porcelain plate, resting on a simple wooden table. The thick, toasted bread is layered with seared, diagonally sliced linguiça sausage and thin slices of cooked ham. A generous blanket of golden, bubbly melted cheese completely envelops the sandwich. A perfectly fried egg, featuring a bright, runny yolk, crowns the top. A rich, reddish-brown chili-infused tomato sauce pools elegantly around the base of the sandwich, with a slight sheen. Colors are warm and inviting: golden cheese, deep red sauce, and the vibrant yellow of the egg yolk. A few golden, crisp French fries are casually placed alongside, honoring its traditional accompaniment. A folded white cotton napkin sits beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting warmth.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with a fried egg on top and French fries.
instructions: Prepare the sauce: Heat olive oil in a saucepan. Sauté diced onion until softened.
Add minced garlic and chili; cook 1 minute. Stir in tomato paste; cook 2 minutes.
Deglaze with brandy or Port wine. Add beer, beef broth, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer. Cook 20 minutes, reducing slightly.
Remove bay leaf. Whisk cornstarch with cold water to make a slurry. Stir slurry into sauce. Simmer until sauce thickens. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Prepare sandwiches: Toast bread slices lightly.
In a separate pan, sear diagonally sliced linguiça sausage until browned.
Assemble each sandwich: Place one toasted bread slice on an oven-safe plate. Layer with thin ham slices and seared linguiça. Top with another toasted bread slice.
Cover each sandwich completely with cheese slices.
Bake: Place sandwiches in a preheated oven at 200°C (390°F) for 5-7 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Fry eggs: While sandwiches bake, fry 4 eggs sunny-side up, ensuring yolks are runny.
Serve: Carefully transfer each hot, cheesy sandwich to a clean serving plate. Top each with a fried egg. Generously ladle warm sauce around the base. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Potato, Bacon, and Swiss Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of Creamy Potato, Bacon, and Swiss Gratin is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The gratin, served as a thick square slice, boasts a rich golden-brown, bubbly crust on top, indicating its perfectly baked finish. Visible through the crust are hints of melted, slightly browned Swiss cheese. The side profile reveals distinct, tender layers of thinly sliced potatoes, interspersed with savory, crispy pieces of smoked bacon, vibrant red halved cherry tomatoes, and bright yellow corn kernels, all bound together by a creamy, luscious cheese sauce. The internal layers show a soft, moist texture contrasting with the crisp exterior. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green chives or parsley garnishes the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The plate sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting warmth. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 1 kg, peeled and thinly sliced (about 2-3 mm thick)

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Lightly butter a 20x30 cm baking dish or four individual gratin dishes.
Cook bacon lardons in a large skillet over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Drain all but 15 ml of bacon fat from the skillet.
Add butter to the skillet with reserved bacon fat. Melt over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
Stir in flour to create a roux. Cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in heavy cream. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Remove from heat. Stir in half of the grated Swiss cheese, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Stir until cheese is melted and sauce is smooth.

Arrange a layer of thinly sliced potatoes in the prepared baking dish. Top with one-third of the cooked bacon, one-third of the halved tomatoes, and one-third of the corn. Pour one-third of the cheese sauce evenly over the layer.
Repeat layering twice more, ending with a final layer of potatoes. Pour remaining sauce over the top.
Sprinkle remaining Swiss cheese over the top.
Bake for 45-55 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and the top is golden brown and bubbly. Insert a knife into the center to check potato tenderness.
Let gratin rest for 10 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chives or parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork, Shrimp, and Mushroom Risotto with Rosemary Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy risotto is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The risotto has a fluid, flowing consistency, not stiff or mounded. Diced, browned pork chunks and pink, tender shrimp are visibly integrated throughout the creamy, pale golden rice, along with earthy slices of sautéed mushroom. A scattering of golden, crispy roasted potato cubes, infused with fragrant rosemary and garlic, crowns the top of the risotto, providing textural contrast. The dish is garnished simply with a few fresh oregano leaves. The overall color palette is warm and inviting, with rich browns, tender pinks, and vibrant greens against the creamy base. The plate is placed on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard restaurant flatware, under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of dry white wine.
Offer crusty bread on the side.
instructions: Dice potatoes into 1 cm cubes. Toss with 15ml olive oil, half the chopped rosemary, salt, and pepper. Roast at 200°C for 25-30 minutes until golden and crispy.
Dice pork into 2 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear pork until browned on all sides. Remove pork from pan.
Add shrimp to the same pan. Cook 2-3 minutes until pink. Remove shrimp.
Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the pan. Add diced onion. Sauté 5 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir 2 minutes to toast grains until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until fully absorbed.

Add a ladle of hot broth to the rice. Stir constantly until liquid is absorbed. Continue adding broth, one ladle at a time, stirring until absorbed, for 18-20 minutes. The risotto should be creamy and al dente.
Stir in seared pork, sliced mushrooms, and remaining chopped rosemary. Cook 5 minutes, adding more broth if needed.
Remove from heat. Stir in butter and grated Parmesan cheese. This step is called mantecatura. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Let rest 2 minutes.
Ladle risotto onto plates. Top with crispy rosemary potatoes. Garnish with fresh oregano if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Sausage and Potato Gratin with Cheddar and Caramelized Onion
recipes.visual_description: A generous, rectangular slice of Sausage and Potato Gratin is centrally placed on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The gratin showcases distinct, tender layers of thinly sliced potatoes, rich caramelized onions, and savory crumbled sausage. The top crust of the gratin is a beautiful golden-brown, with bubbly, melted cheddar cheese and crispy, browned edges. A light sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley adds a pop of color and freshness. The dish appears comforting and substantial, with visible creamy sauce binding the layers. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, set within a modern bistro ambiance. A neatly folded cotton napkin is positioned to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the gratin's inviting textures and warm colors, with a subtle, blurred background focusing attention entirely on the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a fresh green salad
Accompany with crusty bread
instructions: Prepare onions: Melt butter and olive oil in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add thinly sliced onions. Cook slowly for 25-30 minutes until deeply caramelized and tender. Stir occasionally.
Cook sausage: While onions caramelize, brown sausage meat, removed from casings, in a separate pan over medium-high heat. Break it into small pieces. Drain excess fat. Set aside.
Prepare cream mixture: In a medium saucepan, combine heavy cream, milk, minced garlic, chopped thyme, grated nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Heat gently until warm; do not boil.
Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Lightly butter a 23x33 cm baking dish.
Layer gratin: Arrange a single layer of thinly sliced potatoes (2-3mm thick) in the prepared dish. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Add fillings: Sprinkle half of the caramelized onions over the potatoes. Distribute half of the cooked sausage over the onions. Sprinkle with one-third of the grated cheddar cheese.
Repeat layering: Add another layer of potatoes. Season. Top with remaining onions and sausage. Sprinkle with another third of cheddar. Add the final layer of potatoes.
Pour cream: Slowly pour the warm cream mixture evenly over the potatoes. Ensure liquid covers most of the potatoes.
Bake: Cover the baking dish loosely with foil. Bake for 45 minutes.

Finish baking: Remove foil. Sprinkle remaining cheddar cheese over the top. If using, sprinkle breadcrumbs. Bake uncovered for another 25-35 minutes, or until potatoes are tender, and cheese is bubbly and golden brown.
Rest: Let the gratin rest for 10-15 minutes before serving. This allows it to set.
notes: Ensure potatoes are sliced uniformly for even cooking.
Resting the gratin after baking helps it set and makes serving easier.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Potato & Bacon Croquettes with Fresh Tomato-Corn Relish
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Three golden-brown, cylindrical potato and bacon croquettes, each approximately 7 cm long, are arranged slightly offset from the plate's center. Their crispy exteriors show a rich, even golden hue. A small amount of melted Swiss cheese peeks subtly from one end of a croquette, indicating its creamy interior. Beside the croquettes, a vibrant mound of fresh tomato-corn relish is spooned. The relish features small, bright red diced tomatoes, plump yellow corn kernels, and finely chopped green parsley, creating a fresh, colorful contrast. The overall presentation is clean and organized, with moderate negative space. A few extra finely chopped parsley sprigs are scattered lightly over the croquettes as a garnish. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple light wooden table surface. Standard silver flatware is neatly placed beside the plate, and a folded cotton napkin rests nearby. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, unobtrusive background.
instructions: Peel potatoes. Cut into 2 cm chunks. Boil in salted water until tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain potatoes well. Mash with butter and milk until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside to cool completely.
Cook bacon in a dry pan over medium heat until very crispy. Drain on paper towel. Finely chop the crispy bacon.
Dice Swiss cheese into 1.5 cm cubes.
Add chopped bacon to the cooled mashed potato. Mix thoroughly.
Take approximately 50g of potato mixture. Flatten in your palm. Place one Swiss cheese cube in the center. Form into a cylindrical croquette, about 6-7 cm long.
Prepare a breading station: one shallow dish with flour, one with beaten eggs, and one with panko breadcrumbs.
Dredge each croquette first in flour, shaking off excess. Then dip in beaten egg, allowing excess to drip off. Finally, roll thoroughly in panko breadcrumbs, ensuring a complete, even coating.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or Dutch oven to 175°C (350°F).
Fry croquettes in batches, 3-4 minutes per batch, until golden brown and crispy. Ensure internal cheese is melted. Drain on a wire rack lined with paper towel.
For the relish: finely dice cherry tomatoes and red onion.
If using fresh corn, blanch kernels in boiling water for 1 minute, then drain. If frozen, thaw.
Combine diced tomato, corn, red onion, chopped fresh parsley, and lime juice in a bowl. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot croquettes immediately with a generous spoonful of fresh tomato-corn relish.
notes: For best results, ensure croquettes are chilled for at least 30 minutes before frying to help them hold their shape.

recipes.recipe_name: Ham and Gruyere Sandwich with Potato Rosti and Fried Egg
recipes.visual_description: A single portion is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A golden-brown, diagonally cut sourdough sandwich forms the centerpiece, revealing layers of thinly sliced smoked ham and melted Gruyere. A rich, creamy béchamel sauce cascades over the top, lightly browned, with a delicate crust of grated cheese. Perched atop the sandwich is a perfectly fried egg, its vibrant yellow yolk glistening, framed by crisp white edges. Adjacent, a golden, circular potato rosti, with finely grated, crispy edges, offers textural contrast. Finely chopped fresh chives are scattered over the egg and rosti, adding a touch of verdant color. The arrangement is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple, light wooden table, a folded white cotton napkin, and natural, even lighting, creating a modern bistro atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Good quality smoked ham, thinly sliced
Gruyere cheese, grated or thinly sliced
Fresh chives or parsley, finely chopped

instructions: Prepare Béchamel Sauce: Melt 30 g butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in 30 g flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to form a roux. Gradually whisk in 500 ml warm milk. Continue whisking until sauce thickens and is smooth. Season with nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Remove from heat. Keep warm.

Prepare Potato Rosti: Grate 600 g peeled potatoes using a coarse grater. Place grated potatoes in a clean kitchen towel. Squeeze out as much excess liquid as possible. Season potatoes with salt and pepper. Heat 30 g butter and 30 ml vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Divide potato mixture into 4 equal portions. Form each portion into a flat, round patty, about 1.5 cm thick. Carefully place rosti patties into the hot pan. Cook for 6-8 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy. Transfer cooked rosti to a plate lined with paper towel. Keep warm.

Assemble and Cook Sandwiches: Preheat a large non-stick pan or griddle over medium heat. Spread softened butter on one side of each bread slice. Spread Dijon mustard on the unbuttered side of 4 bread slices. Layer ham and grated Gruyere cheese evenly on the mustard-spread bread slices. Top with remaining bread slices, buttered side out. Cook sandwiches in the preheated pan for 3-4 minutes per side, until bread is golden brown and cheese is melted. Remove sandwiches from pan. Carefully open each sandwich. Pour a generous amount of béchamel sauce inside, ensuring even coverage over the ham and cheese. Close sandwiches. Spoon remaining béchamel sauce over the top of each sandwich. Sprinkle with extra grated Gruyere. Place sandwiches back in the pan or under a preheated grill (broiler) for 2-3 minutes, until béchamel is bubbly and cheese is melted and slightly golden.

Fry Eggs: While sandwiches finish, heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a separate non-stick pan over medium heat. Crack 4 eggs into the hot oil. Cook for 2-3 minutes, until whites are set and yolks are still runny. Season with salt and pepper.

Plate and Serve: Cut each sandwich diagonally in half. Place one sandwich half on each of 4 plates. Place one potato rosti next to the sandwich half. Carefully place one fried egg on top of the sandwich half. Garnish with finely chopped chives or parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Mexican Chicken and Potato Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, savory Mexican Chicken and Potato Skillet on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. Golden-brown seared chicken chunks are nestled among tender, rustic 2 cm potato cubes. A rich, reddish-brown tomato-based sauce coats the chicken and potatoes, flecked with dark black beans and bright yellow corn kernels. Finely minced green jalapeño and red onion add texture and color. A generous sprinkle of crumbled white Cotija cheese and vibrant green chopped fresh cilantro adorns the top, providing beautiful contrast. The dish is a single, refined restaurant portion. The plate rests on a simple wooden table with natural, even light. Beside it, a neatly folded cotton napkin and warm corn tortillas are arranged. A lime wedge is placed on the plate's side. The background is a slightly blurred, casual restaurant setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping.
Offer extra lime wedges for fresh acidity.
Serve with a side of Mexican rice.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Season chicken chunks with salt, pepper, smoked paprika, cumin, and oregano.
Sear chicken in the hot skillet until browned on all sides. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced red onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and jalapeño. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced potatoes. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly softened.
Pour in diced tomatoes, chicken stock, and hot sauce. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to the skillet. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C) and potatoes are tender.
Stir in rinsed black beans and corn kernels. Cook for another 5 minutes, uncovered, allowing sauce to thicken slightly.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Garnish generously with crumbled Cotija cheese and fresh chopped cilantro.
Serve immediately with lime wedges.
notes: Adjust hot sauce quantity to desired spice level.
For a richer flavor, use fire-roasted diced tomatoes.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Bacon Potato Hash and Corn Tomato Salsa
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown with a lightly crisped skin, rests beside a mound of rustic bacon potato hash on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is presented as a whole piece. The hash features diced, roasted potatoes with visible crispy bacon bits and melted, glistening Swiss cheese interwoven throughout. A vibrant, fresh corn tomato salsa, bursting with red tomato halves and yellow corn kernels, is spooned artfully over the chicken. Bright green chopped parsley is scattered as a garnish over both the chicken and hash. The plate is centered on a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating a professional yet inviting casual dining atmosphere. The background is minimal, featuring subtle restaurant elements.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Season chicken breasts generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 4 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to oven. Bake 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest chicken 5 minutes before serving.
While chicken bakes, cook bacon in a separate large skillet over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Drain all but 15ml bacon fat from skillet.
Add diced potatoes to the skillet with bacon fat. Cook 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender and browned.
Add diced onion and minced garlic to potatoes. Cook 5 minutes until softened.
Stir in cooked bacon and butter. Season hash with salt and pepper. Remove from heat. Sprinkle shredded Swiss cheese over hot hash. Cover to melt cheese.
In a medium bowl, combine halved tomatoes, corn kernels, and half of the chopped parsley. Add lime juice. Season with salt and pepper. Toss gently to combine.

To plate, spoon a generous portion of bacon potato hash onto each plate. Place one seared chicken breast beside the hash. Top chicken with a spoonful of corn tomato salsa. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Medallions with Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate set on a simple wooden table. A single seared beef medallion, thick and medium-rare with a rich brown crust, rests centrally atop a generous, free-flowing mound of creamy, golden-brown mushroom risotto. The risotto shows visible specks of finely diced onion and tender, earthy sliced mushrooms, with a fluid consistency. A small, artfully placed cluster of golden-crisp, thin julienned potato hay garnishes the beef, adding a contrasting texture. Fresh green chopped parsley and tiny sprigs of thyme are scattered over the beef and risotto, providing vibrant color and freshness. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. Standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin are placed beside the plate on the modern bistro-style table surface. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors.
instructions: Prepare Crispy Potato Hay: Rinse julienned potatoes under cold water until water runs clear. Pat very dry with paper towels. Heat 2 cm olive oil in a deep pan to 170°C. Fry potatoes in small batches until golden brown and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels. Season with salt.

Start Mushroom Risotto: In a large, heavy-bottomed pot, heat 15ml olive oil and 20g butter over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until softened and liquid evaporates, about 8-10 minutes.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir for 2 minutes until rice edges become translucent. Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.

Begin adding warm beef broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly. Wait until each ladleful is almost fully absorbed before adding the next. Continue for 18-20 minutes until rice is creamy and al dente. The risotto should be fluid, not dry.
Remove risotto from heat. Stir in remaining 40g cold butter, grated Parmesan cheese, and half of the chopped parsley. Season with salt and pepper. Cover and let rest for 2 minutes.
Sear Beef Medallions: While risotto rests, pat beef medallions dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a heavy skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Add beef medallions to the hot skillet. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to desired doneness.
Remove beef from skillet. Let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.
Plate the Dish: Spoon a generous portion of mushroom risotto onto the center of each white porcelain plate. Place one seared beef medallion on top of the risotto.
Garnish the beef and risotto with a small mound of crispy potato hay. Sprinkle with fresh thyme and remaining chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork & Chipotle Black Bean Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Pork & Chipotle Black Bean Rice Bowl is presented in a clean white porcelain bowl. Fluffy white long-grain rice forms the base, topped with a generous portion of rich, dark braised pork and black bean mixture. The pork is tender, shredded into natural chunks. The black beans are plump, coated in a deep reddish-brown chipotle-infused sauce, with visible specks of diced onion and minced garlic. The dish is brightly garnished with a cascade of fresh, verdant chopped cilantro leaves. A vibrant green lime wedge rests on the rim. The color palette is warm and inviting: deep browns, bright white, and fresh green. The presentation is clean, approachable, and balanced with moderate negative space. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table surface with a natural cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas on the side.
Offer extra hot sauce or salsa verde for individual preference.
Serve with a side of pickled red onions or a simple cabbage slaw.

ingredients.name: Chipotle in adobo sauce
ingredients.quantity: 2-3 chilies, minced, plus 1 tbsp adobo sauce

instructions: Season pork chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear pork until browned on all sides. Remove pork.
Add remaining 15ml oil to the pot. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, chipotle, cumin, and oregano. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Return pork to the pot. Add 250ml chicken stock and hot sauce. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and braise for 1.5-2 hours, or until pork is very tender and easily shreds with a fork.
While pork braises, prepare rice. Rinse rice under cold water until water runs clear.

Combine rinsed rice with 500ml chicken stock and a pinch of salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-18 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Fluff with a fork.
Once pork is tender, remove it from the pot. Shred the pork using two forks.
Add rinsed black beans to the pot with the braising liquid. Simmer uncovered for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly.
Return shredded pork to the black bean mixture. Stir to combine. Taste and adjust seasoning.
To serve, scoop a generous portion of rice into a bowl. Top with the pork and black bean mixture.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro and a lime wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Pork Carnitas Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of a vibrant Spicy Pork Carnitas Bowl is presented in a clean, matte white porcelain bowl, centered on a rustic, light-toned wooden table. The bowl holds distinct, well-defined sections. Golden-brown, crisped pork carnitas are arranged in substantial, irregular chunks, showcasing varied textures. Adjacent, fluffy, reddish-orange Mexican rice provides warm color. Beside the rice, glossy black beans, slightly mashed, add a deep, rich hue. The dish is garnished with scattered bright green chopped cilantro and finely diced red onion, plus a lime wedge. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. A natural cotton napkin, a small traditional Mexican salsa bowl with red salsa, and warm corn tortillas complete the authentic setting. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for wrapping.
Offer a variety of fresh salsas, such as pico de gallo or salsa verde.
Provide pickled red onions or jalapeños as a tangy accompaniment.

ingredients.name: Chipotle peppers in adobo sauce
ingredients.quantity: 2-3 peppers, minced, plus 15 ml adobo sauce

instructions: Prepare Pork Carnitas: Place pork chunks in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven. Add chopped yellow onion, smashed garlic, bay leaves, cumin, oregano, salt, pepper, and water or broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 2-3 hours, or until pork is very tender and easily shreddable.

Shred and Crisp Pork: Remove pork from liquid. Skim fat from cooking liquid and reserve about 250 ml. Shred pork using two forks. In a large skillet, heat lard or oil over medium-high heat. Add shredded pork in a single layer. Cook, stirring occasionally, until pork is golden-brown and crispy in spots. Add a splash of reserved cooking liquid if pork becomes too dry.

Cook Mexican Rice: Rinse rice until water runs clear. In a medium saucepan, heat 15 ml oil over medium heat. Add rice and toast for 2 minutes. Stir in 600 ml water, 5 g salt, and a pinch of cumin. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15-18 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.

Prepare Spicy Black Beans: In a small saucepan, combine drained black beans, minced chipotle peppers, adobo sauce, and 125 ml water. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until beans are heated through and flavors meld. Mash lightly with a fork for a creamier texture, if desired.

Assemble Bowls: Divide Mexican rice among four individual white porcelain bowls. Arrange crispy pork carnitas chunks next to the rice. Spoon spicy black beans alongside. Garnish each bowl with fresh cilantro, finely diced red onion, and a lime wedge. Serve with optional hot sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Spicy Tomato-Mushroom Ragu
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate set on a simple wooden table. A perfectly seared, golden-brown chicken breast, cut into thick medallions, is positioned slightly off-center. Beside it, a generous mound of al dente rigatoni or penne pasta is tossed in a rich, rustic tomato-mushroom ragu. The ragu is a deep reddish-brown with visible chunks of sautéed mushrooms and a hint of vibrant red from the tomatoes. Randomly placed over the chicken and pasta are irregular pieces of creamy white fresh mozzarella, some slightly melted from the heat. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered over the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with a focus on natural textures and colors. A fork and knife are placed beside the plate on a folded white linen napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, creating a professional yet approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping in the ragu.
A simple side salad with vinaigrette complements the richness.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 4-6 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the same skillet. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are browned and tender.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken stock, hot sauce, oregano, and red pepper flakes (if using). Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer ragu for 15-20 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and sauce to thicken slightly. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
While ragu simmers, cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Slice chicken breasts into thick medallions or keep whole. Return chicken to the ragu. Heat through for 2-3 minutes.
Toss cooked pasta with the ragu. Ensure pasta is well coated.
Serve pasta and ragu onto plates. Place a seared chicken piece on top or beside the pasta.
Garnish each serving with torn fresh mozzarella and fresh basil leaves.
notes: Adjust hot sauce quantity to your preferred spice level.
For extra richness, a splash of heavy cream can be added to the ragu at the end.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Chicken and Rice Skillet with Bacon and Swiss
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Savory Chicken and Rice Skillet is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a rustic yet refined appeal. The golden-brown chicken chunks, roughly 3 cm, are nestled amongst fluffy, savory long-grain white rice. Diced potatoes, approximately 1.5 cm cubes, are visible, along with vibrant red diced tomatoes and bright yellow corn kernels, adding color and texture. A blanket of melted, bubbly Swiss cheese, with slight golden-brown spots, covers the top, creating an inviting crust. Crispy bacon bits are sprinkled over the cheese and throughout the dish. Freshly chopped green parsley provides a final pop of color. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a casual silver fork and knife and a neatly folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and rich colors, with a soft, out-of-focus background suggesting a modern bistro setting. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space, presenting a professional but approachable meal.
instructions: Dice bacon into 1 cm pieces. Cook bacon in a large oven-safe skillet over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Reserve 15 ml bacon fat in skillet. Discard excess fat.

Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper. Add chicken to skillet with bacon fat. Sear chicken 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.

Dice onion into 1 cm pieces. Dice potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes. Add onion and potatoes to skillet. Sauté 8-10 minutes until softened. Mince garlic. Add garlic and smoked paprika. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rice to skillet. Stir 2 minutes to toast lightly.

Pour in chicken broth and diced tomatoes with their liquid. Bring mixture to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover skillet. Simmer 15-20 minutes, or until rice is nearly tender and liquid is mostly absorbed.
Stir in frozen corn kernels and cooked chicken chunks. Stir in most of the crispy bacon, reserving some for garnish. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Sprinkle shredded Swiss cheese evenly over the top of the skillet mixture. Cover skillet. Cook 5 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Chop fresh parsley. Garnish skillet with reserved crispy bacon and chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pickled Beetroot & Wild Rocket Salad
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist, natural presentation of a vibrant salad on a clean, off-white ceramic plate. Thin rounds of deep purple pickled beetroot form the base, artfully arranged. A loose, organic mound of dark green wild rocket and brighter green chopped beetroot leaves is gently placed atop. Translucent, thinly sliced pickled red onion is interspersed throughout. A light scattering of golden-brown crispy bacon crumbs and toasted pumpkin seeds adds textural contrast. The dressing subtly coats the ingredients, providing a delicate sheen. The plate rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. A simple, undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is loosely draped nearby. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, and the background is clean and minimalist, with a blurred hint of natural elements, suggesting an eco-conscious setting. All components are clearly visible and artistically distributed.
instructions: Prepare pickling liquid: In a saucepan, combine apple cider vinegar, water, maple syrup, salt, and black peppercorns. Bring to a boil, then remove from heat.
Slice vegetables: Peel and thinly slice beetroots into rounds or small wedges. Thinly slice the red onion.

Pickle vegetables: Place sliced beetroot and red onion in a heatproof jar. Pour hot pickling liquid over them. Ensure vegetables are submerged. Let cool completely, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or ideally overnight.
Cook bacon: Finely dice the streaky bacon. Cook in a dry pan over medium heat until very crispy. Drain on paper towel. Set aside.
Prepare greens: Wash and thoroughly dry the wild rocket and any available beetroot leaves. Roughly chop the beetroot leaves.

Make dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together Dijon mustard, 1 tablespoon of the pickling liquid (or fresh apple cider vinegar), salt, and black pepper. Slowly drizzle in the olive oil, whisking constantly until the dressing emulsifies.
Assemble salad: In a large bowl, gently combine the pickled beetroot, pickled red onion, wild rocket, and chopped beetroot leaves. Add half of the prepared dressing and toss lightly to coat.
Plate and serve: Arrange the salad on individual plates. Sprinkle with crispy bacon bits and toasted pumpkin seeds. Drizzle with the remaining dressing.

recipes.recipe_name: Mini Entremet Citron-Caramel
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly formed Mini Entremet Citron-Caramel rests centered on an elegant, pristine white porcelain dessert plate with a subtle gold rim, set upon a polished white marble surface. The entremet, approximately 7cm in diameter and 5cm in height, boasts a flawless, reflective mirror glaze in a delicate, warm caramel hue, showcasing its smooth, architectural form. The glaze shimmers under dramatic professional lighting, creating subtle shadows that enhance its three-dimensional presence. A very thin, abstract caramel tuile, translucent and delicate, is artfully placed atop the entremet, adding a precise, elevated crunch and visual interest. A scattering of finely julienned, translucent candied lemon zest strips, few in number, are precisely placed near the entremet's base, providing a subtle pop of vibrant yellow color and texture contrast. Abundant negative space surrounds the dessert, emphasizing its sophisticated simplicity and the meticulous execution of each component. The overall presentation is ultra-minimalist, showcasing the pastry as a jewel-like creation of haute patisserie, with every element positioned with purpose and artistic intent.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served individually as a post-meal dessert, often accompanied by a small espresso or digestif.
Presented on a pristine white plate, emphasizing the pastry's refined aesthetics.

ingredients.name: Heavy cream (35% fat), cold, whipped to soft peaks

instructions: Prepare Candied Lemon Zest: Peel lemon zest in long strips. Blanch zest in boiling water 3 times for 1 minute, refreshing water each time. Combine sugar and water in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Add blanched zest. Simmer gently until translucent. Cool. Cut into fine julienne strips.

Prepare Lemon Crémeux: Hydrate gelatin in cold water. Whisk lemon juice, zest, egg yolks, and sugar in a saucepan. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens (82°C). Remove from heat. Stir in squeezed gelatin. Emulsify in cold butter using an immersion blender until smooth. Pour into a small silicone mold (e.g., 4 x 3cm rounds for inserts). Freeze until solid.

Prepare Almond Dacquoise: Preheat oven to 170°C. Sift icing sugar and almond flour together. Whip egg whites to soft peaks. Gradually add granulated sugar, whip to firm, glossy meringue. Gently fold in dry ingredients. Pipe or spread onto parchment paper to a 5mm thickness. Bake 12-15 minutes until lightly golden. Cool. Cut out 4 rounds (approx. 5cm diameter).

Prepare Light Caramel Mousse: Hydrate gelatin in cold water. In a saucepan, make a dry caramel with 100g sugar. Once amber, carefully add 30ml water (be cautious, it will steam). Stir until smooth. Heat 50ml cream to a simmer. In a separate bowl, whisk egg yolks. Slowly temper hot cream into egg yolks. Pour mixture back into saucepan with caramel. Cook over low heat, stirring, until thickened (82°C). Remove from heat. Stir in squeezed gelatin until dissolved. Cool mixture to 30°C. Gently fold in whipped cream in two additions. Fill mousse molds (e.g., 4 x 7cm silicone sphere or dome molds) halfway with mousse. Place a frozen lemon crémeux insert in the center. Top with more mousse. Press a dacquoise disc onto the bottom. Smooth. Freeze overnight until completely solid.

Prepare Neutral Mirror Glaze: Hydrate gelatin in cold water. Combine water, sugar, and glucose syrup in a saucepan. Bring to 103°C. Remove from heat. Stir in condensed milk. Add chopped white chocolate and squeezed gelatin. Let stand 5 minutes. Blend with an immersion blender, avoiding air bubbles. Strain. Cool to 35-38°C for glazing.

Glaze Entremets: Remove frozen entremets from molds. Place on a wire rack over a baking sheet. Pour warm glaze evenly over each entremet, ensuring full coverage. Let excess drip off. Transfer carefully to a serving plate using an offset spatula.

Prepare Caramel Tuile: Combine sugar and water in a small saucepan. Heat until sugar dissolves and caramelizes to an amber color. Do not stir. Pour a small amount onto a silicone mat or parchment paper. Quickly spread thinly with the back of a spoon to create delicate, abstract shapes. Cool completely. Carefully peel off.

Plate: Place one glazed mini entremet on each plate. Arrange a delicate caramel tuile artfully on top or beside the entremet. Sprinkle a few candied lemon zest julienne strips around the base for color and texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tom Kha Shiitake Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Tom Kha Shiitake Pasta is presented in a simple, deep ceramic bowl, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The pasta is naturally coiled, coated in a luscious, pale cream-colored coconut sauce. Tender, sliced brown shiitake mushrooms are generously interspersed throughout the pasta. A vibrant sprinkle of chopped green cilantro leaves and a few thin slices of bright red chili rest on top, providing a pop of color and freshness. The dish is inviting, showcasing the smooth texture of the sauce and the distinct shapes of the ingredients. The setting is a homely family kitchen, with warm, natural light illuminating the dish. A casual cloth napkin is loosely placed nearby. The overall presentation is comforting and authentic, reflecting a home-cooked meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small bowl of chili flakes or extra lime wedges on the side for personal adjustment of spice and sourness.
Offer small individual ceramic bowls or deep plates, typical for noodle or curry dishes.
instructions: Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain and set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pan or wok over medium heat.
Add sliced shallots and minced garlic. Sauté until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add sliced shiitake mushrooms. Cook until softened and lightly browned, about 3-4 minutes.
Stir in bruised lemongrass, sliced galangal, and torn kaffir lime leaves. Cook for 1 minute until aromatic.
Pour in coconut milk and vegetable broth. Add soy sauce and brown sugar. Stir to combine.
Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low and cook for 5-7 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Carefully remove and discard lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves from the sauce.
Stir in lime juice.
Add the cooked pasta to the sauce. Toss to coat evenly.
Serve immediately in individual bowls. Garnish with fresh cilantro and thinly sliced red chilies.
notes: For a spicier dish, add a small amount of Thai red curry paste with the shallots and garlic.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Shiitake Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Creamy Shiitake Pasta rests in a rustic, light beige ceramic bowl on a worn wooden dining table. Tender fettuccine noodles are loosely swirled, coated in a rich, pale cream sauce. Thinly sliced, sautéed shiitake mushrooms, with their distinctive brown caps, are distributed throughout the pasta and gently piled on top, showcasing their meaty texture. Hints of finely diced, softened yellow onion and minced garlic are visible within the creamy sauce. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley provides a contrasting pop of color and freshness. The dish appears comforting and substantial. A simple fork is placed beside the bowl. The background is a soft, warm blur of a lived-in kitchen, illuminated by cozy, natural light.
instructions: Cook pasta according to package directions. Reserve 125 ml pasta water before draining.
While pasta cooks, clean shiitake mushrooms. Remove stems. Slice caps thinly.
Dice yellow onion finely. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add sliced shiitake mushrooms to the pan. Sauté until browned and tender, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, allowing liquid to reduce slightly.
Stir in plant-based cream and nutritional yeast. Mix well. Season with salt and black pepper.
Add cooked pasta to the pan with the sauce. Toss to coat evenly.
If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, 30 ml at a time, until desired consistency is reached.
Chop fresh parsley. Stir half into the pasta.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Rigatoni al Forno con Mozzarella e Basilico
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Rigatoni al Forno presented in a pristine white ceramic baking dish. The substantial rigatoni tubes are coated in a rich, slow-cooked San Marzano tomato sauce, their ridges perfectly capturing the flavor. Melted fresh mozzarella, torn into irregular chunks, forms golden-brown, bubbly pockets across the top, interspersed with creamy white stretches. A scattering of vibrant green, fresh basil leaves provides a stark, aromatic contrast. A light dusting of finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano adds a delicate finish.
