Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, red bell pepper, green bell pepper, and minced jalapeño to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until vegetables soften, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic, ground cumin, smoked paprika, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Add rinsed rice to the skillet. Stir well to coat rice with spices and vegetables. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring.
Pour in gluten-free beer or chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Add diced tomatoes and 500ml chicken broth. Stir well.
Return seared chicken to the skillet. Bring mixture to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover skillet tightly. Cook for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed.
Stir in rinsed and drained black beans. Cook, uncovered, for 5 more minutes, or until heated through and liquid is mostly absorbed. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove skillet from heat. Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro.
notes: This recipe is naturally gluten-free when using gluten-free beer or chicken broth.
Adjust chili amount for desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo y Frijoles
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo served on a wide white porcelain plate. Two whole golden-brown seared chicken thighs rest atop a vibrant bed of fluffy long-grain rice. The rice is studded with charred yellow corn kernels, earthy black beans, and softened red tomato cubes. Fresh green cilantro leaves are scattered across the top. The chicken skin is crisp and mahogany-toned. A bright lime wedge sits on the side. The plate is positioned on a rustic dark wood table next to a folded white cotton napkin. A small terracotta bowl of salsa verde sits in the background. Natural side lighting highlights the steam and textures of the grains and poultry.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Provide extra lime wedges for acidity
Accompany with fresh salsa verde or pico de gallo
instructions: Season chicken with salt, pepper, and smoked paprika.
Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip chicken and brown the other side.
Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
Add onion, bell pepper, and garlic to the same pan.
Sauté for 3 minutes until softened.
Add rice to the pan.
Toast rice for 2 minutes until opaque and fragrant.
Stir in tomatoes, corn, black beans, and cumin.
Pour in chicken stock and bring to a simmer.
Place chicken thighs back on top of the rice mixture.
Cover pan with a tight lid.
Reduce heat to low.
Cook for 20 minutes.
Check chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat and let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh cilantro.
notes: Use bone-in thighs to keep the meat moist during braising
Do not stir the rice once the chicken is added to ensure even steaming
Ensure the pan lid is tight to prevent moisture loss

recipes.recipe_name: Peanut Butter Caramel Tartlets
recipes.visual_description: A single Peanut Butter Caramel Tartlet rests on a simple, everyday ceramic plate with a subtle, natural imperfection. The tartlet, about 10 cm in diameter, has a golden-brown, flaky pastry shell. The interior is filled with a light, creamy peanut butter mixture, slightly mounded. A rich, amber salted caramel sauce is generously drizzled over the peanut butter, allowing some to pool and some to cascade down the sides. Thin ribbons of glossy white chocolate are artfully drizzled over the caramel, creating a contrasting visual. A light dusting of cocoa powder provides a subtle, matte finish and a hint of dark contrast. The tartlet is presented casually, slightly off-center on the plate, on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple, folded cloth napkin and a standard dessert fork are placed beside the plate, suggesting a relaxed family meal. Warm, soft light from a nearby kitchen window illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and natural colors of the tartlet.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a casual dessert after a family meal.
Enjoy with a glass of cold milk or a cup of coffee.
instructions: Combine flour, cold butter, and salt in a bowl. Rub butter into flour until crumbly. Mix in caster sugar. Add egg yolk and mix until dough forms. Add cold water if dough is too dry. Form into a disc, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.

Preheat oven to 180°C. Roll out dough thinly. Cut circles and press into four 10 cm tartlet tins. Prick bottoms with a fork. Line with parchment paper, fill with baking beans. Bake for 15 minutes. Remove beans and paper. Bake for another 5-7 minutes until golden. Cool completely.

In a saucepan, combine granulated sugar and water. Heat over medium-high until sugar dissolves, then boil without stirring until deep amber. Remove from heat. Slowly whisk in warm heavy cream. Stir in sea salt. Let cool slightly.
In a bowl, cream softened butter and icing sugar until light. Beat in peanut butter until smooth. Gradually add milk, mixing until creamy and spreadable.
Heat heavy cream in a small saucepan until simmering. Remove from heat. Add chopped white chocolate. Let sit for 1 minute, then whisk until smooth.
Spoon peanut butter filling into cooled tartlet shells, spreading evenly. Drizzle generously with salted caramel. Drizzle with white chocolate. Dust lightly with cocoa powder.
notes: Ensure tartlet shells are fully cooled before filling to prevent melting.
Caramel can be made ahead and gently reheated.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Tuna Niçoise Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served on a clean white porcelain plate set on a light oak bistro table. The focal point is a thick, whole rectangular block of seared tuna, showing a thin grey seared edge and a vibrant deep pink center. Beside the tuna, two halves of a soft-boiled egg reveal jammy, translucent orange yolks. The salad consists of vibrant red cherry tomato halves, thick cucumber medallions, and delicate purple red onion rounds. The vegetables are lightly coated in a pale, creamy lemon-mayonnaise dressing. Fresh green parsley is scattered naturally across the plate. The lighting is bright and natural, coming from the side to highlight the textures of the seared fish and glossy egg yolks.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices
Pair with a chilled dry Rosé from Provence
Provide a small bowl of Niçoise olives on the side
instructions: Boil water in a small pot. Add eggs and cook for 6 minutes and 30 seconds. Transfer eggs to ice water immediately. Peel and set aside.
Cut tuna loin into four thick 150g rectangular blocks.
Season tuna with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a heavy skillet over high heat.
Sear tuna for 45 seconds per side until a crust forms but the center remains rare.
Slice cucumber into 2cm thick medallions. Halve the cherry tomatoes. Thinly slice the red onion into rounds.
Whisk mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, and lemon juice in a small bowl until smooth.
Arrange cucumber medallions, tomatoes, and red onion on four plates.
Place one whole seared tuna block on each plate. Do not slice.
Halve the soft-boiled eggs and place next to the tuna.
Drizzle the mayonnaise dressing over the vegetables. Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure the tuna is sushi-grade for the best flavor and safety.
Dry the tuna loin thoroughly with paper towels before searing to achieve a better crust.
The eggs should be at room temperature before boiling to prevent cracking.

recipes.recipe_name: Brussels Sprout and Chickpea Masala
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, hearty Brussels Sprout and Chickpea Masala is presented in a deep, dark grey traditional Indian karahi, placed centrally on a simple light wooden table. The curry has a rich reddish-brown gravy, thick and fluid, with bright green halved Brussels sprouts and pale, firm chickpeas clearly visible throughout. The Brussels sprouts are tender-crisp, retaining their shape. A generous sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped coriander leaves garnishes the top, adding a pop of color. Beside the karahi, on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, a small mound of fluffy white basmati rice is artfully placed. A freshly baked, slightly charred naan bread is folded and placed on the side. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting from the top, creating soft shadows. The background is a subtly blurred modern bistro setting, suggesting a casual yet refined dining experience. Traditional Indian flatware is positioned beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with basmati rice, warm naan bread, or roti.
A side of cooling raita (yogurt dip) or pickled onions is a common accompaniment.
instructions: Halve Brussels sprouts. Rinse and drain canned chickpeas. Finely dice onion. Slit green chilies lengthwise. Crush Kasuri Methi.
Heat 30 ml vegetable oil in a large pot or karahi over medium heat.
Add 5 g cumin seeds. Let them splutter, about 10 seconds.
Add diced onion. Sauté until golden brown, 8-10 minutes.
Add 20 g ginger-garlic paste and slit green chilies. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add 3 g turmeric powder, 10 g coriander powder, and 5 g red chili powder. Stir for 30 seconds.
Pour in 400 g crushed tomatoes. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the oil separates from the masala, 8-10 minutes.
Add halved Brussels sprouts and 400 g chickpeas. Stir to coat well with the masala.
Pour in 250 ml water or vegetable broth. Add salt to taste. Stir.
Bring the curry to a simmer. Cover and cook for 10-12 minutes, or until Brussels sprouts are tender-crisp.
Stir in 5 g garam masala and 5 g crushed Kasuri Methi. Cook uncovered for 2 minutes.
Garnish generously with 30 g fresh chopped coriander.
Serve hot with basmati rice and naan bread.
notes: Adjust green chilies and red chili powder to control desired spice level.
For best flavor, allow the curry to rest for 15-20 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Supreme, Compressed Tomato, Roasted Garlic Emulsion
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly pan-seared chicken supreme, its skin a deep golden-brown and exquisitely crisp, rests with architectural precision on an expansive, pristine bone china plate. The chicken, presented as a whole piece, is positioned slightly off-center, allowing for abundant negative space. Adjacent to the chicken, two to three glossy, translucent rounds of compressed Roma tomato are artfully arranged, their vibrant red contrasting elegantly with the chicken's warm tones. Small, deliberate dots of the pale, creamy roasted garlic emulsion are strategically placed around the plate, adding visual interest and a subtle textural counterpoint. The dish is subtly garnished with a few delicate micro basil leaves. The setting is a luxurious white Carrara marble surface. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, lies nearby. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft, intentional shadows, highlighting the dish's refined textures. The background is ultra-minimalist, ensuring the focus remains solely on the meticulously composed main course.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Season chicken supremes generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil and butter in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken supremes skin-side down for 6-8 minutes until golden and crisp. Do not move chicken during searing.

Flip chicken. Add chicken stock to pan. Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Baste chicken occasionally. Remove from oven, rest for 5 minutes.

For the Compressed Tomato: Slice Roma tomatoes into 5 mm thick rounds. In a bowl, combine 15 ml olive oil and 5 g chopped fresh basil. Place tomato slices in a vacuum seal bag with the basil-infused oil. Vacuum seal tightly. If no vacuum sealer, place in a zip-top bag, remove as much air as possible. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

For the Roasted Garlic Emulsion: Roast garlic cloves (unpeeled) in a foil packet at 180°C for 20-25 minutes until very soft. Squeeze out roasted garlic pulp. In a blender, combine roasted garlic pulp, egg yolk, lemon juice, white wine vinegar, a pinch of salt. Blend until smooth. Slowly drizzle in neutral oil while blending until a creamy emulsion forms. Adjust seasoning.

To plate: Arrange 2-3 compressed tomato slices artfully on one side of a large, elegant plate. Place one rested chicken supreme next to the tomatoes. Dot the plate with small, precise quenelles or smears of the roasted garlic emulsion. Garnish with a few micro basil leaves or a drizzle of chive oil. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Lemon Chicken and Potato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Lemon Chicken and Potato Bake rests on a simple, round ceramic plate with a subtle, rustic glaze. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table in a cozy family kitchen. Golden-brown, irregularly shaped chicken chunks are nestled among tender, light brown potato wedges. A rich, creamy, pale yellow sauce lightly coats all components, pooling slightly at the base. Thin slices of bright yellow lemon are scattered among the dish, offering a pop of color. Fresh, vibrant green parsley leaves are casually sprinkled over the top. The textures are varied: slightly crisp edges on the chicken and potatoes, soft interiors, and a smooth, inviting sauce. A standard silver fork and knife are placed next to the plate. The scene is lit with warm, inviting light from kitchen fixtures, creating a comforting, lived-in atmosphere. The background is minimal, showing just a hint of the kitchen's natural clutter.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut chicken thighs into large, thick chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Peel potatoes. Cut into thick wedges or large chunks.
Slice onion into thin half-moons. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or baking dish on medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Do not cook through. Remove chicken.
Add sliced onion and minced garlic to the skillet. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes.
Deglaze with chicken stock. Scrape up any browned bits.
Stir in cream and juice of half a lemon. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Return chicken to the skillet. Add potato wedges. Stir to coat.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temp 75°C) and potatoes are tender.
Slice remaining half lemon into thin rounds.
Garnish with fresh parsley and lemon rounds before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Lemon Chicken with Roasted Potatoes and Caramelized Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Lemon Chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown seared chicken breast, cooked whole, is positioned centrally. Beside it, a cluster of roasted potato chunks, their skins lightly crisped and interiors fluffy, displays a warm golden hue. A generous mound of deeply caramelized onions, soft and rich brown, rests near the chicken. The creamy lemon sauce, a light ivory color, is elegantly drizzled over the chicken and gently pools around the base. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a light wooden table surface beside a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and warm colors.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold), peeled, cut into 2 cm chunks
Lemon, zest of whole, juice of half

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss potato chunks with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until golden and tender. Turn once during cooking.

While potatoes roast, heat 15ml olive oil and butter in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add sliced onions. Cook slowly for 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply golden brown and caramelized. Remove onions from pan and set aside.

Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Increase heat to medium-high in the same pan. Add chicken breasts. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add minced garlic to the pan. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Stir in heavy cream, lemon zest, and lemon juice. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 3-5 minutes, stirring, until sauce slightly thickens. Stir in fresh thyme leaves.
Return chicken breasts to the pan with the sauce. Simmer gently for 2 minutes to warm through. Stir in half of the chopped parsley.
Serve chicken immediately with roasted potatoes and caramelized onions. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Lemon Cream Sauce and Rosemary Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single seared chicken breast, golden-brown and plump, rests prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Beside it, a neat mound of crispy roasted potato cubes, their edges golden and slightly charred. The chicken is generously drizzled with a smooth, pale yellow lemon cream sauce. The plate is adorned with a few bright green chopped parsley leaves and a fresh lemon wedge. The overall composition is balanced with moderate negative space. The dish sits on a simple light wooden table. A white cotton napkin and classic silverware are placed to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and warm colors of the food, creating an inviting bistro-style presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Wash and cut potatoes into 2 cm cubes or wedges. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, pepper, and 1 sprig of rosemary leaves. Spread on a baking sheet.
Roast potatoes for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown and tender. Flip halfway through.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside on a plate, tent with foil.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the skillet. Add diced yellow onion and minced garlic. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in heavy cream and the juice of half a lemon. Add remaining rosemary sprig. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly.
Remove rosemary sprig from sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper, and more lemon juice if desired.
Plate roasted potatoes alongside chicken breast. Spoon lemon cream sauce over chicken and around the plate.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and a lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Lemon Chicken with Crispy Smashed Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Lemon Chicken is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown seared chicken thighs, cooked until tender, are nestled in a rich, pale yellow creamy lemon sauce. The sauce coats the chicken generously, appearing smooth with flecks of fresh green parsley and lemon zest. Alongside, several crispy smashed potatoes are arranged, showcasing their irregular, craggy edges and golden-brown, crispy exteriors contrasted with soft interiors. Thinly sliced, braised onions are scattered artfully around the chicken and potatoes. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space, resting on a simple wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin and standard restaurant flatware are placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, creating a warm, inviting, casual dining atmosphere. The dish appears vibrant, with the deep golden hues of the chicken and potatoes contrasting with the creamy sauce and bright green herbs. No meat slices are fanned; chicken is presented as whole pieces.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add new potatoes. Cook until fork-tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well.

Place cooked potatoes on a baking sheet. Gently smash each potato with the back of a fork or potato masher until flattened but still intact. Drizzle with 15ml olive oil, season with salt and pepper. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until golden and crispy.
While potatoes bake, pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs for 4-5 minutes per side until deeply golden brown. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the skillet. Add thinly sliced onion. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Deglaze skillet with fresh lemon juice. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Stir in chicken stock and heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook, stirring occasionally, until sauce slightly thickens, about 5-7 minutes.

Return seared chicken thighs to the skillet, nestling them into the sauce. Simmer gently for 5 minutes, ensuring chicken is cooked through to 75°C internal temperature. Remove from heat. Stir in lemon zest and chopped fresh parsley.
Serve chicken with creamy lemon sauce alongside crispy smashed potatoes.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Sour Cream Bundt Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single slice of golden-baked Lemon Sour Cream Bundt Cake is elegantly presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The slice stands upright, showcasing its tender, pale yellow crumb and the distinct fluted edge from the bundt pan. A generous, opaque white lemon glaze cascades down the sides of the slice, pooling slightly at its base on the plate. Beside the slice, a few small, translucent pieces of glistening candied lemon peel are artfully placed, adding a bright yellow accent and delicate texture. In the soft-focused background, the remainder of the whole bundt cake sits on a cake stand, hinting at its complete form. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, with a neatly folded cotton napkin placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the cake's appealing textures and vibrant colors. The presentation is clean, professional, and inviting, with moderate negative space emphasizing the dessert.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour a 6-cup bundt pan thoroughly.
In a medium bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. Set aside.
In a large bowl, cream softened butter and granulated sugar with an electric mixer until light and fluffy. This takes about 3-5 minutes.
Beat in eggs one at a time. Mix until fully incorporated after each addition.
In a separate small bowl, combine sour cream, milk, lemon zest, and vanilla extract.

Add dry ingredients to wet ingredients in three additions. Alternate with sour cream mixture in two additions. Begin and end with dry ingredients. Mix on low speed until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour batter evenly into the prepared bundt pan.
Bake for 35-45 minutes. Or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Let cake cool in the pan on a wire rack for 10 minutes. Invert cake onto the wire rack. Cool completely.
For the glaze: Whisk powdered sugar and fresh lemon juice in a small bowl until smooth. Adjust consistency with more sugar or juice if needed.

For candied lemon peel: Slice lemon into thin rounds. Cut rounds into small wedges or julienne strips. Boil lemon pieces in water for 5 minutes. Drain. Repeat this step once more to reduce bitterness.

Combine 50g sugar and 50ml water in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Add blanched lemon pieces. Simmer gently for 10-15 minutes until peel is translucent. Remove lemon pieces with a fork. Place on parchment paper to cool.
Drizzle cooled cake generously with lemon glaze. Arrange candied lemon peel on top of the glazed cake or around the base.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Sour Cream Entremet
recipes.visual_description: The Lemon Sour Cream Entremet embodies minimalist haute patisserie. Each perfectly cylindrical entremet gleams under an opaque white mirror glaze, reflecting light subtly. A single, precisely placed, vibrant yellow curl of candied lemon zest or a delicate micro-mint leaf provides a precise pop of color and texture atop. Centered on an elegant porcelain dessert plate with a subtle gold rim, abundant white space surrounds the entremet, emphasizing clean lines and architectural precision. The interior reveals distinct layers: light lemon sponge, vibrant lemon crémeux, and creamy sour cream mousse. The plate rests on pristine white marble, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting creating soft shadows, enhancing the dessert's sculptural quality. A finely folded white linen napkin and minimalist flatware complete the luxurious patisserie ambiance.
instructions: Preheat oven to 170°C. Line a baking sheet.

For Lemon Sponge: Whisk 1 egg and 50g sugar until pale and fluffy. Gently fold in 50g flour. Stir in 15ml milk and 1/2 lemon zest. Spread thinly on prepared baking sheet. Bake 8-10 minutes until golden. Cool. Cut into 4 small circles.

For Lemon Crémeux: Bloom 1g gelatin in cold water. Whisk 60ml lemon juice, 50g sugar, 2 egg yolks, and 1 whole egg in a saucepan. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thickened (82°C). Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed gelatin. Add 40g butter in small pieces; whisk until smooth. Pour into 4 small silicone molds (smaller than sponge circles). Freeze until solid.

For Sour Cream Mousse: Bloom 2g gelatin in cold water. Whisk 1 egg yolk, 50ml milk, and 30g sugar in a saucepan. Cook over medium heat, stirring, until thickened (82°C). Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed gelatin. Fold in 150g sour cream until smooth. Cool to 25°C. Whip 100ml heavy cream to soft peaks. Fold into sour cream mixture.

For Assembly: Prepare 4 individual entremet silicone molds. Pipe a layer of sour cream mousse into each mold. Place a frozen lemon crémeux insert into the mousse. Press gently. Top with more sour cream mousse. Place a lemon sponge circle on top, pressing lightly. Smooth the top. Freeze overnight until completely solid.

For Mirror Glaze: Bloom 7g gelatin in cold water. Combine 50ml water, 100g sugar, and 100g glucose syrup in a saucepan. Bring to a boil (103°C). Remove from heat. Stir in 70g condensed milk and bloomed gelatin. Add 100g white chocolate and white food coloring (if using). Blend with an immersion blender, avoiding air bubbles. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Cool to 35°C for glazing.

For Finishing: Unmold frozen entremets onto a wire rack over a tray. Pour glaze evenly over each frozen entremet. Let excess glaze drip off. Carefully transfer each entremet to a serving plate. Garnish with a tiny piece of fresh lemon zest or micro-herb. Allow to thaw in the refrigerator for at least 2-3 hours before serving.
notes: Ensure entremets are fully frozen for best glazing results.
Achieve precise glaze temperature for optimal flow and coverage.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Sour Cream Madeleines
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine perfectly uniform, shell-shaped Lemon Sour Cream Madeleines are elegantly arranged on a pristine white rectangular porcelain serving platter. Each madeleine features a distinct, golden-brown ridged exterior and a characteristic domed 'hump' on its smooth side, indicating proper baking. The delicate cakes are lightly dusted with fine powdered sugar, creating a soft, snowy appearance that contrasts with their warm, pale yellow interior visible on any exposed edges. A few thin, bright yellow lemon curls are scattered sparingly on the platter as a fresh garnish. The arrangement is clean and professional, with moderate negative space, showcasing the refined simplicity of these classic French petit fours. The platter rests on a light wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting, illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside coffee or tea.
Offer as part of a mignardise selection after a meal.
instructions: Melt butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Cook until golden brown and fragrant. Remove from heat. Let cool slightly.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt in a medium bowl. Set aside.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs and granulated sugar until light and fluffy. Add sour cream, milk, and lemon zest. Mix well.
Gently fold dry ingredients into wet mixture until just combined. Do not overmix.
Gradually fold in the cooled brown butter until incorporated. Cover batter and chill for at least 1 hour, or preferably overnight.
Preheat oven to 190°C. Lightly grease and flour a madeleine pan.
Spoon about 15 ml of batter into each madeleine cavity. Do not overfill.
Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until edges are golden brown and a prominent 'hump' forms.
Remove madeleines from pan immediately. Cool on a wire rack.
Dust generously with powdered sugar before serving.
notes: Chilling the batter is crucial for the characteristic madeleine 'hump'.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Sour Cream Cubes
recipes.visual_description: Nine perfectly uniform, miniature Lemon Sour Cream Cubes are meticulously arranged in a precise 3x3 grid on a pristine white bone china rectangular platter. The cubes showcase distinct, clean layers: a vibrant, pale yellow lemon crémeux base, topped with an off-white, silky sour cream panna cotta, and finished with a delicate, golden-brown Sable Breton crumble layer. Each cube is crowned with a single, translucent, precisely cut sliver of bright yellow candied lemon peel, positioned with architectural intent. The platter, occupying only a small portion of the frame, sits on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface. A crisp, white linen napkin, folded into a sharp triangle, rests subtly beside the platter. Dramatic professional lighting casts elegant shadows, highlighting the dessert's textures and colors. The background is ultra-minimalist, emphasizing abundant negative space, creating an image of extreme precision and sophisticated simplicity.

ingredients.name: Gelatin leaves (gold strength, for panna cotta)

instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.

For the Sable Breton Crumble: Combine flour, 30 g granulated sugar, and salt in a bowl. Cut in 40 g cold diced butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Mix in 1 egg yolk until just combined. Spread evenly onto the prepared baking tray. Bake for 15-20 minutes, until golden brown. Cool completely. Crumble into fine pieces.

For the Candied Lemon Peel: Peel zest from 1 lemon in long strips, avoiding the white pith. Blanch strips in boiling water for 30 seconds. Drain and refresh water. Repeat blanching two more times. Combine 50 g granulated sugar and 50 g water in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Add blanched lemon peel. Simmer gently for 15-20 minutes until peel is translucent. Drain the peel. Cool completely. Cut into very small, precise slivers.

For the Lemon Crémeux: Bloom 1 gelatin leaf in ice water. In a saucepan, whisk 100 g lemon juice, 80 g granulated sugar, 4 egg yolks, 1 whole egg, and lemon zest. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens to a nappe consistency (82-85°C). Remove from heat. Stir in the bloomed and squeezed gelatin until dissolved. Let cool slightly to 40°C. Gradually whisk in 100 g cold diced butter until emulsified and smooth. Pour the crémeux into a shallow rectangular mold (approx. 15x15 cm) lined with cling film. Chill for at least 2 hours until firm.

For the Sour Cream Panna Cotta: Bloom 2 gelatin leaves in ice water. Heat 150 g milk and 40 g granulated sugar in a saucepan until sugar dissolves. Remove from heat. Stir in the bloomed and squeezed gelatin until dissolved. Let cool to lukewarm. Whisk in 200 g full-fat sour cream until smooth.

Assemble Layers: Once the lemon crémeux is firm, carefully pour the slightly cooled sour cream panna cotta evenly over the crémeux layer in the mold. Gently sprinkle a thin, even layer of the Sable Breton crumble over the panna cotta. Chill the entire mold for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, until completely set.

To Plate: Remove the layered dessert from the mold using the cling film. Place on a clean cutting board. Using a very sharp knife, dipped in hot water and wiped clean between cuts, trim the edges for perfect squares. Cut the block into 9 identical, precise cubes (e.g., a 3x3 array). Carefully transfer each cube onto a sophisticated serving platter using an offset spatula.
Garnish: Place one tiny sliver of candied lemon peel precisely on top of each cube. Add a very minimal, light sprinkle of extra Sable Breton crumble around the base of the cubes for visual texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Tomato Consommé with Mozzarella Sphere and Lavash Tuile
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion is presented on a pristine, matte white bone china plate, allowing abundant negative space to highlight the dish. In the center, a perfectly spherical, small fresh mozzarella pearl rests gracefully within a pool of translucent, ruby-red smoked tomato consommé. The consommé, clear and shimmering, has a subtle amber hue from the smoking process. Next to the mozzarella, a single, elegantly irregular lavash tuile stands upright, its golden-brown surface crisp and delicate. A few drops of vibrant, emerald-green herb oil are artfully dotted onto the consommé, creating a subtle contrast. The arrangement is organic and flowing, emphasizing simplicity and precision. The setting is a luxurious dining table with a smooth, light grey veined Carrara marble surface. A crisp white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, rests to the side. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the textures and focusing entirely on the dish, with an ultra-minimalist background.
instructions: Prepare Smoked Tomato Consommé: Roughly chop tomatoes, shallot, and garlic. Place in a deep pot. Add white wine, a pinch of salt, and a few drops of liquid smoke.
Simmer gently for 20 minutes. Do not stir much.
Strain mixture through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing lightly to extract liquid. Do not force solids through. Discard solids.
Pass the strained liquid through a cheesecloth-lined sieve multiple times until perfectly clear. Chill the consommé completely.
Prepare Herb Oil: Blanch parsley and dill in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to shock. Squeeze out excess water.
Blend blanched herbs with olive oil until very smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve or coffee filter for a clear, vibrant green oil.
Prepare Lavash Tuiles: Preheat oven to 160°C. Cut lavash bread into irregular, organic shards, approximately 5-7 cm long.
Arrange lavash shards on a baking sheet. Bake for 5-7 minutes, or until golden and crisp. Watch carefully to prevent burning. Cool completely.
Assemble the dish: Place one perfect small mozzarella pearl in the center of a shallow, wide bowl.
Gently pour 80-100 ml of the chilled, clear smoked tomato consommé around the mozzarella sphere.
Carefully place one irregular lavash tuile upright next to the mozzarella sphere.
Drizzle a few drops of the vibrant green herb oil artfully onto the consommé. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Georgian Tomato & Lavash Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of vibrant Georgian Tomato & Lavash Soup is presented in a deep, matte cream-colored handcrafted ceramic bowl, showcasing its smooth, rich red-orange hue. The soup's surface is adorned with a mindful scattering of ingredients. Bright green, roughly chopped fresh parsley leaves provide a burst of color and natural texture. Interspersed are delicate, translucent rings of deep red pickled red onion, adding a tangy visual contrast. Irregular, golden-brown pieces of toasted lavash crisps, with their characteristic bubbly texture, are artfully placed on top. Small, soft white chunks of mozzarella are visibly melting into the hot soup, creating creamy pockets. The bowl rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is casually placed beside the bowl. Soft, natural lighting highlights the fresh ingredients against a clean, minimalist background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra lavash bread for dipping.
Offer a side of fresh herbs like cilantro or dill for individual garnish.
instructions: Prepare pickled onions: Slice one onion thinly into rings. Combine 250ml water, red wine vinegar, sugar, and 5g salt in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil. Pour hot brine over sliced onions in a heatproof bowl. Let cool to room temperature. Drain before serving.
Prepare soup base: Dice remaining onion. Chop garlic. Roughly chop tomatoes. Reserve any tomato cores/skins and onion ends for broth.
Make quick broth: Combine 1 liter water with reserved tomato cores/skins and onion ends in a pot. Bring to a simmer for 15 minutes. Strain and reserve broth.
Cook soup: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion and garlic. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add roughly chopped tomatoes and parsley stems. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Blend soup: Remove parsley stems. Blend soup mixture until smooth using an immersion blender or standard blender. Return to pot. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Keep warm.
Prepare lavash crisps: Tear lavash into irregular pieces. Toast in a dry pan over medium heat until golden and crispy. Alternatively, bake at 180°C (350°F) for 5-7 minutes.

Assemble and serve: Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Add small chunks of mozzarella; they will melt into the soup. Garnish generously with drained pickled onion rings, roughly chopped fresh parsley leaves, and lavash crisps. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by using vegetable scraps for broth and stale lavash for crisps.
The quick pickled onions provide a tangy, fermented element typical of Georgian cuisine.
traditional_techniques: Pickling and fermentation (as seen with the onions)

recipes.recipe_name: Lavash Flatbread with Fresh Tomato and Mozzarella
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lavash Flatbread is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centrally positioned on a simple wooden table. The lavash crust is golden-brown and crisped at the edges, maintaining a softer center. Melted fresh mozzarella creates a bubbly, slightly browned surface, interspersed with vibrant red diced ripe tomatoes. A generous scattering of bright green chopped fresh parsley provides striking color and freshness. A glossy drizzle of olive oil enhances the visual appeal. The flatbread is cut into four casual wedges, arranged organically on the plate. Beside the plate, a neatly folded cotton napkin rests. The setting is a modern bistro, with natural, even lighting, creating an inviting and approachable atmosphere. A small, simple ceramic bowl containing a side of mixed olives and a small dish of za'atar with olive oil are subtly placed, honoring Middle Eastern serving customs.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm, sliced into wedges.
Offer a small side dish of mixed olives or a simple herb salad.
Provide a small bowl of za'atar mixed with olive oil for dipping crusts.
Traditionally enjoyed as part of a larger mezze spread or as a light meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Dice ripe tomatoes into small cubes. Mince garlic cloves. Coarsely chop fresh parsley.
Place lavash sheets on baking trays. Brush each sheet evenly with olive oil.
Distribute diced tomatoes, minced garlic, and dried oregano evenly over each lavash sheet.
Tear fresh mozzarella into small pieces. Scatter mozzarella over the tomatoes.
Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Bake for 8-12 minutes. Bake until cheese is melted and bubbly. Edges of lavash should be golden and slightly crisp.
Remove from oven. Garnish generously with chopped fresh parsley.
Drizzle each flatbread with extra virgin olive oil before serving.
Slice each flatbread into four wedges. Serve immediately.
notes: Use fresh, good quality mozzarella for best melting and flavor.
Adjust baking time based on oven and desired crispness of lavash.

recipes.recipe_name: Orecchiette with Roasted Cherry Tomatoes and Mozzarella
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A generous individual portion of orecchiette pasta forms the base, centrally mounded. Interspersed throughout the pasta are vibrant, slightly shriveled roasted cherry tomatoes, some whole, some halved, showcasing their concentrated red hue. Thinly sliced, caramelized red onion and golden-brown roasted garlic cloves are visible amongst the pasta. Creamy, irregularly torn pieces of fresh white mozzarella are partially melted into the warm pasta, creating soft, inviting pockets. Fresh green basil leaves, some whole, some gently torn, are scattered generously over the top, providing a striking color contrast and aromatic lift. A light drizzle of golden-green extra virgin olive oil glistens over the dish. The overall composition is organic and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard European flatware, under soft, natural even lighting, evoking a modern bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of freshly grated Parmesan cheese.
Accompany with crusty Italian bread for soaking up the sauce.
Enjoy with a glass of light-bodied red wine, such as a Sangiovese.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Halve cherry tomatoes. Thinly slice red onion. Smash garlic cloves.
On a baking sheet, combine halved cherry tomatoes, sliced red onion, and smashed garlic. Drizzle with 30 ml olive oil. Season with salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes (if using).
Roast for 20-25 minutes, until tomatoes are soft and slightly caramelized, and onion is tender.
While vegetables roast, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add orecchiette pasta. Cook according to package instructions until al dente.
Drain pasta, reserving 120 ml of pasta cooking water.
Transfer cooked pasta to a large mixing bowl. Add roasted vegetables and their pan juices.
Add fresh mozzarella pieces and most of the fresh basil leaves (reserving some for garnish).
Add remaining 30 ml olive oil and 60 ml reserved pasta water. Toss gently to combine. If needed, add more pasta water, 30 ml at a time, until a light sauce forms and mozzarella begins to melt.
Serve immediately in individual portions. Garnish with remaining fresh basil and grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Rosemary and Oregano Stuffed Chicken with Roasted Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, plump and inviting, is centrally plated on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The breast is sliced into two thick medallions, revealing a creamy, molten filling of finely diced mushrooms and melted cheese, speckled with vibrant green oregano. Alongside, a vibrant cluster of roasted cherry tomatoes, some gently burst, are arranged artfully, their skins slightly blistered and caramelized. Fresh green rosemary sprigs are tucked among the tomatoes, adding aromatic contrast. A light, savory pan sauce, reduced to a glossy sheen, pools subtly around the chicken. Textures vary from the chicken's crisp, seared exterior to its tender interior and the soft, juicy tomatoes. Colors are warm golden-brown, creamy white, vibrant red, and deep green. The dish is set on a simple wooden surface, with a white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware, under natural, even lighting, highlighting a refined, approachable Italian main course.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty ciabatta bread to soak up the delicious pan juices
Pair with a simple mixed green salad with a light vinaigrette
instructions: Pound chicken breasts to an even 1.5 cm thickness. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Finely chop mushrooms and garlic. Sauté mushrooms and garlic in 10ml olive oil over medium heat until softened and moisture evaporates. Remove from heat.
Stir shredded mozzarella, grated Parmesan, and chopped oregano into the mushroom mixture. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Place a quarter of the filling onto one half of each chicken breast. Fold the other half over to enclose the filling. Secure edges with toothpicks if necessary.
Heat remaining 20ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear stuffed chicken breasts for 3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Add cherry tomatoes and two rosemary sprigs to the pan around the chicken. Toss tomatoes with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Transfer the pan to a preheated oven at 180°C. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with remaining fresh rosemary sprigs.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken and Potato Rosti with Gruyère
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown, circular potato rosti, approximately 10 cm in diameter, forms the base, showcasing a crisp, lacy edge and a finely textured surface from the shredded potato. A neat, generous mound of tender, light brown shredded chicken is piled centrally atop the rosti. Over the chicken, a blanket of melted Gruyère cheese glistens, with subtle bubbling and a rich, creamy texture. A sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh thyme leaves and chives provides a contrasting pop of color and freshness. The dish is presented centrally on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, allowing for ample negative space around the edges. The composition is balanced and inviting. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, with a neatly folded cotton napkin and standard European flatware positioned beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its varied textures and warm, appetizing colors against a subtly blurred, modern bistro background.
instructions: Poach chicken breasts: Place chicken in a pot. Cover with cold water. Add a pinch of salt. Bring to a simmer. Cook 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Cool slightly. Shred chicken using two forks. Set aside.
Prepare potatoes: Peel potatoes. Grate potatoes coarsely. Place grated potato in a clean kitchen towel. Squeeze out all excess moisture. This is crucial for crispy rosti.
Mix rosti ingredients: In a bowl, combine grated potato, grated onion, half of the chopped thyme, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Form rosti: Divide potato mixture into four equal portions. Form each portion into a compact, round disc, approximately 10 cm in diameter and 2 cm thick.

Cook rosti: Heat olive oil and butter in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Place rosti discs in the pan. Cook for 6-8 minutes per side, until deep golden brown and crispy. Ensure rosti is cooked through.

Assemble and melt cheese: Place cooked rosti on a baking sheet. Top each rosti with a generous mound of shredded chicken. Sprinkle grated Gruyère cheese over the chicken. Transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C for 3-5 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly. Alternatively, use a kitchen torch to melt the cheese.
Serve: Carefully transfer each rosti to a white dinner plate. Garnish with remaining fresh thyme and chopped chives. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Mushroom Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of hearty beef and mushroom stew sits on an everyday ceramic plate, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The stew is rich and thick, filling the plate with natural, comforting portions. Tender, browned beef chunks, approximately 4 cm, are nestled among roughly chopped orange carrot rounds and soft potato chunks, about 3 cm. Earthy sliced mushrooms and tender diced onions are visible throughout the dark, savory gravy. A light scattering of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley adds a fresh contrast. The components touch and slightly overlap, creating a homely, casual arrangement. The scene is lit with warm, cozy kitchen lighting, highlighting the stew's comforting textures and natural colors. Standard flatware and a casually placed cloth napkin are nearby, completing the relaxed family dining atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Beef chuck, cut into 4 cm chunks
Carrots, peeled and cut into 2 cm thick rounds
Potatoes, peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks

instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper. Toss with plain flour until lightly coated.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onion and carrots to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are browned and tender.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in red wine, if using, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until liquid is reduced by half.
Return beef to the pot. Add beef broth, fresh thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until beef is very tender.
Add potato chunks to the stew. Continue to simmer, uncovered, for another 20-30 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and the gravy has thickened to desired consistency.
Remove bay leaf and thyme sprigs. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Browning the beef well in batches is key for deep flavor.
The stew can be made ahead and reheated; flavors often improve the next day.

recipes.recipe_name: Coffee-Braised Beef Short Ribs with Creamy Polenta
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a single, generously portioned coffee-braised beef short rib, showcasing its natural, irregular shape, resting atop a creamy, golden-yellow bed of free-flowing polenta. The short rib is dark mahogany brown, with visible tender muscle fibers. A rich, glossy, dark brown braising sauce, thick but still flowing, is spooned over and around the short rib, creating a small pool on the polenta. Scattered around the plate are a few small, vibrant green sprigs of fresh parsley, providing a contrasting color and freshness. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space on a round white porcelain plate. The polenta is soft, not molded, allowing for a natural, slightly irregular spread. The beef is presented as a whole piece, not sliced.
instructions: Pat short ribs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear short ribs on all sides until deeply browned. Remove and set aside.
Add diced onions, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Deglaze the pot with red wine, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Pour in brewed coffee and beef stock. Add thyme sprigs and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared short ribs to the pot. Ensure liquid mostly covers the ribs. If not, add more stock or water.
Cover the pot. Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F).
Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until short ribs are fork-tender.
Remove short ribs from the pot. Strain the braising liquid into a saucepan, discarding solids. Skim off excess fat.
Reduce the braising liquid over medium-high heat until it thickens into a rich sauce. Season with salt and pepper.
For the polenta: Bring stock and milk to a simmer in a separate pot. Gradually whisk in cornmeal.
Reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring frequently, for 20-25 minutes until creamy and tender.
Stir in grated Parmesan cheese and butter until melted and smooth. Season with salt.
Serve short ribs over creamy polenta. Spoon sauce over the ribs.

recipes.recipe_name: Cream Cheese and Tatsoi Stuffed Chicken Breast
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of golden-brown, pan-seared chicken breast is centrally placed on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. The chicken, plump and whole, shows a crisp, savory crust from searing, and its interior, where a natural opening might be, hints at a creamy, pale green filling of wilted tatsoi and rich cream cheese. A light, glistening pan sauce, made from chicken broth and butter, pools subtly around the base. A few whole, fresh tatsoi leaves are casually arranged beside the chicken, providing a vibrant green contrast. The plate rests on a warm, well-worn wooden dining table, illuminated by soft, natural kitchen light. A casual, folded linen napkin and simple metal flatware complete the homely setting. The dish evokes comforting, expertly prepared home cooking.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Slice a deep pocket into each chicken breast, being careful not to cut all the way through.
Wash tatsoi thoroughly. Chop tatsoi roughly.

In a pan, melt 15g butter over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add chopped tatsoi and cook until wilted, about 2-3 minutes. Remove from heat.
In a bowl, combine wilted tatsoi mixture with cream cheese. Season with salt and pepper.
Carefully stuff each chicken breast pocket with the cream cheese and tatsoi filling. Secure opening with toothpicks if needed.
Season stuffed chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Lightly dredge in flour.
In a large oven-safe skillet, melt remaining 35g butter with olive oil over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 190°C (375°F). Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).

Remove chicken from skillet. Deglaze skillet with chicken broth, scraping up browned bits. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 2-3 minutes until slightly reduced. Season with salt and pepper. Stir in fresh thyme if using.
Serve immediately with pan sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Turkey, Broccoli & Cheddar Mac Bake
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of Homestyle Turkey, Broccoli & Cheddar Mac Bake is served on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. The dish presents a comforting mix of tender elbow macaroni, savory ground turkey, vibrant green broccoli florets, and soft diced tomatoes, all enveloped in a rich, creamy cheddar cheese sauce. A golden-brown, crispy breadcrumb topping covers the surface, offering a textural contrast. The components are naturally scooped onto the plate, showing organic shapes and slightly overlapping edges. Colors are warm and inviting: creamy yellow, earthy brown from the turkey, bright red from tomatoes, and deep green from broccoli. The scene is set on a well-used, light wooden kitchen table, with warm, natural overhead lighting. A casually folded cloth napkin sits beside the plate. The overall impression is one of hearty, homemade comfort food, ready for a family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve family-style directly from the baking dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Lightly grease a 2.5-litre baking dish.
Cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add ground turkey. Cook, breaking up chunks, until no pink remains. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion to the skillet with turkey. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in diced tomatoes, garlic powder, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Steam broccoli florets until tender-crisp. Set aside.
In a separate saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Stir in flour to form a roux. Cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in milk until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Remove from heat. Stir in 200 g of grated cheddar cheese until melted and smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, combine cooked macaroni, turkey mixture, steamed broccoli, and cheese sauce. Mix well to combine.
Transfer the mixture to the prepared baking dish. Sprinkle remaining 50 g of cheddar cheese and breadcrumbs evenly over the top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until bubbly and the topping is golden brown. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Stacked Eggplant Parmigiana
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant Stacked Eggplant Parmigiana stands centrally on a pristine white porcelain starter plate. The dish features three layers of tender, pan-fried eggplant rounds, each about 5mm thick, interlaid with vibrant, deep red San Marzano tomato sauce, melted creamy white fresh mozzarella slices, and generous sprinkles of golden-yellow grated Parmigiano Reggiano. Small, bright green fresh basil leaves are tucked between layers and scattered artfully on top. The top layer of Parmigiano is lightly golden and bubbly from baking. A drizzle of glistening extra virgin olive oil graces the stack. The plate is clean with moderate negative space, showcasing the dish. A folded white linen napkin and simple silver flatware are placed beside the plate on a rustic light wooden table. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the rich colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread (pane casereccio) to sop up the sauce.
Pair with a light, crisp Italian white wine, such as Vermentino or Pinot Grigio.
instructions: Slice eggplants into 5mm thick rounds. Lay slices on paper towels. Sprinkle generously with salt. Let sit 30 minutes to draw out moisture.
Press eggplants gently with more paper towels to remove excess water.

Heat 30ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Fry eggplant slices in batches until golden brown and tender, about 2-3 minutes per side. Add more oil as needed. Drain fried eggplant on paper towels.
For tomato sauce: Heat 20ml olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed San Marzano tomatoes. Add a pinch of salt and pepper. Simmer sauce 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened. Stir in half of the fresh basil, torn.
Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).

Assemble individual stacks: On a baking sheet, place one fried eggplant round. Top with a spoonful of tomato sauce. Add a slice of fresh mozzarella. Sprinkle with grated Parmigiano Reggiano and a few small basil leaves.
Repeat layers twice more: eggplant, sauce, mozzarella, Parmigiano, basil. Finish with a top layer of eggplant, sauce, and a generous sprinkle of Parmigiano.
Bake 15-20 minutes, or until mozzarella is melted and bubbly, and cheese is golden.
Let stacks rest 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Salting eggplant helps remove excess water and bitterness, leading to a better texture.
Use good quality San Marzano tomatoes for authentic flavor and richer sauce.
traditional_techniques: Salting eggplant to draw out moisture and bitterness.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato, Cucumber, and Diced Chicken Salad
recipes.visual_description: A homely, comforting salad presented on a simple, round ceramic plate. It rests on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm kitchen light. The salad features vibrant red diced tomatoes and refreshing green half-moon cucumber slices, forming a colorful base. Small, golden-brown diced chicken pieces are interspersed, adding a savory note without dominating. Crumbled white feta cheese and fresh green dill flecks are distributed over the ingredients, adding texture and color. A light, glossy vinaigrette subtly coats the components. The arrangement is casual and organic, with elements naturally overlapping, as if served from a family bowl. A plain cloth napkin rests nearby. The focus is on natural textures and inviting colors, highlighting the fresh ingredients in an unpretentious, comforting manner.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 1.5 cm cubes. In a bowl, toss chicken with 2 tablespoons soy sauce, garlic powder, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper.

Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until chicken is golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove from pan and let cool.
Dice tomatoes into 2 cm cubes. Slice cucumber into half-moons or dice into 1.5 cm cubes. Finely chop fresh dill. Finely dice or thinly slice red onion.
In a small bowl, whisk together 4 tablespoons olive oil, red wine vinegar, 1 tablespoon soy sauce, Dijon mustard, salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper until emulsified.
In a large serving bowl, combine diced tomatoes, cucumber, cooked and cooled chicken, and red onion.
Gently add crumbled feta cheese and chopped fresh dill to the salad.
Pour dressing over the salad. Toss gently to combine. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Beer and Mustard Chicken Puffs
recipes.visual_description: Golden-brown, puffed pastry triangles are arranged casually on an elegant white ceramic serving platter. Each puff, roughly 6-7 cm per side, showcases its flaky, airy texture. A hint of savory chicken filling, diced into small, tender cubes, peeks subtly from slightly parted seams. The warm, inviting golden hues of the pastry contrast with the flecks of vibrant green parsley sprinkled on top. The pieces are placed with natural spacing, creating an appetizing, inviting display for a gathering. The overall presentation is refined yet approachable, emphasizing the comfort and homemade quality of these bite-sized appetizers.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add finely diced onion. Cook until softened, about 3-4 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken breast, diced into 1 cm cubes, to the pan. Cook until browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Stir in Dijon mustard, beer, and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cook until liquid is mostly absorbed and chicken is tender, about 5-7 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Remove from heat. Stir in chopped fresh parsley. Let chicken filling cool slightly.
Unroll one thawed puff pastry sheet. Cut into 6 equal squares. Repeat with the second sheet for a total of 12 squares.
Place a spoonful of chicken filling onto the center of each pastry square.
Fold each square diagonally to form a triangle. Press edges firmly to seal. Crimp edges with a fork.
Transfer puffs to the prepared baking tray. Brush tops with beaten egg wash.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until puff pastry is golden brown and puffed.
Let cool slightly on a wire rack. Garnish with extra fresh parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Honeyed Greek Yogurt Panna Cotta with Brown Butter Crumble and Berry Compote
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dessert plate. A single, individual serving of the Honeyed Greek Yogurt Panna Cotta is unmolded, standing elegantly. The panna cotta has a smooth, creamy texture and a soft, off-white color. It is topped with a vibrant, jewel-toned mixed berry compote, showcasing whole and slightly softened berries. Around the base and lightly scattered on top are golden-brown, irregular crumbles of brown butter. A small, smooth dollop of pale, creamy cottage cheese cream is placed neatly beside the panna cotta. The overall presentation is clean and professional, with balanced elements and moderate negative space. The colors are natural and appealing. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface and a white cotton napkin folded beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dessert.
instructions: Bloom gelatin sheets in cold water for 5-10 minutes. Squeeze excess water.
Heat heavy cream, 80g honey, and a pinch of salt in a saucepan over medium-low heat until warm. Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Add bloomed gelatin. Whisk until gelatin dissolves completely.
Whisk in Greek yogurt until the mixture is smooth. Pour into 4 serving glasses or molds.
Chill for at least 4 hours, or until completely set.
Melt 50g unsalted butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Cook until butter browns and smells nutty. Strain if desired.
Combine browned butter with all-purpose flour, granulated sugar, and a pinch of salt in a bowl. Mix until crumbly.
Spread crumble mixture on a baking sheet. Bake at 160°C for 12-15 minutes, until golden brown. Cool completely.
Combine mixed berries, 30g honey, and lemon juice in a small saucepan. Simmer over medium-low heat for 5-7 minutes until berries soften and sauce thickens slightly. Cool.
Blend cottage cheese, 15ml milk, and 10g honey until completely smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for extra smoothness if desired. Chill.
To assemble, unmold panna cotta onto plates if using molds. Spoon berry compote over or alongside panna cotta.
Sprinkle brown butter crumble generously around the panna cotta and compote.
Add a small, smooth dollop or drizzle of cottage cheese cream beside the panna cotta.

recipes.recipe_name: Caramelized Onion Braised Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Caramelized Onion Braised Chicken is presented centrally on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown, seared and then braised boneless chicken thighs, each a distinct piece, are nestled together. The rich, deep amber-brown sauce, infused with slow-caramelized onions, generously coats the chicken and pools elegantly around it. The sauce has a smooth, velvety texture with soft, tender remnants of the onions. A sprinkle of vibrant fresh chopped parsley provides a contrasting green pop against the dark sauce and golden chicken. The arrangement is professional yet approachable, with ample negative space. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A silver fork and knife are placed neatly beside the plate, with a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, and a subtly blurred restaurant background completes the scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices to soak up the rich sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with a vinaigrette.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on both sides. This takes 3-4 minutes per side. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.

Reduce heat to medium-low. Add butter to the pot. Add thinly sliced onions. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 30-40 minutes until deeply caramelized and soft. They should be a rich amber-brown color.
Add minced garlic to the onions. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Sprinkle flour over the caramelized onions. Stir constantly for 1 minute.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine reduces by half, about 3-5 minutes.
Stir in chicken broth, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in the liquid. Cover the pot.
Transfer pot to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Braise for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove from oven. Discard thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Let chicken rest in the sauce for 5 minutes.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Caramelizing the onions slowly and deeply is crucial for developing the rich, complex flavor of the sauce. Do not rush this step.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Marsala
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast is centrally placed on a round white porcelain plate. The chicken, a golden-brown whole piece, is partially covered with a rich, glossy Marsala mushroom sauce. Thinly sliced, tender cremini mushrooms and finely diced shallots are visible within the deep brown sauce. A generous sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley garnishes the chicken and sauce, adding a pop of color. The dish exhibits a clean, organized, yet organic plating style with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate. Standard polished flatware (fork and knife) are arranged next to the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere with a softly blurred restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside creamy polenta or a simple pasta like fettuccine or linguine.
Offer a side of steamed green beans or asparagus.
Crusty Italian bread is ideal for soaking up the Marsala sauce.
instructions: Place each chicken breast between two sheets of plastic wrap. Pound to an even 1.5 cm thickness. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Dredge each chicken breast lightly in flour, shaking off excess.
Slice mushrooms thinly. Finely dice shallots. Mince garlic.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the skillet. Add sliced mushrooms and diced shallots. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and browned. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour Marsala wine into the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce liquid by half, about 3-5 minutes.
Stir in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes until sauce slightly thickens. Stir in heavy cream, if using.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet. Simmer in the sauce for 2-3 minutes, ensuring chicken is fully heated through. Chop fresh parsley.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in half of the chopped parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh parsley.
notes: Pounding the chicken ensures even cooking and tenderness.
Ensure Marsala wine is dry, not sweet, for a savory dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Italian Sausage and Olive Crostini
recipes.visual_description: Rustic slices of toasted baguette are piled high with a hearty mixture. Crumbled, golden-brown Italian sausage forms the base, interspersed with finely chopped dark black olives and vibrant green olives. Bright green, roughly chopped basil leaves are generously sprinkled over the top, adding a fresh contrast. Each crostini is slightly irregular in shape. A light sheen of olive oil glistens on the sausage and bread. The crostini are arranged casually on a simple, round ceramic plate with a slight rim. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple linen napkin is casually folded beside it. Warm, natural light from a kitchen window illuminates the scene. The overall impression is one of inviting, rustic comfort food, perfect for a family gathering.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as part of an antipasto spread.
Accompany with a simple glass of red wine.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Remove sausage from casings. Crumble into a large pan.
Cook sausage over medium heat until browned and cooked through. Break up any large pieces. Drain excess fat.
Slice baguette diagonally into 1.5 cm thick pieces. Arrange on a baking sheet.
Toast baguette slices in the oven for 5-7 minutes, until light golden and crisp.
While bread toasts, finely chop black and green olives.
Roughly chop fresh basil leaves.
Peel garlic cloves. Cut one in half.
Remove toasted bread from oven. Immediately rub one side of each slice with the cut garlic clove.
Drizzle toasted bread with a little olive oil.
In a bowl, combine cooked sausage, chopped olives, and most of the chopped basil. Add a splash of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper.
Spoon generous portions of the sausage and olive mixture onto each garlic-rubbed crostini.
Arrange crostini on a serving platter. Garnish with remaining fresh basil. Serve immediately.
notes: Use fresh, good quality basil for best flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Greek Lemon Chicken Noodle Soup with Spinach
recipes.visual_description: A comforting bowl of Greek Lemon Chicken Noodle Soup with vibrant green spinach. The clear, golden chicken broth is rich with dried oregano and bright lemon. Tender, shredded chicken pieces are nestled among al dente small pasta noodles. Wilted fresh spinach adds a pop of color and earthy flavor. The soup is served in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl with a slightly chipped rim, placed on a well-worn wooden dining table. A simple metal spoon rests beside the bowl. A quartered lemon wedge and a sprig of fresh oregano are casually placed on a small side plate. Warm, inviting light from an overhead kitchen fixture casts soft shadows. The scene evokes a cozy, lived-in family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
Offer extra lemon wedges on the side for individual preference.
instructions: Dice onion finely. Mince garlic. Roughly chop spinach.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken breast to the pot. Brown lightly on all sides.
Pour in chicken broth. Add dried oregano. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from the pot. Shred chicken using two forks or cut into small cubes. Set aside.
Increase heat to medium-high. Add pasta noodles to the simmering broth. Cook according to package directions until al dente.
Return shredded chicken to the pot.
Stir in roughly chopped spinach. Cook until wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
Squeeze juice from the lemon into the soup. Stir well.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Greek Lemon Spinach Orzo Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of vibrant Greek Lemon Spinach Orzo Soup is presented in an off-white, rustic ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The soup features tender, pale yellow orzo pasta and bright green, wilted spinach leaves suspended in a clear, savory broth. A thin slice of fresh lemon floats on the surface, alongside a small sprig of fresh dill. The ingredients are naturally arranged, showcasing the wholesome, comforting nature of the dish. The bowl is accompanied by a simple metal spoon and a casually draped linen napkin. Warm, natural kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, evoking a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. The focus remains on the nourishing soup, with minimal background distractions, emphasizing its homely appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in vegetable broth. Bring to a boil.
Add orzo pasta. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer for 8-10 minutes, or until orzo is al dente. Stir occasionally.
Stir in fresh spinach until wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
Remove soup from heat. Stir in fresh lemon juice.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh dill or parsley if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Mushroom Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and whole, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. It is generously coated with a rich, creamy mushroom sauce. The sauce features irregularly sliced, deeply browned cremini mushrooms and finely diced shallots, creating a rustic yet refined texture. Bright green chopped parsley is sprinkled over the chicken and sauce, adding a fresh color contrast. The chicken breast shows a crisp exterior and a tender interior. A small pool of sauce surrounds the base of the chicken. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table, with a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and texture. A single portion, balanced and appealing.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the pan.
Add sliced shallot. Sauté 2 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add irregularly sliced mushrooms. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened and browned.
Sprinkle flour over mushrooms. Stir for 1 minute to coat.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the pan.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer for 3-5 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Return chicken breasts to the pan. Turn to coat with sauce.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken and Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single, hearty portion of roasted chicken (one whole drumstick or thigh) is centered on a round, rustic ceramic plate.
