The pasta, penne or rigatoni, is generously coated in a vibrant, rustic tomato sauce. Seared chicken chunks, approximately 3 cm, are interspersed throughout, showcasing their golden-brown crust. Bright red and yellow bell pepper squares (2 cm) and golden corn kernels add bursts of color and texture. Fresh green parsley, roughly chopped, is scattered over the top, along with a delicate dusting of grated Parmesan cheese. The dish appears moist and inviting, with a balanced arrangement of ingredients. Natural, soft light illuminates the scene, creating a warm, approachable bistro ambiance. A folded white cotton napkin sits beside the bowl.
instructions: Cut chicken breasts into 3 cm chunks. Season with salt and black pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown and cooked through to 75°C internal temperature. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Dice onion. Mince garlic. Cut bell peppers into 2 cm squares.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the same pan. Add diced onion and bell peppers. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and fresh thyme sprigs. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in diced tomatoes and vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 10 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
While sauce simmers, cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 120 ml of pasta water.
Add cooked chicken chunks and corn kernels to the simmering sauce. Stir to combine. Cook for 2-3 minutes to heat through.
Add drained pasta to the pan with the sauce. Toss to coat. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, 30 ml at a time, until desired consistency.
Grate Parmesan cheese. Roughly chop fresh parsley.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with grated Parmesan and fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken with Caramelized Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single braised chicken thigh with crisp, golden-brown skin rests atop a generous bed of deeply caramelized, amber-hued onion slices. The chicken is tender, showing its natural form, not sliced. A rich, savory pan sauce, slightly thickened, coats the chicken and onions, reflecting light. Freshly chopped green parsley is sprinkled over the dish, adding a vibrant contrast. The plate is a rustic, off-white ceramic, placed on a warm, well-used wooden kitchen table. A simple fork and knife are set beside it. The background is a soft-focus, lived-in kitchen atmosphere with warm lighting. The overall impression is comforting and hearty.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with creamy mashed potatoes to soak up the sauce
Accompany with crusty bread for dipping
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken, skin-side down, for 5-7 minutes until deeply golden and crisp. Flip. Sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.

Reduce heat to medium-low. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil and butter to the pot. Add thinly sliced onions. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 20-25 minutes until onions are deeply caramelized and very soft.
Add minced garlic, bay leaf, and fresh thyme leaves. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in dry white wine (if using). Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Reduce liquid by half.
Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up. Ensure liquid comes halfway up the chicken.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and is very tender.
Remove lid. Discard bay leaf. If sauce is too thin, increase heat to medium. Simmer uncovered for 5-10 minutes to thicken slightly.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: This dish can be prepared a day in advance and reheated gently for enhanced flavors.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Heirloom Tomato Carpaccio with Crispy Chorizo and Parmesan Snow
recipes.visual_description: A large, pristine white bone china plate presents a sophisticated, minimalist composition. Paper-thin slices of vibrant heirloom tomatoes, showcasing a spectrum of reds, oranges, and greens, are arranged in an organic, flowing swirl across one side of the plate. A precise drizzle of glistening garlic-infused extra virgin olive oil coats the tomato surfaces. Small, golden-brown crumbles of crispy chorizo are scattered artfully over the tomatoes, adding textural contrast. A delicate, ethereal dusting of white Parmesan 'snow' is meticulously applied over the chorizo and parts of the tomatoes. A few tiny, vivid green basil leaves and finely snipped chives are strategically placed for color and freshness. The presentation emphasizes abundant negative space, highlighting the architectural precision of each element. The plate rests on a polished dark grey marble surface, accompanied by a perfectly folded white linen napkin. Dramatic, professional lighting casts subtle shadows, enhancing the textures and forms, with an ultra-minimalist, dark, blurred background.
instructions: Place Parmesan cheese in freezer for at least 30 minutes.
Thinly slice heirloom tomatoes into carpaccio rounds. Arrange slices on a large platter or individual plates, slightly overlapping.
If using liquid smoke, lightly brush or mist tomato slices with 2-3 drops diluted in a tablespoon of water for a subtle smoky aroma. Alternatively, cold smoke tomatoes for 10-15 minutes.

Heat a small pan over medium heat. Add finely diced chorizo. Cook until chorizo is very crispy and its fat is rendered. Remove chorizo crumbles with a slotted spoon. Drain excess fat. Set crispy chorizo aside.

In a small saucepan, combine olive oil and minced garlic. Gently heat over low heat for 5 minutes. Do not brown garlic. Remove from heat. Let cool slightly to infuse. Strain garlic if desired for a clear oil.
Drizzle garlic-infused olive oil over the tomato carpaccio.
Sprinkle crispy chorizo crumbles over the tomatoes.
Retrieve frozen Parmesan. Using a microplane or fine grater, grate Parmesan directly over the dish to create a fine 'snow' effect.
Season lightly with sea salt and freshly ground black pepper.
Garnish with small basil leaves and finely snipped chives.
If using, drizzle aged balsamic vinegar sparingly around the plate.

recipes.recipe_name: Shorbet Banadoura ma' Riz (Sustainable Tomato Rice Soup)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lebanese Tomato Rice Soup is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl with a warm, natural beige tone, resting on a light reclaimed wood table. The soup, a rich, earthy red-orange color, is fluid and comforting, with tender white short-grain rice grains visible throughout. Floating on top are small, perfectly diced pieces of fresh tomato and vibrant green flecks of finely chopped parsley. A subtle drizzle of golden-brown maple-caramelized onion oil glistens on the surface, with a few soft, sticky strands of caramelized onion resting atop the soup. The plating is minimalistic, allowing the natural textures and colors of the ingredients to shine. To the side, an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige hue is casually folded. A small ceramic dish holds a fresh, bright yellow lemon wedge, ready to be squeezed. The background is clean and uncluttered, with soft, natural light illuminating the scene, highlighting the pure beauty of this sustainable, authentic dish. The entire plate is visible, showcasing mindful negative space around the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with fresh lemon wedges on the side for squeezing.
Accompany with fresh or toasted pita bread for dipping.
Offer a small bowl of mixed fresh herbs (mint, parsley) on the side for an extra fresh garnish.

ingredients.name: Zero-Waste Vegetable Broth
ingredients.quantity: 1 litre (made from onion skins, garlic skins, tomato trimmings, herb stems)

ingredients.name: Fermented Tomato Paste (or high-quality concentrated tomato paste)

instructions: Prepare Zero-Waste Vegetable Broth: Combine onion skins, garlic skins, tomato trimmings, and any herb stems with 1.5 litres water in a pot. Simmer for 30 minutes. Strain, discard solids. You need 1 litre of broth.
Dice 1 medium onion. Mince garlic cloves.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced fresh tomatoes and fermented tomato paste to the pot. Stir well. Cook for 5 minutes, breaking down tomatoes with a spoon.
Rinse rice thoroughly under cold water until water runs clear. Add rinsed rice to the pot. Stir to combine.
Pour in the 1 litre of prepared Zero-Waste Vegetable Broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Simmer, covered, for 15-20 minutes, or until rice is tender.

While soup simmers, prepare maple-caramelized onion garnish: Thinly slice the remaining 1 medium onion. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a small pan over medium-low heat. Add sliced onion. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized and soft, about 15-20 minutes.
Stir in maple syrup to the caramelized onions. Cook for 1 minute more until sticky. Remove from heat.
Stir dried mint and ground allspice into the soup. Add fresh lemon juice. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle soup into individual serving bowls. Garnish each bowl with a spoonful of maple-caramelized onions and freshly chopped parsley.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing vegetable trimmings for a flavorful broth.
The use of fermented tomato paste adds a layer of complex umami, honoring preservation techniques.
traditional_techniques: Balancing sweet, sour, and savory flavors common in Lebanese cuisine.
Utilizing fresh herbs and lemon as key finishing elements.

recipes.recipe_name: Maize & Umami Entremet
recipes.visual_description: A single, exquisitely plated portion of the Maize & Umami Entremet rests off-center on a pristine white porcelain plate with a subtle gold rim. The entremet is a perfectly sculpted 8x8 cm square, showcasing its architectural layers through a clean, sharp cut. The top layer is a smooth, almost translucent white chocolate glaze, beneath which the pale yellow of the sweet corn sponge cake is visible, followed by the creamy, off-white caramelized onion and white bean mousse, and a second layer of corn sponge. Adjacent to the entremet, a small, vibrant orange dollop of the confit tomato gel provides a striking color contrast. Scattered artfully around the base of the entremet are delicate, irregular shards of the golden-brown mustard seed praline, offering textural intrigue. A few precise, micro-drops of the glossy, deep amber umami glaze are strategically placed on the plate, adding a subtle visual accent and promising a surprising flavor note. The plate features abundant negative space, emphasizing the minimalist composition. A single tiny microgreen or edible flower is placed with tweezers on the entremet for a final, refined flourish. The scene is illuminated by dramatic professional lighting, casting soft shadows and highlighting the dish's precise details against a stark, ultra-minimalist background, with a crisply folded white linen napkin in a precise triangle beside the plate.
instructions: Sweet Corn Sponge Cake:
Preheat oven to 170°C. Line a 20x20 cm square baking tin with parchment paper.
Melt 100 g butter. Set aside to cool.
Whisk 100 g caster sugar and eggs until pale and thick.
Fold in melted butter.
Sift corn flour, all-purpose flour, and baking powder. Gently fold into egg mixture.
Combine 60 ml milk and puréed corn kernels. Fold into batter until just combined.
Pour batter into prepared tin. Bake 15-18 minutes, or until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in tin for 10 minutes, then invert onto a wire rack. Cool completely.
Trim edges. Cut into two 8x8 cm squares for assembly.
Caramelized Onion & White Bean Mousse:
Melt 15 g butter in a pan over medium-low heat. Add thinly sliced onions. Cook slowly for 30-40 minutes, stirring often, until deeply caramelized and jam-like. Do not brown.
Soak gelatin in cold water.
In a blender, combine caramelized onions, drained cannellini beans, and 50 ml milk. Blend until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve.
Melt white chocolate over a double boiler or in microwave.
Heat a small portion of the onion-bean purée. Squeeze excess water from gelatin; stir into warm purée until dissolved.
Whisk melted chocolate into purée until smooth.
Whip cold heavy cream to soft peaks. Gently fold into the cooled onion-bean mixture in two additions.
Refrigerate mousse for 30 minutes to firm slightly.
Confit Tomato Gel:
Preheat oven to 140°C.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Arrange on a baking sheet. Sprinkle with 10 g caster sugar and thyme sprig.
Bake 45-60 minutes until slightly shriveled and intensely flavorful. Remove thyme.
Blend confit tomatoes until smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve.
Whisk 2 g agar-agar into the strained tomato liquid. Bring to a boil over medium heat, whisking constantly for 1 minute.
Pour into a shallow dish. Chill until set.
Once set, cut into small cubes or re-blend until smooth for a fluid gel.
Mustard Seed Praline:
Toast mustard seeds in a dry pan until fragrant, about 2-3 minutes.
In a separate saucepan, combine 50 g caster sugar and 15 ml water. Cook over medium-high heat without stirring until it reaches a deep amber caramel.
Remove from heat. Stir in toasted mustard seeds and pinch of sea salt.
Pour onto a silicone mat or parchment paper. Let cool completely.
Break into small shards or crush into a coarse crumble.
Umami Glaze (Clarified Chicken Consommé Reduction):
Pour clarified chicken consommé into a wide saucepan.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce slowly over low heat until it becomes a very concentrated, slightly viscous liquid (approx. 50-70 ml). This can take 1-2 hours. Skim any impurities.
If desired for slight thickening, whisk 1 g agar-agar into the warm reduction, bring to a boil for 30 seconds. Cool slightly.
Assembly:
Line individual entremet molds (e.g., 8x8 cm square) with acetate strips if using.
Place one square of corn sponge cake at the base of each mold.
Pipe or spoon a layer of the chilled caramelized onion & white bean mousse over the sponge, filling about two-thirds of the mold. Smooth the top.
Place another square of corn sponge cake on top of the mousse. Press gently.
Pipe or spoon another thin layer of mousse to cover the second sponge, smoothing the top.
Chill molds in the freezer for at least 4 hours, or until completely frozen.
Once frozen, unmold the entremets. Remove acetate.
Allow entremets to thaw slowly in the refrigerator for 2-3 hours before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chorizo and White Bean Stew
recipes.visual_description: A hearty single portion of Spanish Chorizo and White Bean Stew is presented in a deep, pristine white ceramic bowl, centered on a light wooden table. The stew boasts vibrant colors: rich, smoky red from the diced chorizo and crushed tomatoes, contrasting with creamy white cannellini beans and softened translucent diced onions. Thick rounds of pan-seared chorizo are interspersed throughout, showcasing their browned edges and robust texture. The stew is thick but fluid, clinging to the ingredients, with a visible sheen of olive oil. A generous sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped flat-leaf parsley garnishes the top, adding a fresh aromatic lift. Beside the bowl, a thick, rustic slice of crusty bread with an open crumb is positioned. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere typical of a modern bistro setting. A simple cotton napkin and traditional silver flatware are neatly arranged beside the bowl, complementing the clean presentation without overcrowding the frame.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping into the rich sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.

ingredients.name: Canned cannellini beans, rinsed and drained

instructions: Remove chorizo from casings. Cut into 2 cm thick rounds or rough chunks.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chorizo. Cook until browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Remove chorizo with a slotted spoon. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened and translucent, about 8-10 minutes. Stir occasionally.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Stir constantly.
Pour in diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Add rinsed cannellini beans and cooked chorizo back to the pot. Stir well.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken slightly. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Adjust seasoning as needed.
Ladle stew into individual serving bowls. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef with Ginger-Mustard Mushroom Sauce
recipes.visual_description: Seared beef, cut into thick, irregular chunks, showcases a pink medium-rare interior and a dark, caramelized crust. The beef is arranged off-center on a round, clean white porcelain plate. A rich, glossy, amber-brown sauce with sautéed sliced cremini mushrooms is generously spooned beside and partially over the beef chunks. A scattering of vibrant green, thinly sliced spring onions provides a fresh contrast. The plate is placed on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A small, white rice bowl filled with fluffy steamed jasmine rice is positioned nearby. A pair of elegant wooden chopsticks rests on a small chopstick rest next to the plate. A folded white cotton napkin is placed to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors. The background is clean and slightly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Steamed jasmine rice
instructions: Pat beef dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Combine 30 ml soy sauce, grated ginger, and half minced garlic. Marinate beef for 15-20 minutes.
Heat vegetable oil in a skillet over high heat. Sear beef 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare. Adjust time for desired doneness.
Remove beef from skillet. Let rest for 5 minutes.
In the same skillet, add remaining garlic and chili flakes. Sauté for 30 seconds.
Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Whisk together remaining 30 ml soy sauce, Dijon mustard, and beef broth. Pour into skillet. Bring to a simmer.
Mix cornstarch with water to create a slurry. Stir slurry into simmering sauce. Cook until sauce thickens.
Slice beef into thick chunks. Arrange beef on plates.
Spoon sauce and mushrooms generously over beef.
Garnish with thinly sliced spring onion. Serve immediately.
notes: This dish offers a balanced profile of protein, healthy fats, and carbohydrates when served with rice.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Chicken Breast, Crispy Rice, Garlic-Umami Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single seared chicken breast medallion, precisely cut into two or three thick, clean pieces, is artfully arranged slightly offset on a pristine, stark white bone china plate. Adjacent to the chicken, a perfectly round, golden-brown crispy rice disk provides contrasting texture. A delicate, glossy dark amber garlic-umami glaze sweeps across the plate, connecting the elements with a fluid, organic line. A few vibrant green shiso sprouts are meticulously placed atop the chicken, with a barely visible whisper of red cayenne dust. Accompanied by a small cup of hot green tea.
instructions: Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Place each breast in a vacuum-sealable bag with one thyme sprig. Sous vide at 63°C for 1.5 hours. Chill immediately.

Rinse rice until water runs clear. Cook rice with 150 ml water. Once cooked, spread thinly on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Press firmly to create a thin, even layer. Cut into 6 cm round disks. Dehydrate or air dry for 2 hours.
For the glaze, combine soy sauce, mirin, sake, dashi, and 2 crushed garlic cloves in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Reduce by half until syrupy. Strain to remove garlic. Keep warm.
Heat neutral oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add remaining garlic clove, thinly sliced, and thyme sprig. Infuse oil for 2 minutes. Remove garlic and thyme.

Remove chilled chicken from bags. Pat dry. Slice each breast into two or three thick medallions. Sear chicken medallions in the infused oil over medium-high heat until golden brown, about 2 minutes per side. Cook to an internal temperature of 75°C. Add butter during final minute.
Heat clean neutral oil in a separate pan to 180°C. Fry crispy rice disks until golden and puffed, about 30 seconds per side. Drain on paper towels.

To plate, arrange chicken medallions on one side of a clean plate. Position a crispy rice disk nearby. Drizzle glaze artfully across the plate, connecting elements. Garnish with shiso sprouts and a whisper of cayenne pepper.
notes: Chilling the chicken after sous vide ensures a clean cut and prevents overcooking during searing.
traditional_techniques: Umami layering (via dashi and glaze reduction)
